Crossposted from a [ similar thread about superpowers ] ( URL_0 ) . I think the real question here is not why these powers are impossible , but why do they seem intuitively possible ? I mean , the idea makes immediate sense to virtually everyone , so why are scientists so convinced that there 's no such thing as superpowers ? Your brain thinks . That 's what it does . It deals with thoughts . Thoughts loom large in your brain . Thoughts are fundamental to how your brain works . Thoughts are not fundamental to how the universe works . The universe has one fundamental level , that of elementary particles . These are things like quarks and electrons . Everything above that level is fully explainable in terms of that level . If you model the exact behavior of all the elemental particles in a region of space , you have modeled that space exactly , full stop . But , your brain does n't think about the level of quarks and electrons . It thinks at the level of bricks and thoughts , and its way more efficient to store a mental model of the universe at the level of those things . So , thoughts feel like a fundamental thingummy to your brain .

Some while back , someone decided to organize living things in order to understand them better . The categories included : things that are useful to man ; things that are harmful to man ; and things that are neither useful nor harmful . It was a practical system , but if you look at current taxonomies ( organizational schemes ) , they are based on different criteria . So , what is the purpose [ to us ] of pumpkins ? Arguably , if we keep religion out of the discussion , what is the purpose of anything ? Pumpkins exist because they can . They have no more choice than other forms of life : they come into being because their ancestors were successful enough to make their appearance ( " birth " , so to speak ) possible . The " purpose " of living things is to reproduce ; individuals may be indifferent to whether or not they do so successfully , but a species usually has enough individuals " to whom it matters " ( so to speak ) to keep them going . It is not a matter of " wanting " to live , or of being " needed " to live ; capability to live keeps things around .

Here in the UK , the phrase is “ red sky in the morning , shepherd ’s warning ; red sky at night , shepherd ’s delight ” and DOES have a basis in reality . The prevailing wind direction in the UK is from the south - west , meaning that weather will generally move from west to east across the country . In the morning , the sun is in the east , so if it is being reflected / light scattered by clouds they are to the west of it : this means that cloud , and possible rain , is likely coming towards you . In the evening , the sun is in the west , so if the sky is red the weather is going away from you so rain is less likely . So , as long as the wind is coming from its “ normal ” direction , the phrase is a useful rule of thumb . If the wind is coming from the N , S , or E then it ’s not much use .

You start of with crude oil - C^n H^(n+2 ) roughly speaking . There might be some variants in there , but the general gist is that it 's long chains of carbohydrates . The longer the chain , the lower the melting point and the more viscous the fluid . Up to C3H8 and some forms of C4H10 it 's still gas at room temperature , above that and it 's a fluid . The first thing they do is to break down the long carbohydrates into short ones . They then try to get a single type of short ones - for example , C2H4 ( ethene / ethylene ) , C3H6 , ... The thing you should notice is that they have a double bond in there somewhere . The next step is polymerisation - add a catalyst ( H+ ) and it will connect to one ( forming C2H5 + ) and then to another ( forming C4H9 + ) and so on . This creates very long chains that are ( see above ) solid . This is what you call plastic . In this process , the end result is determined by what the original stuff was ( so ethene is going to become polyethene ( PE ) and urethane is going to become polyurethane ( PU ) etc .

Two laws of electronics : V = IR and P = RI^2 . That is , voltage = current * resistance , and power = resistance * current squared . If you connect 5V to 0 directly on the microcontroller , V = 5 . Assuming you 're connecting them with a typical wire , a quick google suggests that the resistance of that wire is ~ 0.001 . Which makes current 5 / 0.001 = 500A. Which is a lot . Plug it into the other format . R = 0.001 . I^2 = 250,000 . Multiply those and you get 250W. Which is a lot of W. Especially since most microcontrollers are rated to deal with < 1W of power . All of that power will be radiated away as heat . For reference , 4000W could raise a pitcher ( 1 litre ) of water by 1 degree C every second . So , your wire there could boil a pitcher of water in 20 minutes . Which is not as impressive as a kettle , but given that this is just a shitty little wire , should give you pause . tl;dr : IT MAKES A LOT OF HEAT AND BURNS SHIT

In Europe in the 18th century , every little state had their own little measurement systems . What would become the metric system was under development since the 1500s . Some European states saw the logic in adopting a continent - wide standard of measurements , but others did n't . Thomas Jefferson argued in favor of a base-10 system of measurement , but Congress did n't adopt it . France formally adopted a system very similar to the metric system in 1799 . Napoleon then proceeded to conquer most of Europe , bequeathing the French system to those territories . Post - war , most states maintained the system . In the mid 1800s , Britain saw the need for a standardized system and organized an international conference to firmly establish and already - mostly - established metric system . Most of Europe signed the resulting treaty , and then gave the standard to all of their colonies ( pretty much the whole world , minus the US ) . Congress even authorized the use of the metric system in 1866 . But for whatever reason , " customary " units kept their dominance outside of professional applications . This is somewhat true in the UK as well .

Basically when you have a lot of interconnected variables which would make a problem hard or practically impossible to solve purely mathematically , you instead build a model that assigns odds of all the various events occurring , then run a large number of simulations where you use random numbers to determine what occurs in each simulation , and finally determine the percentage chance of some particular outcome occurring ( by counting how many times in the simulator that outcome occurred ) . For example let 's say you are a hockey fan , and there are 10 games left in the season , and you want to find the odds of varying teams making the playoffs . Since there are 150 games remaining , to figure out every possible way things could happen you need to determine 2 ^ 150 ( 1.42x10 ^ 45 ) different game outcomes ( and that 's ignoring the actual complexities of NHL scoring and tie breaking procedures , but it 's unimportant for this example ) .

A lot of the time they do things like gold - plate the connectors . That kind of thing is good for old - style ( analogue ) connections , because gold does n't oxidise nearly as much as most metals , so a gold - plated connector keeps a better quality connection for longer . However that is * not true * for HDMI . HDMI is digital , the information is effectively sent as 1s and 0s . So having the 1s and 0s be neater or clearer or bigger or whatever , does n't matter at all . As long as the TV can tell what 's a 1 and what 's a 0 , the entire signal comes through perfectly . In other words , HDMI cables either work completely perfectly or they do n't work at all . If a $ 10 cable gives you any kind of picture on your screen at all , that picture is exactly as good as the picture from a $ 100 cable .

Calculating the probability is simple if the two things are " independent . " Basically , independent things do n't effect each other or are not related . Here 's an example of independent events . Say you roll a dice and flip a coin at the same time . The probability of rolling a ( say ) 4 and flipping a head is 1/6 x 1/2 = 1/12 . It 's simply the multiplication of the probability of rolling a 4 ( 1/6 ) with the probability of flipping a heads ( 1/2 ) . But not all events are independent . Say we roll our dice first and flip the coin only if we roll a 5 or a 6 . Otherwise , we declare a heads if the number is even and tails if the number is odd . ( A side note : I could have gotten rid of the random flip upon rolling a 5 or a 6 to make the flip completely determined by the roll . But I want to emphasize that dependent events can still be related in a random way . One event does n't have to cause the other with pure certainty . ) The probability of rolling a 4 is still 1/6 . The probability of flipping a heads is still 1/2 . However , the probability of rolling a 4 and flipping a heads is not 1/12 , as it was when the events were independent .

When you are a theoretical physicist , you have a job of explaining things that ca n't be seen . One of the things they are working on now is that a black hole can be created at a level smaller than can be seen . All good so far , because at a super small , sub - atomic , level , you can make up your own rules since no one can see it anyway . So , the theoretical physicist says that a black hole is a hole in space . ( It is n't , a black whole is just a super massive , super dense ball of gas . ) The theory is that you can take this hole , and stretch the end of it somewhere . Maybe stretch it out the distance light could travel in a minute . If you can stretch this non - existent hole out into space at the speed of light , you can travel ahead in time . The reason you can time travel is because time slows down the faster you go . So , you would be one minute younger than anybody that did n't go through your tunnel . Stretch the tunnel out for the distance light could travel in 1000 years , and you would be 1000 years in the future .

Most children start school around 4 or 5 with kindergarten . This is the youngest level of school that the government says everyone must go to . Some parents put their children in preschool at an even younger age , but that 's almost like day care and may not actually teach very much . After kindergarten is elementary school ( they may both be part of the same actual school building ) . Elementary contains grades ( or years ) 1 through 6 . After Elementary is Junior High ( also called Middle School ) , which usually is grades 7 and 8 , though it some areas it is 6 through 8 , 7 through 9 , or 6 through 9 . Junior High is usually the first level at which students do n't stay with one teacher for the whole day , but move from class to class . It 's also the first time students may have some choice of what subjects they want to study . The final level of school required by the U.S. government is High School , which usually is grades 9 through 12 . These four years are often referred to as " Freshman " , " Sophmore " , " Junior " , and " Senior " years , in that order .

Haiku is a minimalist form of poetry . Although traditional Japanese haiku was written in a 5 - 7 - 5 syllabic structure , many English - speaking writers and translators do n't conform to this pattern because of the differences in grammar and rhythm between the two languages . A poem with 17 syllables in English tends to sound wordy and less precise than a poem written in Japanese with the same number of syllables . Therefore , many contemporary English haiku writers use 17 syllables as a maximum and often compress the poems into around 11 - 13 syllables . They believe these shorter poems more closely approximate the Japanese form , although this remains controversial . The purpose of haiku is communication and awareness , like conveying an experience . Along with other forms of writing and poetry , it is a vehicle for conveying feelings , sentiments , impressions , perceptions to other people . What then is the form of a haiku ? Some of the critical aspects of haiku form are : * Brevity : one to three lines totaling 17 syllables or less ; the average length of published English - language haiku tends to be about 13 syllables .

It 's not really a " vs. " thing - they work in tandem . First off , lets define multicore processors , like dual and quad core . A multicore processor is a singular piece of computer hardware with two or more actual processors ( hence " dual - core " ) , which execute instructions from the operating system . This basically means that two or more processors are slapped together . Picture conjoined twins - they share the resources in order to accomplish a task . Within a core , you have processes . Within processes you have threads . Threads are used to split the load of the process , basically . Each thread has a different thing to do in order to execute the process . Because of this , they help to share resources , like RAM . It 's teamwork -- many hands ( or threads , in this case ) make light work . What I just spoke of does n't happen on a hardware level ( ie . in the processor ) - threads are actually " scheduled " by the operating system . The handling of multiple threads by a processor is called multithreading . On a single core processor ( rare these days ) , multithreading is done by , essentially , multitasking ; the processor switches between threads .

Einstein 's theory of special relativity is actually quite simple . It 's general relativity that gets overly complicated . The core concept to understand is that no matter your frame of reference , you will always measure light traveling at the speed * C * . For example , if you are standing still and a train moves by you at 100 mph , you 'd measure it at 100 mph . If you 're driving in a car at 40 mph in the same direction as the train , and it passes you , you 'd only measure it moving away from you at 60 mph . With light though , it does n't matter if you are standing still , in a car or a train or a space shuttle , you always measure light at * C * . This means that the things that make up speed , distance and time , must not be absolute . They are relative to a frame of reference . As your speed approaches the speed of light , strange things start happening . For one it takes more and more energy to accelerate the same amount . Your mass increases . Space in front of you gets scrunched up , while space behind you gets stretched out . Time " slows " relative to other frames of references . This is how the time travel would work .

In order to understand this , you have to understand something about writing surfaces . I 'll just use paper for an example . Paper is not completely flat . While it might feel rather smooth , it actually has fibers sticking up out from it , somewhat like ' teeth ' , jutting out from the surface . When a pencil is scrapped across the paper , the graphite is broken off on these ' teeth ' , and that 's what you see as a mark . The softer the graphite , the deeper into these teeth the pencil reaches . The same idea works for erasers . They work by grabbing the graphite away from the paper . Again , the softer the eraser , the deeper it can reach down into the paper and the better it erases . Most pencils like the ones you 'd use in school have rather hard and stiff erasers , which do n't work very well . The higher quality ones , such as those an artist might use , tend to be softer .

I 'll try to be as non - rigorous and quick about it as possible . ---- * I. Euclidean Spaces * I assume you 've heard of some of the following concepts : points , lines , planes , space . These are the " Euclidean spaces " in 0 dimensions , 1 dimension , 2 dimensions , and 3 dimensions respectively . What does that mean ? The dimension of a space is the fewest number of directions you need to get anywhere . In a plane , you can get anywhere by going in the east - west direction a bit and then north - south a bit . In space you need to add in up - down . On a line , you only need east - west . On a point , well , you do n't need anything at all . Good ? Good . So why are they Euclidean ? That just means they 're not curved and they have no holes . Not curved means if you walk in a line you 'll never get back home . A sphere is curved . If you walk in a line , you 'll get back home . No holes means any roundtrip path you take can be shrunk down progressively smaller until it becomes a point .

A darknet is basically a secret internet among people who trust each other . In the normal internet , you want to access a website , so your computer connects to the website through your provider and asks for the content . Your provider can see everything you access . In a darknet , you 're only connected to people you trust , more like an actual web . So if you want something that someone else has , you find the shortest path to them . For example , let 's say there are a couple of people who are in the same darknet . A , B , C et cetera . You are connected to the darknet through your friend A who you trust absolutely . A is connected to both you and B. B is connected to A and C. The graph looks like : ` You < - > A < - > B < - > C ` If you want something that C has , your computer asks A for it , A asks B for it , and B asks C for it . The idea is that you can still get the content even though you might not want C to know you want it . From C 's perspective , it can be either B himself or any of B 's friends ( or friends of friends ) who want it . From B 's perspective , it can be either A , or any of A 's friends .

I know that this is n't exactly the question you asked , but I thought it might be helpful to clarify that " write off " can mean different things in different situations . This often makes it a very confusing term . Let 's say there is a boy named Tom . Tom starts a lemonade stand as a business . Tom must keep track of the business 's * assets * and * liabilities * on a document called a * balance sheet * . Assets are things that help the business make money , such as cups , lemon presses , pitchers , tables , chairs , etc . Suppose one day , Tom drops a glass pitcher , and it shatters into pieces . An asset that was previously valuable is now worth nothing , and must be " written off " of the balance sheet . This is one type of write off . When accountants who are not preparing taxes use the term " write off , " this is usually what they mean . For another example , suppose that another kid named Bob wants to buy some lemonade , but does n't have any money with him . Tom agrees to let Bob have some lemonade now , and pay the money later . Tom puts the debt on the balance sheet as an asset . Bob , however , moves out of town , and is never seen again .

In a crystal of PZT , the most common piezo material ( found in lighters , microphones , watches etc ... ) there is a lattice of atoms that becomes deformed . Specifically , there is a positive metal ion surrounded by negative oxygen ions . Now , when the metal is exactly in the middle , the charge in every direction is equal . With pressure , the metal atoms each shift inside their unit cells . Since the metal is more positive , the side that it moves to makes that side of the crystal more positive , and the opposite side more negaative . Remember though that these materials are insulators so they produce high voltage with low current .

When a computer writes something to a disk , like when you 're installing something , it has to do two things . First , it has to write the data to the disk . This takes up most of the time . Then it has to make a record in a special part of the disk called an index that says " the data you 're looking for is over here " so that the disk can remember to find it again later and so that it is n't overwritten by accident when more data is written . When removing something from the disk , like when uninstalling , the computer just needs to remove the record from the index . That will make the disk " forget " that the data is there . This takes a lot less time than actually writing the data .

For instance , suppose you are programming a little robot that can move around on a piece of paper . The robot has a pen in its belly , so it draws a line wherever it goes . You would like to get the robot to draw a square . But all it knows how to do is * go forward or back by some number of inches * , and * turn left or right by some number of degrees * . So you have to tell it how to make a square out of those moves . You might write a program like this : to draw_a_square forward 2 right 90 forward 2 right 90 forward 2 right 90 forward 2 right 90 end If the robot runs that program , it will have drawn a square , and ended up back where it started . The light receptor cells in the human eye do not correspond to red , green , and blue ; they would be better described as yellow green and violet . Our brain then identifies what color the light is by looking at the relative responses of those three types of cells . [ here ] ( URL_0 ) is an image that shows the absorption spectra of the three types of human cone cells . So , if light entered your eye in around the 555 nm range , the M(green ) and L(yellow ) cells would be strongly activated , while the S(blue ) cells would not . Your brain would therefore interpret this as yellowish green light . There is no cell that corresponds to red light , but when red light strikes the retina the L cells are most strongly activated , then the M cells less strongly , and the S cells least of all . The brain interprets this as red light . Incidentally , I believe the fact that the L and M cells are so " close " on the spectrum explains why the green to orange portion of the spectrum is the easiest to differentiate .

IP addresses are just numbers that designate a connection . You get one assigned by your service provider to your modem , into which you plug in your router . The reason Local Area Network ( ie all the computers in your house ) IP addresses do n't conflict with the rest of the world is because they ca n't actually be reached by the rest of the world without a few tricks . As far as your service provider is concerned , they gave you only one ip address ; that ip address happens to be tied to your router . The router polices traffic from all of your devices - when a particular device asks for , say , URL_0 , it makes sure to remember that device , and then sends the request itself . When the reply comes back , it redirects it back to only that device . This way , you can have whatever IPs you want for all your devices connected to that router because they never actually communicate directly with anything but your router . DNS is the Domain Name Service . Because people do n't really want to remember lists of semirandom numbers for what website they want to go to , DNS was born . Its a giant tree - like structure of servers that know a certain amount of information on each address .

So imagine you have two completely separate , giant office buildings with hundreds of offices between them . It uses something called a * bimetallic switch * . Your kettle heats the water using an electrical current . A switch is a break in an electrical circuit , which switches it off . A bimetallic switch is a switch made from two kinds of metal stuck together . One of the metals bends one way at high temperatures , while the other bends back as it cools . The bimetallic switch is calibrated so that it bends to break the circuit when the water reaches boiling point . Once the water cools , it bends back , allowing you to switch it back one when you need to . Clever science in a simple household appliance !

First thing to remember is that language changes over time . It changes as it passes from generation to generation , and even over the course of your lifetime . No two people talk exactly the same . We 've all got our own little idiosyncrasies - words we prefer , words we avoid , etc . This personal way of talking is called an ' idiolect . ' We tend to sound like the people we are closest to . Family ( parents ) close friends , neighbors . In turn , they tend to sound like people they are closest to , including you . You get a large group of people , they will each have their own way of talking , but it will be fairly similar - it averages out , more or less . These tend to be geographical - people tend to sound like people they interact with a lot , which tends to be people they live near . So you 've got a group of people who you interact with a lot , who live near you - this is a * dialect * or an * accent * ( the main difference is , an accent is only how you pronounce words , a dialect also includes words you use that others do n't . Good example is * bubbler * - in Wisconsin , it means drinking fountain . Anywhere else , it means you 're from Wisconsin ) .

Video games are made from Building blocks of code stacked on Building blocks of code . These blocks , called ( methods / classes / or subroutines ) accomplish a task , such as adding a number or checking a variable . A complicated program ( video game ) has thousands of methods or subprograms that are run constantly . imagine you made a SUM program that adds all of the numbers together in a list . then you made a DIVIDE program that takes an inputted number and divides it by the number of items on a list . Together these two programs could be combined to give you an average . To do that you would make a program that calls first the Sum program , and then the Divide Program and call it the Average Program . Now in the future , if you want an average , you do n't have to add and divide numbers , you simply run the Average program and give it a list . Imagine running a program that is 20 lines long , but executes thousands of smaller programs which make up millions of lines of code . Once you build the framework , you can accomplish complicated tasks with very little code . This is the basis of [ Object - Oriented Programming ] ( URL_0 ) .

Atoms of metals connect to each other in a very special way . They share their electrons with each other , but not in the conventional sense where only two atoms grab on to the electron and hold it . Instead , the atoms are free to move about in a " sea of electrons " that flows between and around all the metal atoms . This explains why metals are good conductors , but what 's so great about copper ? Well , copper atoms are n't very attracted to each other . which means that the " sea of electrons " has more wiggle room to move around . ( They have only one atom in the d sub - level ) Combine that with durability , ductility , stability , and relative abundance and you have the perfect charge carrier .

Tides are just gravity pulling and distorting things . Our sun and moon both pull on the earth . This raises and lowers water levels . This is n't restricted to just water though . Rocks that make up planets , and moons are also affected by gravity and tides . Grab a ball of Play - doh and roll it into a ball . Now you have a planet / moon . Squeeze it just a little so it is distorted a small bit in two directions . This is what a planet / moon looks like under tidal pressures . Now rotate that ball a bit , and warp it again . Rotate it some more and warp it some more . I hope you see where i 'm going with this . Every time your planet / moon rotates the other body distorts it towards one another . As it continues to rotate it is distorted again and again . With a LOT of gravity , like Jupiter and it 's moon IO , the constant distortion and friction generates massive amounts of heat on IO , and makes it geologically active . But with our moon , friction just slows down the moon 's rotation to a point where it is tidally locked . It no longer has to distort constantly due to tides ; the " heavy " side is always facing Earth .

In the old days , whenever you wrote to a drive , you would n't be able to do anything else until it was done . As operating systems and computers became more complex , somebody came up with the idea of stuffing the data into memory ( since writing to memory is going to be hundreds of times faster ) and writing it to disk in the background ( called ' caching ' ) , so your program becomes usable immediately . While this is great for usability , if the drive gets removed , you lose power , or the system crashes , your data might end up lost or corrupted . When you tell the computer to " safely remove " a device , it forces all the data in memory to be safely written to the drive immediately , so that no corruption occurs .

It 's very , very rare to find complete , intact dinosaur skeletons . Here 's one example , [ the famous Archaeopteryx skeleton ] ( URL_2 ) . Most of the time you find incomplete skeletons with all the bones jumbled up , or just scattered individual fossil bones . Without a complete skeleton that 's still got everything in place , you look at all the individual bones found at a given site and try to figure out which ones are from the same animal and how they fit together . This process used to be very difficult-- we 've gotten better at it over time , mostly because we 've found more intact skeletons to use as models , and partly because we now have better technological tools to help analyze and sort fossils . The brontosaurus controversy came about because a pair of 19th century paleontologists were racing to see who could classify the most dinosaur species , and one of them got sloppy . [ Othniel Charles Marsh ] ( URL_0 ) put together a skeleton from a bunch of [ sauropod ] ( URL_1 ) bones and called the new species * brontosaurus * .

Not all languages do , as you know , but we can be more specific than that . Nearly all of the languages that * do * capitalize the first letter of a sentence ( or * any * letters at all , really ) are those that use the [ Latin alphabet ] ( URL_1 ) . The reason most of those languages capitalize has a lot to do with the historical development of written Latin . You see , written Latin was n't always divided into upper - case and lower - case letters . An important thing to remember is that most languages start out as spoken languages , and only become written languages when people start to find uses for writing things down . A lot of the elements of written language that we think of as basic parts of language only really develop as we figure out ways to write down what we 've said . For example , completely oral languages ( that is , languages that have n't yet been codified into a written form ) have no periods or commas .

On the scale of the really small , everything you see and feel ( matter , forces , energy ) is made out of tiny tiny building blocks called particles . There 's years ' worth of study in this field , which is known as quantum mechanics , but it 's important to understand one major part known as the Standard Model . The Standard Model is essentially a Periodic Table of Elements for all of the different types of particles . Some particles make up matter ( like atoms ) , others act as messengers and transmit forces ( think magnetic forces ) , but what 's important is that the Standard Model is supposed to explain why matter and forces act the way we do . The good news : the Standard Model does this , and it does it * insanely well * . It makes prediction after prediction and continues to match up with experiment . However , there 's an important part missing : what gives things mass ? Despite a century of understand into what makes stuff stick together or explode or attract , we do n't know why anything has mass .

Certain diseases are related to genes . Now for every gene in your body it has a partner . You have two sets of genes , one from mom and one from dad , and need both to live . Some times a defect or change in the gene causes a disease . Now here is the tricky part : if the change is only in one of the two copies of the gene and you get the disease , it is called Dominant . If you need the defect in both copies it is Recessive . Lets make up a gene , called DERP1 . Remember you have two copies of DERP1 , mom and dad versions or DERP1 ( m ) and DERP1 ( f ) . Your DERP1 ( m ) is defective , i.e. it does n't work and can not be used to make proteins , but DERP1 ( p ) is just fine and there is no disease . You are a CARRIER for a disease of DERP1 , but you do not have it , because it is Recessive and you need both copies to be defective to have a disease . Now DERP1 defects are rare , so if you marry some random woman , the odds of her and you both having a DERP1 defect are small , and you wo n't pass along the disease to your kids . But your sister may also be a carrier for the defective DERP1 from mom .

It has to do with * * energy states * * and * * activation energy * * . Firstly , to clarify , flame is a reaction with oxygen . Hydrogen ' burning ' is Hydrogen ( H2 ) reacting with Oxygen ( O2 ) to produce water ( H2O ) . Since air is ~21 % oxygen , when you burn hydrogen in air , it reacts with oxygen . Water has a higher * * energy state * * than hydrogen , so when oxygen and hydrogen react , is releases energy . Now onto activation energy . Most reactions do n't just ' happen ' . If they did everything would just instantly react together , right ? Most reactions require what is called * * activation energy * * . It 's the energy input you need to start the reaction . In the case of hydrogen and oxygen , the activation energy is quite small . You use energy in the form of fire ( like a match ) . When the hydrogen touches the fire , it gets enough energy from it to reach it 's activation energy , so it can react with oxygen . As mentioned above , this releases energy . If you have a lot of hydrogen and a lot of oxygen , it releases a lot of energy . When a lot of energy gets released quickly , it 's usually observed as an explosion .

Intuitively , many people think the answer should be 50 % . After all , the chance of one dog being male should n't be conditional on the gender of the other ! But try enumerating the choices . If B represents a boy and G represents a girl , each of BB , BG , GB , and GG dogs has a 25 % chance . Knowing that at least one is a boy lets you exclude only the last option , and of the remaining 3 ( which are all equally probable ) only 1 is the BB result you 're looking for . Where 's the issue ? Well , it 's difficult to explain in a satisfying way , because human intuition is just * so bad * at conditional probability . The basic problem is that " at least one dog is a boy " is n't a statement about one particular dog ; depending on the facts , it could refer to either . So the truth value of the statement says something about * both * dogs , meaning the probability of either one being male can be conditional on it .

Do you want to know about the theory behind them , or about which ones are better in which situations and how to use them ? Video is a series of still images ( called * frames * ) played rapidly in a row . Most commonly , people will use 24 frames per second ( * 24fps * ) for video ; that 's 24 still images played quickly enough that it seems like smooth motion . Each of these images is made up from many tiny coloured squares , called * pixels * . Think of a [ mosaic art piece ] ( URL_0 ) ; the more pieces of mosaic -- pixels -- you use , the more detailed the image can be . The number of pixels used in an image is called its * resolution * . To illustrate the differences in resolution : a DVD has 345,600 pixels per frame , HDTV has around 921,000 , and Blu - ray has over 2 million . For every second of video you see on a Bluray , the player is putting 49.76 million tiny coloured squares on the screen in a specific order . That 's a * lot * of information . The player would have to say " Put a red square first . Then a blue square . Then a yellow square . Then a green square " to the TV almost 50 million times a second .

Infinities are an interesting subject . The word infinite is really a shorthand for a variety of related things . Some * thing * , anything really , is called infinite in some sense if , in that sense , it is unbounded . Now , there are two major kinds of infinite : countable and uncountable . Countably infinite structures can be paired up with the natural numbers and uncountable ones can not . Countable sets are unbounded in the number of elements you can identify in them , but there is always a " unit " element that is added when you " count " . Uncountable sets are unbounded in the number of elements you can identify , but there is no " unit " element , so they are also unbounded in how many elements can find in some range . There are many more kinds of infinite , but they are n't much more exciting than these two , as far as I know . The practical use of this relies on the fact that structures described as infinite have some property in common with other infinite structures . This allows you to express things in one structure in terms of another .

The spinning of the fan is done by a motor . That motor is n't 100 % efficient . Some of its energy is turned into heat due to friction . This is exactly the same reason that the engine in a car heats up when it 's running . So , why do you feel cool when you use a fan ? Well , as long as the air around you is cooler than you are you will naturally cool off . In the same way that if you mix hot and cold water you get warm water , the heat in your body mixes with the cooler air around you and reduces your temperature and increases the temperature of the air . This works well until the air directly next to your skin is the same temperature as your body . That warm air needs to move away so more cool air can get close to your and cool you off . This is what a fan does . As the air near your body heats up , the fan pushes it away so that more cool air can get close to your skin faster . So , a fan does n't actually lower the temperature of the air . In fact , because its motor is n't 100 % efficient , it raises the temperature . But , it does move the air you 've warmed up away from you faster so you can cool off easier .

First off , remember that sound is vibrations in the air . The vibrations hit out ear drums , and are transmitted to the brain and interpreted . That 's kind of like how a record works . The grooves of a record contain tiny , tiny bumps . A needle , usually made of diamond , is attached to a thin , metal strip inside the record player 's tone arm . As the needle travels down the grooves , it hits the bumps and it moves up and down . This causes the metal strip to vibrate . The vibrations are sent to the cartridge , which are then turned into electrical signals , then amplified , and then sent out the speaker as sound . The needle and metal strip are like ears ; they receive the vibration . The cartridge is like a simple brain ; it interprets the vibrations and lets you understand them .

Itch follows the same neural tracts as pain ( which are separate from vibratory , fine discrimination , and proprioceptive sensation tracts ) but it is n't pain because pain causes a recoil reflex , whereas itch causes a scratch reflex . Largely , the stimulus to itch is histamine release and detection by neurons , but there are other stimuli . Interestingly , mast cells , which are white blood cells in your skin ( and responsible for a lot of allergy - related stuff ) degranulate and release histamine when stimulated . They can be stimulated by allergens ( like in drug reactions , atopic dermatitis , hives , poison ivy , etc ) or other stuff ( like hot water in the shower ) . Once they release the histamine , the nerves pick it up and you process it as itch .

This is a tricky question to answer because the terms can be easily confused . First , let 's clarify exactly what refresh rate is . Refresh rate refers to how often the screen is sent a signal from the onboard computer to update the pixels on it , and it 's measured in Hertz ( Hz ) . This is not the same as the framerate of the content you are watching , which is measured in frames per second ( fps ) and is a lot slower . This is * also * not the same as the " 600Hz " number bandied about by the Plasma TV makers . Before you continue , please read my explanation on [ how LCD , LED and Plasma TVs work ] ( URL_0 ) . It 'll help you understand the next part better . So this " 600Hz " number refers to the * subfield * rate of the set . This is where the screen sends a brief charge to each pixel to make it light up . It is n't actually * changing * any of the pixels , it 's just making them light up , over and over and over again , 600 times a second . This is done to maintain a smooth , constant level of light output . If it happened any slower , you would start to see the entire screen flicker very slightly , enough to bother you .

There are four forces of nature . You 've all probably heard of electromagnetism . There are two more which are less know but just as important . The strong force holds every nucleus together and the weak force is responsible for radioactivity . The bosons are the carriers of these four forces . You have photons for electromagnetism , gluons for the strong force and the W and Z bosons for the weak force . Gravity is an outsider and does n't have a boson for as far as we know . The quarks are the buildingblocks of protons and neutrons . Those quarks are held together by the strong force . Leptons are a bit rarer and less known . The most common lepton is the electron and revolves around a nucleus . The force that keeps the electrons around the nucleus is electromagnetism . After all , the electrons are negativly charged and the protons in the nucleus positive . I hope this clears things up a bit , but this explanation is far from complete . Triglyceride are long chains of carbon molecules that , when burned , release TONS of energy . In this sense they are largest the energy reserve for the body . Energy storage is good for our bodies , but remember too much of a good thing is n't always good . Below are separate explanations for why triglycerides are bad . Excess triglycerides are known to be main cause of diabetes type II . When your fat cells start to store too much , your body realizes that there 's something wrong . Your own immune system detects this and start attaching to these fat cells . They start releasing signals to tell your fat cells to release more triglycerides into the blood stream . These fats can go through the body and signal your muscles to take up the fats instead of glucose ( your body 's main energy source ) . This causes too much glucose build up in your blood , and that in itself causes more stress on the body . Fats are also involved in the development of plaques in the blood vessels . See , your body uses molecules called VLDL molecules to transport fats from your fat cells to your muscle . Cholesterol is packaged into the mix because it likes to come for the ride .

You see those little " garbage can " things on the power poles in your neighborhood ? They step the powerline voltage down from 10,000 volts to 240V and 120V , and they send out wires to many nearby houses . ( They 're transformers , basically the same as little black cube power supplies for recharging batteries . ) You see the thing in the above photo ? It 's a bunch of transformers for stepping down 100,000 volts coming in from the really tall power poles with the three evenly - spaced wires . It gets stepped down to around 10,000v and sent out to many nearby neighborhoods . But there are two extra things in that photo : huge circuit - breaker cabinets , and clusters of little tuning capacitors . Suppose a tree falls on a 10,000v power line ( or on 100,000v power line . ) If you try to automatically turn off power using a switch , the spark just jumps across the switch . Even if the switch is 20 ft across , you 'll just form lightning . The current wo n't halt . To stop the lightning , you need special cutoff switches inside high - pressure insulating material . They 're circuit breakers , but rated for 100 kilovolts . That 's inside the cabinets .

The really simple reason is that multiplication is counting X amount Y times . So , if you do 3 x 5 , you 're counting three five times , and adding up the total ( 15 ) . If , on the other hand , you multiply 15 by one third , you 're counting up one third of fifteen . So , when you 're dealing with fractions multiplied by fractions , you 're essentially counting part of a part . So , take this out of the realm of fractions for a second . If I multiply 1000 by 1/2 , it 's 500 ( because I 'm counting up to half of the original ) . And if I multiply 500 by 1/2 , it 's 250 . So , what 's the relationship between the final result and the original ? The result is 1/4 of the original . So , if we now take the numbers out , we simply know that a number multiplied by 1/2 twice becomes 1/4 of the original , thus 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4 .

The US refrained from aiding Israel up until the early 1960 's . The context was the Cold War and a policy of containment that sought to minimize Soviet / Communist influence whether it was in the Near East , Asia , Eastern Europe , etc . Arab regimes in the region were also supported in this manner and on equal footing until the Johnson administration decided to encourage Israel 's qualitative edge . Growing anti - Western sentiment in Iraq , Syria , Egypt in the 70 's and an increasing awareness of the non - interest of Arab states to militarily support the US in the region led to a cementing of what had become the US policy of Israeli support . It is important to note that Israel is on a rather long list of countries that receives aid which is disbursed to emerging / young countries , countries recovering from war and strategic allies . Israel does receive more military and economic aid than other nations in return for perceived benefits and capacity for reciprocation that Israel represents .

Binary is a different form of counting . The standard counting system , 1 , 2 , 3 etc is a decimal system and you count with units , tens , hundreds etc . Binary is different and instead of everything being in 10s , it is in 2s . You can match a binary number to any decimal number like so : binary decimal 00 0 01 1 10 2 11 3 etc . The 1s and 0s are represented by a switch in the computer , 1 is on and 0 is off . This means that a combination of these switches can make any number . When a certain number is made by these switches , a certain action will happen such as a pixel on the screen being on or off . By rapidly computing millions of these different numbers , the computer is able to form an image , or do a calculation !

A hard drive contains flat circular pieces of a material that can be magnetized and demagnetized . It rotates as an arm with a device at the end that floats over the disk . The device at the end of the arm can either read the magnetization of the disk as it rotates under it or in can change the magnetization , to write data . Each bit ( a single 1 or 0 ) is represented as the magnetization of a certain area of the disk . The smaller the area , the more bits fit on the drive , and so the more data you can store on the drive . As technology improves , companies can make disks and heads that can read and write the magnetization of smaller and smaller areas of the disk , which is why the amount of data you can store on a new hard drive increases over time .

Chimps and gorillas utilize sign language as system with which to request goods / services and relate intentions / emotions . Human language is unique from this in that it can also create novel concepts and statements as well as address concepts beyond those that we might need to acquire food and social control . Non - human primate sign language lacks this aspect and is used by the apes purely to gain material and social resources , not to relate abstract concepts and novel ideas . In this sense it is not full language , as defined by human abilities , and thus the " lesser " of the great apes can not be said to posses language , but rather a complex system of communicating intentions . ( For further information I would direct you to research the foundations of linguistic anthropology and the academic definition of language . ) * * EDIT * * Additionally , humans have a vocabulary of thousands of words and can systematically place these words into the grammatical structure of a sentence ( syntax ) . Gorillas and chimps that have learned sign language generally only know a couple hundred words at best , and lack the ability to place these words into a sentence .

We do n't know how big the universe is . When we look farther and farther out into space we see older and older light from stars many millions of light - years away , and the light was sent out the same amount of years ago . We can also see that the wavelength of the light have become longer and our explanation is that the space that the light have traveled through has expanded , stretching the light . When we look farthest out for the longest wavelengths we can see farther back in time , to the beginning of the universe . We see the background radiation of the big bang . This is the edge of our known universe . We do n't know how big it is , but we can see how old it is . As the universe expands some of the farthest light wo n't reach us . This is because the stretch of space between the light - source and us will expand at a faster rate than the light can cover . This theoretically means that if we look at the distant galaxies they will slowly disappear over time because the new light they send out wo n't be able to cover the expanding distance to us . After a very very long time , we will only be able to see the light from the stars in our galaxy .

The internet , is kind of like a series of tubes . Ok with that out of the way . The internet is kind of like a maze of rooms , where you can only talk to the people in the rooms attached to yours . Each room has a number ( IP address ) , and there are some special messages ( routing protocols ) you pass back and forth which let you build up a book of all the other numbers on the internet ( routing / forwarding tables ) . Now this book does n't tell you exactly where the other room is , it just tells you where you need to hand off messages to get to this room . Every room updates it 's own book on where to reach every other room based on the special messages , then passes the messages onto all their neighbors to let them know how to reach everything they know how to reach ( in practice we do n't let EVERYONE know how to reach everything , but this is an ELI5 example ) . So I have this big maze , and we 're both somewhere in the middle of it , and I want to send a message to you . So I open my book to your page and it says I need to send a message to Fred to my north .

The caucuses are part of the US Primary election . Each state has a certain number of delegates for the Presidential Nominating Convention . Essentially , the state votes to select Delegates , these delegates than vote to select the Presidential nominee at the convention . States can have either " binding " primaries , which means votes are automatically given to the winner of the primary , or " non - binding , " which means the delegates are free to vote as they please at the convention . Non - binding primaries can result in flips at the convention , but in practice this rarely happens . States can also assign delegates in either a " winner takes all " fashion , or give them to candidates depending on how much of the vote they won in the state ( proportional primaries ) . Republican primaries can decide which version they will use , while all Democratic primaries have been proportional since 2006 . Anyway , in almost all states the primaries work just like a regular election : voters go to the polls , vote , and the delegates are assigned as explained above . In Iowa ( and Texas ) however , there is a caucus .

What is transubstantiation ? Let 's break it down . Trans - obviously to change . Substance - that which stands under . In the time the word " transubstantiation " was formed , the word substance was not " physically touchable stuff " but " essential nature , " i.e. that which stands under the physical object , that facet of being which lies under the purely physical . So what does it mean to transubstantiate ? It should be obvious - to change the internal nature of some object , i.e. to alter its essential being in some way . Not to change the physical nature of the object , but to change the being which that physical body delimits . This is of course an old conception of being which is n't the same as the modern " everything is just particles , " but if you accept any dualist thought it 's pretty easy to see where transubstantiation can make sense . If you just think about one of the shitty paradoxes where if you replace the hilt of a sword then replace the blade is it still that thing , you can see where this sort of being fits naturally into what humans think . Basically , the modern conception of being equates it with extancy .

It 's all about how you define " by the Constitution " . Basically it comes down to whether or not you think the Constitution should be interpreted and precedent should be considered or the wording should be explicitly followed . For instance , the federal government regulated the production of ADHD medication . This is usually done underneath the auspices of the Commerce Clause ( Article I , Section 8 , Clause 3 ) , saying that since the medicine can ( but might not ) be produced in one state and sold in another that the federal government can regulate the product . The constitution does n't actually mention the regulation of medicine or Adderall and an extremely strict constructionist would insist that the US government has no ability or right to decide what can be in the medication or who can receive it . They would leave this up to the states individually to regulate this . This would seem ridiculous , but it 's one example of skirting around the 10th amendment .

Each ear by itself can only hear how loud a sound is . However , both of your ears combined with your brain can tell the direction a sound comes from because one ear is often closer to the sound than the other ear , so that ear hears the sound first . Your brain can also tell that the quality of the same sound in one ear is different than the same sound in the other ear as the sound wave wraps around the shape of your head and the shape of your outer ears . With mono sound , there is only one channel of audio , so no matter how many speakers you have , they all play the same sound at the same volume . If you have one speaker , the sound always sounds like it comes from that speaker . If you have more speakers , the sound always sounds like it comes from a fixed spot in between the speakers . This is unusual in the real world , because imagine listening to a band where every instrument and the singer 's voice are all " placed " in the exact same position making their sounds . Instead , a more life - like sound spreads the instruments and voices in different locations .

Think of a program as being like a house . A house needs to be built from a blueprint so the people working on it know how to built it . However , even if they 've seen a similar house before , they do n't necessarily know how to build it just by looking at another one , even if it 's exactly the same as the new one is supposed to be . A source code is the blueprint of a program . When it goes through a process called " compiling " , the computer turns the source code into an executable program much like how the construction workers change the blueprints into a house . However , the executable does n't look just like the source code , as the source code is built to be a human readable code equivalent to what the computer can read while the executable is what it looks like after it is translated to the computer 's own language . This makes it so other programmers do n't know how to reproduce it just by looking at the executable program . Reverse engineering is theoretically possible with anything , but it is n't always easy , as you are trying to build a blueprint based on looking at the final product .

Ex - Navy fire control petty officer who had to take several months worth of radar training in order to be able to say that he was a fire control petty officer . :) From a military standpoint there are essentially two basic functional types of radar : Search radar and Tracking radar . Search radar is the classic ' sweep ' type that simply shows you everything in the area . It 's more or less realtime and good enough for tactical decisions like where to vector in fighters or deploy ordinance . It is n't , however , good enough to shoot a missile or gun at the target because the target is only lit while the radar is sweeping over it . ( The sweep is managed by physically rotating the radar emitter around . ) The other type , Tracking radar is different and again the difference is in the emitter head . It will be told to ' track ' a particular target and the head will swivel up / down / left / right as needed to keep the target in the center of the radar beam . ( Sometimes this is n't a physical movement but can be managed by electromagnets ) Of course the emitter can only swivel so far off axis so if the target moves beyond that limit then you will lose your ' lock ' on the target .

Why Paul likes the gold standard ( LI5 ): The United States , along with most other countries , has a currency that is a " fiat currency , " rather than a " representative currency . " A representative currency means that the currency is backed by a commodity , for instance , gold or silver . Libertarianism is a political philosophy which says the government 's power should be limited in size and scope , and freedom for the individual is the most important aspect of society . He wants to reduce government spending by ending wars , eliminate some of the inefficient government bureaus , and keep the federal government out of social issues such as marijuana legalization . There are actually several types of drugs that attack bacteria ( antibiotics ) . Each type targets a specific part of the bacteria to kill it . Pretty much all of these drugs actually come from bacteria though , since bacteria have been trying to kill each other for a few billion years . Humans have found a few species of bacteria that produce chemicals that are good at killing bacteria but bad at killing humans , since our cells are different . We refine these chemicals to make antibiotics . Because this bacterial civil war has been going on for billions of years though , bacteria have evolved defenses . The simplest defense is simply to have a system that pumps the antibiotic out of the bacterium fast enough that it does n't have time to work ( think pumping water out of a leaky boat ) . Bacteria have also evolved systems that bind to the antibiotic . This makes the drug unable to attach to its target ( think chaff confusing guided missiles ) . Another way to resist antibiotics is for the bacteria to change the target . Antibiotics aim for very specific parts of the cell , so even a minor change can cause resistance ( think of changing a lock ) .

Tesla was an inventor first and businessman second . Edison was the other way around . Tesla worked for Edison for a while after immigrating to the US from Eastern Europe . Tesla developed the concept of alternating current ( AC ) power and presented it to Edison . Edison , along with one of his benefactors Westinghouse , had already invested deeply into direct current ( DC ) power and was not willing to see his financial status be jeopardized by a competitive technology . Tesla went into business on his own promoting AC electricity as being more efficient in transmission over long distances , pissing off Edison royally . Edison spared no opportunity to try and discredit Tesla , including show piece demonstrations such as electrocutions by AC electricity to proved how " dangerous " it is and scare investors and adopters away from it . As it turned out , Tesla was absolutely correct about AC 's superiority in long - distance transmission . Without his efforts the development of electricity grids would have been reduced or never achieved until a later date ( if at all ) . But Edison was also correct in the importance of DC .

There are 4 basic settings , if you put everything ( camera and lens ) into manual mode , assuming no flash : * ISO : How sensitive the sensor will be to light . Low ISO ( like 100 or even lower ) is not very sensitive ( you need a lot of light to take the picture ) , but is the best quality . High ISO ( like 1600 or even higher ) is very sensitive ( you can take pictures even if it is kind of dark ) but is usually pretty noisy . * Aperture : How much light is the lens going to let in all at once ? Lower numbers ( like 4.0 or lower ) let in more light , but things that are not exactly in focus will be blurry . Higher numbers ( like 16 or higher ) let in ~~more~~ less light , but more things will be in focus . * Shutter speed : How long is the shutter going to be open for ? If the shutter is only open for 1/100th of a second or less , then less light will be let into the camera , but you will be able to " stop motion " more easily . If the shutter is open for a long time ( 1/30th of a second or more ) , then more light will be let into the camera , but moving objects will be blurry , and you may even need a tripod to keep the camera steady enough to take a good picture .

Fundamentally , it 's just a way of evaluating how slow an algorithm ( i.e. , a way of doing things ) can be if it has to do what it does on a large number of different things . Pretend there are two cashiers at the supermarket . One of them totals up what you have to pay by looking at each item individually and typing in its price . If there are 30 items , she has to type in 30 prices . Hence , if there are * n * items , then she has to type in * n * prices . We say that her way of doing things is O(n ) ( pronounced " big oh of n " ) . Pretend that another cashier has a different way of doing things . He weighs your cart once , and charges you a flat price for everything , depending on the weight . No matter how many items you have in your cart , it takes the same time to weigh your stuff . If it takes 1 minute to weigh your cart , it does n't matter if you have 10 items or 1000 ; it will always take one minute . So for * n * items , it takes a " constant " amount of time . In this case , we say that this way of doing things is O(1 ) ( pronounced " big oh of one " ) .

When an object travels faster , its length appears to get * shorter * . So if you saw a ruler traveling by you at a really high rate of speed , that ruler will simply appear to you to be shorter than it should be . But from the ruler 's perspective , the ruler is normal size . Suppose you were on a spaceship traveling very quickly . To outside observers , your spaceship looks squished . * But from your seat , the spaceship looks fine ... it 's the entire world around you that looks squished . * Suppose from an outside perspective you were coming up on a planet a million kilometers away . LY5 : Imagine you have a toy chest that you want to keep locked , but all you have are crummy plastic locks that are really easy to break open . So , you put 200 or 1000 of those bad boys on your toy chest and now , even though your locks are crummy , it 's still going to take a robber a really long time to get into it . Each " bit " is like one of those plastic locks . LY16 : The " bit strength " of an encryption scheme is basically a measure of how hard it is to get into . In computing a " bit " is just a one or a zero , and single binary digit . Encryption keys are just numbers of a certain size . 8 - bit , 16 - bit , 128 - bit , 256 - bit , etc . Now , the number of possible keys you can make with a certain number of bits doubles with each bit . Just like there 's are ten times as many two digit ( decimal ) numbers , than single digit numbers . I.E. 0 - 9=10 numbers , 00 - 99=100 numbers , 000 - 999=1000 numbers , etc . So , if an attacker does n't have any special way to break your encryption they just have to resort to trying every possible key . With a large enough number of bits , this can take a * very * long time .

Electricity is like a waterfall . The water flows from higher points to lower points . With electricity , this we have net electric charge instead of water . Voltage is like elevation of the waterfall . Current is the amount of water that flows down the waterfall . You may have heard of Ohm 's law before . We write V = I x R , where V is voltage , I is current , and R is is something called resistance . If we have a resistor with a certain value for R , putting a specific voltage across the two terminals of the device means the same current will flow through it every time . Ohm 's law describes what this current is . Memristors are a lot like resistors . They have two terminals . Current flows through them . The difference here is that their resistance changes .

The electoral college works by having a group of electors who select their state 's nomination for the presidency . They can vote for anyone they please but almost always declare who they will vote for prior to the election . In this way , when an average citizen votes for who they want to be president , they are actually indirectly voting for which elector will be allowed to vote for the president . By and large , the way most states operate is that whichever presidential candidate received the most votes from the general public , then only the electors that declared their vote for that candidate would be allowed to vote for the presidency . As such , even if 50.0001 % of the state 's citizens voted for the democratic nomination and 49.9999 % voted for the republican , only the democratic electors would be allowed to vote . Each state receives a number of electors in proportion to it 's population . So states with lots of people get more electors ( CA - 55 , TX - 38 , NY 29 , etc . ) and states with small populations get less ( Montana gets 3 ) .

Its hard to explain like you re 5 , but I will do my best . Matter is made up of things called atoms . The atom is made up of up to 3 particles known as the proton neutron and electron . The proton has a positive charge while the electron has a negative charge . Neutrons are neutral . There is this other particle called a photon , which is responsible for visible light , as well as the entirety of what s called the electromagnetic spectrum ( hint hint ) . Photons are given off as electromagnetic radiation . For the sake of simplicity lets talk about photons , electrons and their antiparticle , the positron . The electron and positron have the same properties except the positron has positive charge where the electron is negative . The easiest way to think about it is when 2 electrons are near , they exchange a photon . The photon acts like a little billiard ball . It pushes the electron that emitted the photon away , and the photon knocks into the other electron , pushing it away as well . This is repulsion . Attraction between an electron / positron is similar , but the resulting momentum pushes the particles towards each other instead .

If you 've ever salted your soup or your casserole or your stew you 've consumed salt water . Salt+water will have sloshed together around your digestive system before now . What we ca n't drink is water high in salt content , for the same reason we ca n't just eat piles of salt . Because it 's toxic in large quantities . Salt is an irritant to the stomach which triggers vomiting in large quantities - this may be partially an evolutionary response to discourage you from drinking dehydrating salty - water as your body really does n't want you to do that . So if you drink sea - water your body should just purge you ASAP to get rid of the excess salt . If you 're otherwise healthy it should just be unpleasant but if you 're already dehydrated or malnourished it can be fatal . Your body requires salt in small doses , it can deal with a certain amount at a time but a large concentration spells danger because it can rapidly dehydrate you . Too much salt over a long period carries more insidious dangers , In simple terms salt retains water ( through a process called osmosis ) and so having too much entering your blood stream thickens the blood and causes high blood pressure .

Buddhism comes from Buddha ( meaning ' the enlightened one ' ) , which is not a name but a title given to Prince Siddharta . He was born into royalty around 2500 years ago , somewhere in Nepal or North India . He had an easy upbringing and lived comfortably , until on one day , after his son was born , he saw three men in his city - one old , one diseased and one on his deathbed . For whatever reason that separates great men from their more ordinary counterparts , the experience had him shattered . He left his throne , wife and children , in search of an answer to why lives can be so different to one another , and , if there is a god , why there is pain , death and suffering while others enjoy great lives . After experiences with Hinduism , Jainism , fasting , and other occult religions brought him nowhere closer to the answers he wanted , around 4 years after he began his search , he sat down below a Bodhi ( Fig ) tree to meditate - vowing to not get up until he had understood . Forty days later , he became Enlightened . He attained a state of being that goes beyond anything else in the world .

Direct Democracy is a form of political system in which all people with the right to vote can take a direct part in making the decisions . So every proposal would be voted on by all citizens . In a representative democracy , the people choose other people ( the representatives ) to vote for them . It began in small communities , first in ancient Greece ( Athens is the most famous example ) , where around the 5th century B.C. a new political system was invented in which all full citizens ( those were only rich males , who had enough time to devote to political questions , women , slaves and immigrants from other cities had no right to vote ) would debate and vote in big assemblies . However , the Athenian democracy ended finally when they were conquered by Macedonia , which was ruled by a King . In modern times , direct democracy was ( and still in some parts is ) very prominent in Switzerland . Like ancient Greece , Switzerland is made up of very small districts , the Kantone , making direct democracy practicable . Switzerland nowadays is a so - called half - direct democracy . On all political levels , they have direct - democratic elements .

The general rule of thumb for interspecies breeding is that it comes down to chromosomes , which are strands of DNA . The rest of the Great Apes ( Gorillas , Chimps , Bonobos , Orangutans ) have 48 chromosomes , but 2 of these chromosome have fused in Humans , leaving us with 46 chromosomes . The greater the difference in the number of chromosomes , the harder it is for species to breed . Basically , the sex cells ( sperm / egg ) have problems aligning and combining when the chromosome count is off . This has n't stopped animals with different number of chromosomes from interbreeding . Mules are the best example . Horses have 64 chromosome and donkeys have 62 , so this is similar to the difference between Humans and the rest of the apes . A very , very good book about this is " [ The Measure of All Things ] ( URL_0 ) " , describing what early scientists went through to define the meter ( which is the first metric unit ) , and why . The meter was finally defined late in Louis XVI 's " ancien regime " . Although Louis himself saw the benefit and supported the effort , the concept was itself a pretty revolutionary idea -- up until then , most trade units were established through royal decree , and changed from place to place and from regime to regime . Many , many lengths were considered before the meridional definition ( one 10 - millionth of the semimeridian from the North Pole to the Equator , through Paris ) was adopted . Even that rather precise definition was n't particularly useful at first because the length of the meridian was only known to within a few percent . In order to measure the length , a whole new science ( * geodesy * ) was invented , and two stout heroes of Science ( or , rather , Natural Philosophy , as it was then called ) set out to measure the distance across France and Spain -- from Dunkirk to Barcelona -- as precisely as possible .

There are typically two types of cheat cartridge , Game Genie and Action Replay . Game Genie patches the ROM , Read Only Memory . For example , in the ROM of Shining Force 2 , a Medical Herb restores 10 HP . This is hard - coded into the game , and that data is transmitted to the hardware of the console . On its way to the console , it 's interrupted by the Game Genie , and the Game Genie changes the incoming value of 10 to something else . This can be anything like " Restore 20 HP " , or " Increase the character 's level " . Most Game Genie functions are very limited . Inversely , an Action Replay changes the RAM . Say Bowie has 80 HP , that 's in the RAM as a variable that can change . A Game Genie can change his starting HP , but it ca n't do anything to keep it up there . Action Replay devices work on two variables , Address , and Value . They typically look something like this : 57BD522D:00BF The Address is what the variable is . Every dynamic number in a game that can potentially change is a variable and can be changed . The Value combined with the Address freezes the variable at that number .

Often in a movie , you ’ll see a villain screw a " silencer " onto his pistol before shooting the hero ’s loved one . What exactly is a silencer , and how is it different from a suppressor ? In short , there is no such thing as a " silencer . " The term was invented in Hollywood , and is not a proper term , per se , although when it comes to legal terms ( such as in the National Firearms Act of 1934 ) , a silencer is the same thing as a suppressor . But in reality , " silencer " is simply the popular term for a suppressor . Alright then , what ’s a suppressor ? Well , a suppressor is any device which helps to muffle the report of a firearm when it is fired . When a firearm is fired , a small amount of gunpowder is exploded in order to propel the bullet down the barrel of the firearm . When this explosion reaches the muzzle of the weapon , it expands rapidly , making a loud report . The exact sound of the report varies from weapon to weapon , and its intensity depends on a number of things regarding the design of the muzzle , the absence or presence of a muzzle break or a flash suppressor and so forth .

With a little bit of inflation ( i.e. prices going up ) , people are encouraged to spend what they 've got so their money does n't lose value . The GDP tends to grow nicely in these conditions . With a lot of inflation , people want to instantly invest in bonds or commodities that are very stable . The idea is they want to turn their money into a product that wo n't change in value . So when inflation stops rising , they can sell their bonds or commodities , and effectively be where they left off . This hurts the economy , but it has a strange effect of artificially growing the GDP . ( If the cost of items has gone up , then the GDP also artificially goes up . ) For example , some of the more liberal economists have suggested we hyperinflate our way out of our national debt . Make everything perhaps 10 times more expensive to buy , so our employers give us 10 times as much , we spend 10 times as much , products cost 10 times as much . And now our national debt feels 10 times smaller . But getting there would almost certainly involve a huge recession along the way .

Imagine you are on a big empty playground that only has merry - go - round in the middle of it . You tired of the merry - go - round so you invent a new game . You mark out and number squares all over the play ground and in each square you put a card with the number of some other square . The game is look at the card and move to the new square as indicated by the card . Now repeat . For the Mandelbrot Game you want to use very special numbering and directions for moving . First use two numbers , not just one number . The first number is the distance to the merry - go - round for that square , for the second number you can imagine someone on the merry - go - round pointing at both the school and at you standing on the square . Depending on the square , there will be an angle between their arms . The second number is that angle ( so one arm is always pointing at the school house , the other is swinging around pointing at you depending on the square . ) Now what do the directions say on them ? Just the double angle of the current square and square the distance to the merry - go - round . So if you start on square ( 3 , 30 degrees ) you move to ( 9 , 60 degrees ) .

This is the most common form of sarcasm , and it is why it 's often assimilated to irony . * * * You could n't punch your way out of a wet paper bag . * * This is meant as a caustic , insulting remark , but it means exactly what it says . The GTD method is a style of planning that makes you " only think things once " and relies on two things to do it . 1 . Moving the stuff you normally try to keep in your head into a trusted external source that you check regularly . This could be a notepad , a binder , or even a file on your computer . This lowers your overall stress because you do n't have to remember every little thing that normally goes through your head , it 's all right there , the only thing you have to remember is to check it regularly . 2 . Planning out each step in advance . Again , this lowers your stress because you 've done all or most of the thinking beforehand . All you have to do is look at your list , cross off the action you 've just completed and look at it for the next step . It 's like having someone tell you exactly what to do instead of trying to figure it out on the fly . Personally , I like and use a lot of the GTD method , especially the notepad . Every morning I write a list of what I need to do , grouped by how important it is ( i.e. emails , phone calls , getting questions answered ) and work through it as the day goes on .
