Our behaviors are the result of neural networks ( basically " webs " which form associations and links between different behaviors , thoughts and actions ) - they are the strings and we are the puppets . Different strings control different behaviors , and when used in tandem they can produce very complex and intelligent looking behaviors . Some of these strings are added over the course of the puppet 's life , for example , suppose the puppet master wants his puppet to move each individual finger , then he might add a string to each finger . However , some of the strings are there from the very creation of the puppet . Importantly , there is no functional difference between the strings that are added throughout our lives , and the strings that are there from birth . The string , or neural network , just represents a specific response to a particular stimulus - for example , herring gull chicks will automatically peck at a red spot ( because their mothers have a red spot on their beak and pecking at it results in them getting food ) .

Let 's start with ` while ` loops because they are simpler . A ` while ` loop needs only one bit of information we 'll call the * * condition * * and takes the form while ( condition ) { DoStuff ( ) ; } When the code comes across your ` while ` loop , it checks the condition . If the condition is true ( or evaluates to a true value ) , the program runs the code between the braces : ` DoStuff ( ) ` in this case . After the execution , it checks the condition again . Eventually^ * , or even at the first check , the condition will be false . When that happens , we stop executing the code in the braces and continue after the loop . ` for ` loops seem more difficult , but when you understand them , they can be just as simple . Our ` for ` loop needs three bits of information : an * * initialiser * * , a * * condition * * and something I 'll call the * * incrementer**^ * * . It takes the following form : for ( initialiser ; condition ; incrementer ) { DoStuff ( ) ; } Like I said , the execution is rather simpler than it looks . First , before looking at the condition , we 'll execute the initialiser . We'll usually use it to set up the variables used for our loop .

Historians use the term " Renaissance " to described both a specific period in European history , and for periods of cultural rebirth in other historical contexts ( ex . " The Carolingian Renaissance " ) . As a historical period it forms a nice bridge from the Medieval period and the Early Modern period . Although start dates may vary ( the invention of the printing press in 1440 , the fall of Constantinople in 1452 , the discovery of the new world in 1492 ) most generally agree that it began in the 15th century and ended in the 17th . Chronology becomes a bit more tricky if the Renaissance is considered in the context of a cultural movement . Artistic innovation based on classical models began in Italy far earlier ( 13th century ) and in places like far northern and eastern Europe , the new ideas took considerably longer to arrive . So to answer your question a bit more directly , it is a time period because of the movement which spread through Europe caused a cultural change which later authors felt differentiated the period enough from earlier and later modes of thinking to warrant its own name .

First off , sorry to hear it . My friend 's husband just passed away from a brain tumor that he 'd been fighting for years . Cancer sucks . Cancer is a big blanket term for a bunch of different things . They all have one thing in common : the body 's cells start dividing and do n't stop . Normally cells have limits on them , but with cancer , they just start going nuts . They keep dividing over and over . That 's what a tumor is - a bunch of cells of a particular sort that just keep dividing . Depending on what sort of cancer it is ( what sort of cells are dividing ) there are various effects . But the endgame for most cancers is that parts of the tumor break off into the bloodstream , land somewhere else , and start growing there . Your body has weird cells like this all the time , but most of the time your immune system gets 'em first or they do n't manage to get access to the bloodstream ( nutrients and such ) . But when your immune system does n't get them , that 's when they become a malignant cancer . So , short story : cancer is when a part of the body goes nuts and does n't stop growing .

Conservatives tend to maintain the * status quo * . Typically , this means that what 's good right now is what we should continue . Liberals tend to buck the * status quo * and try to " progress . " This means attempting to change the current status in hopes that it improves . Democrat and Republican are party affiliations . Currently , Republicans are considered conservative ( * status quo * ) while Democrats are considered liberal ( " progress " ) because of their political stances . It has not always been this way . For example , in the 1850 's Democrats attempted to maintain slavery while Republicans ( such as Abraham Lincoln ) freed slaves by declaring them to have equal rights . This standpoint switched during the Great Depression . The Republicans attempted to maintain a smaller governmental stance on economics the Democrats wanted to change the policy to increase government spending to stimulate the flagging economy . It has pretty much been the same ever since then . But it could change again if the Democrats and Republicans happen to change their opinions .

Lets start at the beginning , with a star . A star 's size is stable because it has the force of gravity pulling it inwards , and the force of the ' explosion ' of its fusion reactions pushing it outwards . These forces are balanced . Eventually , all the possible fusion reactions run out of fuel and stop , and the star collapses because the fusion reactions do n't support it any more . There 's a lot of detail to this , and possibly several stages , but the main result is that the star can do one of several things . If it 's mass is on the low side , it can be held up solely by the heat of compression of the centre ( analogously , it 's hard to squeeze a stress ball smaller than a certain size because you run out of air gaps to compress it into ) . If it 's mass is high but not high enough to become a black hole , it remains held up by quantum degeneracy pressures - a result of quantum mechanics where it turns out some kinds of particle extremely strongly resist being tightly packed . However , if its mass is high enough to overcome these , then the force of gravity overwhelms everything else . There 's literally nothing stopping it from collapsing to a point ... so it does .

* * What sort of a thing is neoliberalism ? * * Neoliberalism is an ideology : this means that it 's a set of ideas , evidence ( * epistemology * ) and conclusions ( * ontology * ) which produce a set of guidelines for how you should run a country . This means you should compare it to other ideologies : on the similar side , compare with neoconservatism , as well as classical liberalism ; on the opposing side , consider marxism and socialism . You might also want to compare with anarchism and anarcholiberalism , which can be viewed as either similar or radically different depending on your exact stance . * * Next , what does neoliberalism take as evidence and conclusion ? * * Most important is the idea of a * free market * , which is a special sort of idealised market where people can buy and sell things . Central to the idea of a perfectly free market is the idea that it will always * clear * , or allocate all of the things that are for sale , for the best price for both sides . Exactly why is pretty complicated , and looking up " market clearing " and " free market " in an economics primer will explain it in much better detail than I can .

I mean , we do have a recipe that works very well and agrees with experimental data , but my personal impression is that there is much to be unveiled about the " quantum measurement problem " . You see , quantum mechanics does not predict the position of an electron subjected to the double slit experiment . The ingredients of the theory are not those , but something much more subtle and hard to grasp , namely the " distribution of probability of the result of a measurement of the position of the electron " . That is , " position " in the way we all understand it , is * * not * * a property of an electron or a property of its dynamics . Its property ( albeit a quantum property ) is actually the set of probabilities of obtaining a certain place x as the result of a measurement of its position . * That * is well defined for an electron .

When you initially start working for a company , you fill out a form called a W-4 . This form asks you various questions like if you are married , how many children you have , and how many jobs you have . The information on this form is then used to decide how much of your paycheck should go directly to the government . The government generally overestimates the amount of taxes you owe for two reasons . First off , people are much happier receiving a refund in April rather than having to pay the government extra money . Secondly , the money taken out of your paycheck acts as a free loan . The government gets to hold on to your money for months without paying you interest . If you normally get a refund every year , I would recommend talking to your employer 's HR or finance person . Ask them to help you adjust your W-4 exceptions so that you are n't over paying your taxes . They should be able to help you adjust your withholdings so you pay less taxes upfront . This would result in a generally smaller refund or possibly even owing the government extra money come tax time . EDIT : This is specific to the US .

In ancient Greek plays , tragedies often ended with a God descending from heaven ( lowered by a machine , of course ) and bringing closure to the plot . Hence the saying Deus ex Machina ( * or * * God from the machine * ) . It is usually used when someone or something out of the blue brings a storyline to an end which would not have been possible otherwise . Example : In the final matrix movie , Neo makes a pact with one of the machines to kill Agent Smith . Without the help from that machine , this would not have happened and nothing in the film up to that point indicates that such an event was even a possibility . Note that the thing interfering in the plot line does not have to be divine or a machine to be called a Deus ex Machina , it simply needs to bring about an improbable change in the story .

The simplest explanation of transfering data over radio is to treat radio signals as on / off impulses . You send a radio signal at the frequency that the reciever listens to , and switches it on and off at intervals . It would be a bit like Morse code , a certain series of on : s and off : s would mean different things . Let 's say on = 1 and off = 0 , so a series of on : s and off : s could be represented like this : 10001110111001 , 1001101111011 , 0110011110 . Now let 's say we read these 8 at a time , and call that a " Byte " , and call each individual number a " bit " . 00000000 would be interpreted in one way , 00000001 in another , and so on . Some represents letters , some represent numbers , etc . Now that is very basic . There are lot 's of different varieties , and most are more complex . For example , you can use varying levels of signal strengths and assign a representation in series of bits for each one , but that 's rare since background radiation ( radio waves from microwave ovens , stars , etc ) would easily disturb that , like how it can be hard to hear others in a crowd with plenty of people shouting , at variying strength .

To understand the project , we need some background . During Kant 's time European philosophers divided ( very roughly ) into two camps . There were the Rationalists , who believed that the way to learn about the fundamental structure of reality was by reasoning . They thought that determining what kind of reality we are actually in is determinable via a kind of rational insight . Many of these philosophers thought this insight was a kind of faculty given to us by God . Examples of such philosophers include Descartes and Leibniz . On the other hand , there were the Empiricists , who believed that the only way to learn about reality was via the senses . According to them , reason could at best tell us about " analytic " truths i.e. the kinds of truths that are simply guaranteed by the definitions of or terms or the shape of our concepts . For example , you can know via reason alone that " all bachelors are unmarried men " . Why ? Because the concept bachelor just is the concept of an unmarried man . Denying the statement would lead to a contradiction . One of the more famous empiricists , Hume , divided all statements into two types : relations of ideas , and matters of fact .

Money by itself is n't worth anything ( it 's not really worth much even if backed by gold because you ca n't do much with gold either ) , so it 's value depends on what others value money at . So you have to influence how people value money . Even if you keep a dollar 's value " constant " it wo n't be constant , because people use dollars as the other end of an exchange for all sorts of goods . The value of a dollar when used for , say , postal stamps has probably changed much differently than that same dollar exchanged for college education , so there is n't a true " constant " . So we typically compare the dollar 's value to some " standard " basket of goods that we pretty much expect all people to buy in some quantity ( gas , food , utilities , etc . ) ... this is the Consumer Price Index ( or various other forms ... if you compare currencies it is Purchasing Power Parity , as in , how much of these " standard goods " can the Indian Rupee buy compared to the US Dollar ) .

The null hypothesis is the most important one . Science is only legitimate when it tries to * * falsify * * something . Science that affirms is not very legitimate . It 's the science that disproves that is legitimate . Therefore , the best theories arise from multiple attempts at failing to falsify a null hypothesis . Alternate hypotheses should only be formulated after multiple failures to falsify a hypothesis . For example : A famous null hypothesis would be that " natural selection does not account for changing allele frequencies in a population of species . " As thousands of studies and scientific papers show , no one has been able to reject this null hypothesis . It always is falsified . There is no evidence in the history of the theory of natural selection that shows that it does not occur . Therefore , it is will supported . We have not proven that natural selection accounts for genetic change . We have merely never found counter - evidence showing that it does not account for genetic change . We have always failed to falsify the null hypothesis .

* * Overview :* * A deterministic finite automata ( DFA\ * ) is essentially a " program " that reads a string ( an ordered collection of characters , members of an " alphabet " ) . The program maintains a state and keeps track of where in the string it currently is during the reading . The machine defines , for every state , which one state it goes to next for a given character ( this is why it is * deterministic * - it has to specify * exactly * one destination for every combination of state and character ) . The machine either " accepts " or " rejects " a string , depending on what state it 's in when it finishes reading . * * Example :* * So , for instance , let 's say we have an alphabet of just " a " and " b " , and we have a DFA with two states , " s0 " and " s1 " . Let 's define the function as follows : * When the machine is in state " s0 " and reads " a " , stay in " s0 " . * When the machine is in state " s0 " and reads " b " , go to " s1 " . * When the machine is in state " s1 " and reads " a " , stay in " s1 " . * When the machine is in state " s1 " and reads " b " , go to " s0 " .

Finally , particles crash into each other , and ensure that they 're all moving in the same general direction . Because a number ca n't be divided by zero , the only way to make this problem not work is to make " x " = 0 . We can get infinitely * close * to zero , but we ca n't use zero . As we get closer to x=0 , y gets bigger and bigger . Gabriel 's Horn is a 3 - dimensional version of the problem y=1 / x. As x gets smaller and smaller ( approaching zero ) , the length of the " horn " gets bigger and bigger . For instance , if we make x 0.00000000000001 cm , the horn 's corresponding length , " y " , is 1 trillion meters . So , we have a horn whose length approaches infinity as x approaches zero . Now let 's talk about width , " x " . The " bell " of the horn ( the wide - open end ) is n't able to get bigger than 1 , because those are the rules ( the rules have to be set because if x gets bigger than 1 , the whole thing falls apart ) .

One argument I have heard is that marijuana is a poor medication . The main method of taking it is smoking it , in which you burn the plant and all sorts of unknown ( and known ) chemical reactions take place and exactly how much of , and what exactly you are inhaling is not consistent . Even if taken by another less harmful way ( via oils or vaporizing ) there is no way to really control the dose ( or how much ) of the active ingredient ( the chemical doing the work ) you are getting . An analogy is the willow tree , which contains a chemical commonly known as Aspirin . You could take extracts or poultices of willow bark and potentially have the same effect as a aspirin pill , however there is no way to know exactly how much aspirin you are getting or what other chemicals might be present . Modern medicine prefers precision in its medications so that it can try and give you the appropriate amount , this is easiest with a standard amount delivered in a pill , which is available for marijuana in the Marinol pill which I think contains just delta-9 - THC , the main active chemical in marijuana .

Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules in the fluid . When you reduce the temperature , you reduce the amount of energy . Liquid fluids have a molecular structure that allows the movement of particles in a free manor . When you reach the freezing point , the molecules all align into a structure , and are forced into an expanded state . When you have the same amount of matter in a larger area , the density is lowered . Two substances of varying densities experience buoyancy . Buoyancy causes an upward force equal to the weight of the amount of liquid displaced by the solid inside the fluid . To understand steampunk , you must first understand cyberpunk . Cyberpunk is effectively film noir set in an 80s/90s concept of the high - tech near future in a society dominated by large corporations , with strong brand awareness as a recurring theme amid seamy tales of industrial espionage and corporate politics . Steampunk is a derivative of cyberpunk . Instead of an 80s/90s concept of a high - tech near future , it is set in a Victorian - Britain concept of one . Thus instead of neon , black plastic and Japanese kitsch , the aesthetics are dominated by riveted brass instrumentation everywhere , pneumatic tubes , oak paneling , zeppelins and occasionally fanciful ray - guns . The society depicted is typically more Victorian - dominated by the state and military rather than commercial interests , and the protagonists , while roughly fitting the noir genre , tend to be more accidental adventurers and slightly dashing engineers than the cynical , gritty anti - heroes that dominate cyberpunk . Steampunk as an aesthetic rather than literary genre simply consists of a design aesthetic based on a weird mix of art deco , Boy 's Own Paper and early science fiction .

One of the things that made it easier to break German codes was the Germans were big on pro forma messages . For example , there might be a requirement that a German Army platoon leader has to report to his company leader once a day , saying something like " Lieutenant Bob , checking in with Captain Smith , 23 April 1942 " . If you know the exact text ( or at least close enough ) for one message , you try decryption until you get that message , then use that same method on a message you do n't know the contents of and see if it makes sense . This made code breaking a LOT easier for the allies . If you do n't have a known message to compare against , then you basically do have to try things until you get a result that looks like it 's from the target language . If you try three code breakings , and the results are " AFJKJDSF DEFKJSF DFKLJDF " , " YUWERNJKVIH FFHUFNE " , and " ATTACK AT DAWN " , it 's pretty obvious which one is the actual message .

Take a periodic waveform . Just any random shape which connects to itself and repeats over and over again with some frequency . Let 's say it 's a sound wave . The math of * fourier series * says that this sound wave can be represented as the sum of a bunch of sine waves . Sine waves are more or less the simplest possible periodic function ( they sound like [ this ] ( URL_0 ) ) . The frequencies of those sound waves , however , must be a multiple of the basic frequency of the signal you started with- either the same frequency , or twice the frequency , or three times , and so on . If one of them was at a different frequency that was not a multiple , it would spoil the periodic nature of the original signal ! The first sine wave in the series , with the same frequency as the original signal , is called the fundamental . The other sine waves in the series are called the harmonics . So , the fourier series is giving you a way to characterize the shape of a signal- by knowing the strength of the harmonics . Our ears listen to sounds by examining what frequencies are in them .

When you open a computer , you 'll see a lot of little black rectangles . Those are called " chips " , and they are what makes a computer work . They notice when you move the mouse & let you create the pretty pictures mommy pins to the fridge . But how do they work you ask ? Good question . They consist of even smaller parts , called " transistors " , and work like a valve . With just a little bit of work they can regulate a lot of water . But unlike a valve , they usually are either open or closed . And any switch between open and closed takes time , and during that time they resist the flow , and begin to heat up from the energy , like the old valve in the basement makes noise when turning on and off . Now , in a computer these transistors switch between on an off about 800 million times per second . Each switch generates only a little bit of heat , but over time it gets more . In old computers , the transistors were bigger and slower , so there was more time for heat to build up , and they also needed more energy to switch around , which is why they needed coolers , while your new phone does n't .

Essentially , when you think , signals travel through the nerves in your brain . When two nerves connect there is a synapse . Signals are transferred across the synapse by diffusion of neurotransmitter chemicals . After the neurotransmitters diffuse , they have to be moved back into the first half of the synapse , so that they can carry another signal . This happens via a method called active transport , and is the reason for the energy use . EDIT : To clarify , synapses are one - way connections . The signal is carried across by the diffusion of chemicals called neurotransmitters , which are released form the first half of the synapse , and detected in the second half . Once they are detected , these chemicals hang around . To move them back into the first half of the synapse requires energy . EDIT2 Concentration does require far more signals to transfer than simple reflex actions .

The biggest mistake people make regarding irony is to consider that there 's only one kind of irony . For example , when you compare irony with sarcasm , you 're thinking about * verbal * irony : when you say something that means the opposite of its literal meaning . Sarcasm is very often done in the form of verbal irony . But there are many more kinds of irony that have nothing to do with sarcasm . Another example is when white knights will say " that is not irony because irony is this [ insert link to YouTube video ] " , often followed with a reference to Alanis Morissette . Their mistake is that they assume the person is wrong because it does n't match the one definition they know . The person is sometimes rightfully using a different form of irony . So what is irony ? At its core , it deals with an incongruity between two opposite things , but this can take several forms . * Verbal irony is when you say something and mean the opposite : " That did n't hurt at all " while wincing in pain . The irony is in the contrast between literal meaning and real meaning . This is the form of irony defined by [ Bender ] ( URL_1 ) .

If you take the weight of all the adults in a population and put them on a graph you 'll get what looks like a smooth hump which tails off into nothing at the left and the right , and has a big clump in the middle . The BMI is a ratio of weight and height , and if you chart everyone 's BMI you also get this same curve . All the people with the very small BMI are on the left , and very large BMI are on the right . It turns out from hospital records , death certificates and so on that people on either extreme are more likely to be ill . Note this is a statistical measure of a population : it ca n't predict your health any more than you being male and 22 can predict a car crash . But it is still an important guideline , like the connection of smoking and cancer .

It 's about competing interests and competing rights . Schools can not control a student 's speech ( for the most part ) outside of school . But when speech within school disrupts the school 's functionality , there is a competing interest . This is based on reasonableness in reaction to speech . For instance , if you come into a school wearing a shirt that says " I have a bomb strapped to my chest , " yes that is speech , you have n't " done " anything other than put a statement on your shirt . If you do this , you will be promptly arrested , searched by dogs , and the school will be evacuated . If a school could n't place reasonable restrictions on what students wear and say , the school would risk not functioning . There is a balance here , and certainly schools overstep and do lose court cases , but that is the rationale .

* * How accents work :* * Accents come from the vowel . When you speak , the vowel can be shaped in a variety of ways . The ' a ' in ' hay ' is not the same as the ' a ' in ' cat . ' Same letter , different sound . The ' a ' in ' hay ' looks more like ' aaaeee ' because of two different vowel sounds combining . This is called a * * diphthong * * ( pronounced dip - thong , stupid ' h ' messing stuff up)--when two or more vowel sounds are smushed together to represent one sound . Different accents are based on how a vowel is spoken and the amount of diphthong it has . * * How vowels work for singing :* * Singing a vowel is considerably more work than speaking one . Singing the ' a ' in ' hay ' for a minute straight is actually quite straining on the throat . This is bad because people who sing for a living -- from 5 to 10 hours a day -- can get hurt . Hence , singing focuses on the easiest way to get a sound out of the human body without hurting it . The vowels that are used to sing with are called * * pure vowels * * . These vowels are * completely stripped of a diphthong * to allow the throat and tongue to relax and let the sound come out unhindered .

The idea of acupuncture is based on a concept that only exists in Eastern medicine : qi ( also spelled chi ) . Qi is the concept of an invisible " life force " that flows through living things . Those who practice Eastern medicine claim that medical problems are often caused by inbalances in the flow of qi . Stimulating certain points of the body , they say , can correct these inbalances and restore the proper flow of qi . As far as Western / allopathic / conventional medicine is concerned , there is no evidence to suggest that qi exists in the first place . Western medicine agrees that things flow through the body like blood and electric impulses , but nothing matching the description of qi has been observed or demonstrated experimentally . So , how does acupuncture help people ? It helps only with pain relief . In other words , acupuncture ca n't cure a disease , but it can lessen the symptoms . A technique called " sham acupuncture " has been used in experiments , in which some patients are given a acupuncture - like treatment with the needles in incorrect locations . Generally , acupuncture does not give results significantly better than the sham treatment .

One bit that I feel was missed : You know how the top comment mentions XO , Turner Syndrome ? I.e. a woman with only one X chromosome ? This is what happens when something goes wrong while a set of 46 chromosomes is reduced to 23 to create sperm or egg cells ( the process is called meiosis ) , and one of the end products ( a sperm or egg cell ) ends up with a missing chromosome or an extra one ( Down 's , having 3 of chromosome 21 , happens the same way ) . What has n't been mentioned is that it * is * possible for a fertilized egg to have the sex chromosome combination YO ( an Y chromosome from the father and a faulty egg without an X chromosome from the mother ) . However , there are too many vital genes on the X chromosome for this combination to be viable . It dies before you ever realize you were pregnant . Edited to add : In addition to Down 's , trisomy 21 , it is also possible to end up with trisomy 15 or 18 . Having extras of any other chromosome besides these three or X / Y is similarly lethal .

This often means pursuing a trope 's inherent contradictions and the difference between how the trope appears in this one work and how it compares to other relevant tropes or ideas both in fiction and Real Life . > The simplest and most common method of applying Deconstruction to tropes in fiction among general audiences and fan bases , and the method most relevant to TV Tropes , takes the form of questioning " How would this trope play out with Real Life consequences applied to it " .

To be a little more technical , your CPU has millions and millions of tiny operational gates made out of relatively fragile material . Though electrical instead of mechanical , heat and use can change their electrical properties . When non - critical components of the chip fail , the result is slower performance ( You do not want to know the fail rate of computers if every single logic gate had to be operational for the entire thing to work ) This si basically what ' celeron ' chips were . Intel would run initial tests , and anything with to high a failure percentage / slow performance would be downgraded to celeron status , with a reduced speed to prevent heat from causing more failures to fast . When simpler ICs fail ( like a chip with only 8 or so logic gates ) , this is effectively a total failure for the system . When you have millions of gates , only a few are actually critical to the function , the other paths just stop being used , and it takes longer to process all the data and you have a higher error rate , which then the computer has to spend more CPU cycles in correcting .

Who is for the subject , while whom is used for the object . For an example , the question " Who do you love ? " is incorrect because the person you love is the object of your love . You probably are more familiar with how mail and post offices work , so I 'll try explaining it by using that as a parallel . Each ip address is assigned to a certain computer , just like each building or house has its own address . If you sent a letter to a penpal , lets say their address is 255 Reddit Ave , Minneapolis MN , your post office would look at the letter , see that it should be sent to Minneapolis , and send it there . For computers , instead of letters , they use packets , but it 's basically just a chunk of info it 's sending to another computer . It uses the IP address to find that computer . Subnets are similar to office buildings , where the letter would get to the building by the post office , but a smaller " post office " in the building will actually figure out which cubicle to deliver the letter to once it gets inside the building . Old Joe Postman does n't know or really care what happens to the letter after he drops it off at the front desk , but lets the people who work in the building figure out how to get it to the right person . Network routing is just the process of deciding where to send it , based on the address .

it 's actually an interesting concept ( well , if you 're a computer science kid ) . 32 or 64 bit stands for the relative size of the registers and possibly other components in the computer . Basically , when the computer is doing operations and stuff , it needs to remember where things are , so it has a little address system to write things down . This is so it can use the RAM , or random access memory , to remember lots of things . the RAM is composed of lines of space that can hold numbers , and each one needs an address . It needs to be able to fit these addresses in the Registers , which are used to do the most basic of calculations in a computer . But the registers are only so big , so it limits the size the addresses can be . A 32 bit machine is designed around a 32 bit architecture , meaning the largest number a register could hold would be 4,294,967,295 . That 's actually not that big nowadays , and meant that at around 3 - 4 gigabytes of RAM , you actually ran out of addresses . The computer could n't figure out how to use all the ram , because it did n't have enough addresses for it .

In the specific example you cite , we are fortunate enough to have use of the Rosetta stone which has the same passage in Hyrogliphics , Demotic Egyptian Script and Ancient Greek . Since we know what Demotic Egyptian sounds like , we can do pretty well with figuring out what Ancient Egyptian sounds like . Also , Languages do n't exist in a vacuum . For Ancient Egyptian , the modern derivative language would be Coptic , primarily used as the liturgical language of Egyptian & Sudanese Christians . Last , through our experience studying language , we have developed a number of linguistic shortcuts that help us map out how sounds change across language and time . For example , in Semitic languages , we find that the " sh " sound and the " 's " sound are frequently interchangeable . This gives us short hand rules for reconstructing the sounds of dead languages .

Let 's say you 're in kindergarten and you draw a picture of a purple bunny rabbit . The bunny rabbit is popular , so you can sell copies of your drawing . Obviously , if Timmy down the street were to copy your drawing , he could sell it instead of you , and you 'd lose money . Based on this , you think copyright is a good thing . But what if Johnny has a good idea for a story about how your bunny fights dinosaurs ? Under copyright , he ca n't sell ( or even give away ) that story . Maybe it was a really good story and people would have loved it . Too bad for Johnny . It 's your drawing and you are n't letting people tell stories about it ( unless they pay you off ) . Well , years come and go , and eventually you die . And your spouse dies . And so do all of your children . Now Jimmy comes along and sees your painting . He wants to write a story about the bunny fighting aliens . Should he be prevented from doing so because he 's not the one that drew the picture 100 years ago ? The basic idea is that while only one person can use a physical object at a time , anyone can use intellectual property at the same time .

Despite what some people think , the earth would not " explode " . The crust of out plant is astonishingly thin , covering a fluid like mantle and outer core . A big asteroid hitting the earth would be like dropping a bowling ball into a small pool . The surface would splatter off at the point of impact , and massive fluid like shockwaves would reverberate all around the globe . This is of course , in tandem with the planet engulfing firestorm that would scorch the earths surface clean from the point of impact . A MOON sized object hitting the earth would be like dropping a bowling ball into a barrel of water . Gargantuan amounts of planetary material would be ejected out into space ( possibly coelescing into another moon , in time ) The earth would literally melt into a somewhat less circular shape as it absorbed most of the intruder into itself over thousands of years . Eventually , the crust would resolidify , although the chances of life reforming in any significant quantity before our sun goes dark is pretty low . What you would need to worry about , is the chances that such an impact could knock the earth out of it 's current orbital path .

Here 's another way to think about it : Imagine you are looking down from above at a man , who is standing at the center of a circle . Now imagine he is holding at arm 's length a stick that is one meter long , and he 's holding it so it is sideways . Looking down from above , trace a line from each end of the stick to the center of the circle , where he is standing — these lines define a wedge in the circle . We can ask " how much of the circle does that wedge occupy ? " and measure that in degrees . In this example , let 's say it 's about 80 degrees . Then we could say that a one meter stick , _ at that distance from his eye _ , covers an arc of 80 degrees . Now move the stick farther away — say all the way down a football field , and trace the lines again to make a new wedge . This is a much narrower wedge , because it is so far away , even though the stick is the same size . Maybe now the stick only covers an arc of 1 or 2 degrees .

If last year you went to the store , did your normal shopping , and then went home , then during that event you did n't interact with a future - self . Now , a year later , you go back in time and go to that store where you see yourself shopping . If you walk up and start talking to yourself , you have now explicitly changed an event in the past . There are two primary ways used to deal with this . the first is that the universe simply ca n't withstand a paradox such as this , where there are two different sets of events that happen at the same time and place , but has no mechanism to prevent it so any such interaction destroys the universe . The other is to assume that when you do this you split off into a " parallel universe " where the interaction * did * happen . Unfortunately , this raises questions of whether your memory changes , which universe is " real " , what you do about being in the wrong time in the wrong universe , whether any actions you take after that point really matter to the universe from which you came , and so on , and this gives writers a headache . In either case , the story dictates that the time - traveler be instructed not to interact with herself .

In this respect itching is analogous to tickling , which is thought to be related to the * * sense of pressure * * . There are numerous " itch points " scattered about the surface of the body where it 's possible to induce itching simply by touching with a fine metal wire . Other areas on the skin usually are relatively insensitive . Itch points appear to be associated with concentrations of fine free nerve endings . It 's known that in some cases the nervous system has different mechanisms for conducting sensory impressions of varying intensity , such as light and firm pressure , and there is speculation that * * itching may be a watered - down sense of pain * * , designed to detect extremely faint stimuli . Thus if you have dry skin or a stretched hair follicle or some minor localized chemical imbalance , the nerves may multiply it into the sharp irritation that you instinctively scratch .

Both are means for your computer to find its way on the Internet . When your computer starts up , it wants to connect to a computer network , usually the Internet but sometimes a corporate network . The reason it wants to connect is so that you can check your mailbox and surf the web . In order to be able to connect to a network , your computer needs a unique address assigned to it . Compare this to sending a Valentine card through the postal system to your sweetheart . The postal system requires you to write the address of your sweetheart on the envelope . In much the same way , every computer that wants to use a computer network needs an address . For the postal system , an address is a street name , house number , city , state and zip code . For a computer network , an address is a number , called the IP address ( IP is short for Internet Protocol ) . Now , back to your question . When your computer starts up and connects to the network , it needs an IP address . There are several ways of getting one . The most simple one is that your computer already knows what its IP address is ( stored somewhere in a local configuration file ) and it simply uses that .

bases are just the same way of counting numbers , but with less digits . Base 2 you only get 2 numbers , 0 and 1 ( in base ten we get 10 numbers , 0 thru 9 ) . when your number ends in 9 in base 10 ( like with the number 9 ) , and you want one more , you have to add 1 to the decimal place after it and change the original one back to 0 , so the number becomes ten . in base 2 , when the number ends in 1 and you want one more ( like for the number 1 ) , you need to do the same thing , so it becomes 10 , but not ten . it becomes a 1 and then a 0 , and that 's very important . Saliva flow normally decreases when we sleep . In general , dry mouth ( or xerostomia , for you precocious 5 year olds ) is not good for your teeth or the soft tissues ( tongue , gums , throat ) of your mouth , but if it only happens overnight , it should n't be a problem . Your mouth tastes gross because saliva is not flushing food and bacteria out of your mouth , and into your stomach . To reduce the bad breath , and potential harm to your teeth , make sure you brush ( flossing is good also ) your teeth after you eat ( or drink , except for water ) the last food for the night . Food on your teeth with less saliva causes decay ( cavities ) to happen faster . Other factors : your mouth may be drier in winter because the moisture in heated air is lower ; and you could try drinking more water while awake .

Time and space are fundamentally mixed up in our world . In particular , there is no such thing as * simultaneous * events far from one another . If you are in Topeka and your buddy is in New York , you might talk on the phone or something and arrange to jump up and down at the same instant -- but a scientist zooming by in a rocket and observing you both might see you jump first -- while a scientist zooming by in a different rocket in the opposite direction might see your buddy in New York jump first . That effect happens * even after * both scientists account for the finite speed of light . The speed of light forms a barrier both for rapid travel and for that slippage of simultaneity -- if you and your buddy are ( say ) 1 light - second apart , no scientist would be able to see your jumps as separated by more than 1 second of time , no matter how fast he was zooming by .

Waves happen when you have a value that varies over a certain object . Also , the value of a piece of the object depends on what its neighbors used to be . Let 's use a specific example - a slinky held by one end . What determines where each ring of the slinky is ? It depends on where the last and next ring * used * to be . This sort of thing means that if you push the end of the slinky around , you 'll see the rest of the slinky move around in a delayed manner . Ocean waves work the same way - if you make a tall pile of water , the height of water next to it will go up a bit later . It 's a kind of abstract concept , but it 's useful for applying a certain kind of math ( differential equations ) to model many different things .

The Earth 's water surface area is approximately 361,132,000 km2 , which is 3.89 × 10 ^ 15 square feet . That means the top one foot of global sea level contains approximately 3.89 x 10 ^ 15 cubic feet of water . So , approximately that many cubic feet worth of animals would have to be removed to lower the sea level by one foot . I 'm not sure it 's possible to estimate the total volume of all living creatures in the oceans , but it 's safe to say it 's nowhere near 3.89 x 10 ^ 15 cubic feet . To put it in context , the volume of an average human is about 2 cubic feet . Which means it would take about 1.95 x 10 ^ 15 humans to displace sea level by one foot . That 's about 285,000 times the Earth 's current total human population .

Taste buds work by reacting to different chemicals in our food . Salt receptors turn on when they come into contact with salt , sweet receptors for sugar , etc . We do n't have any taste specific receptors for water . That being said , if we did , they would n't be of much use . The way our senses are perceived in our brains means that it 's not necessarily the stimuli themselves that are noticed but rather the changes in their levels . The oft - used example is that you do n't feel the temperature of the room you are in ( if it is comfortable ) until it changes . Since our mouths typically already have lots of water in them ( saliva ) tasting water would n't be all that useful . That being said , we do taste things that are dissolved in water , and we do have receptors in our brains that tell us to be thirsty and drink water , so we can still get satisfaction out of drinking water , it 's just not related to it 's taste .

Energy is an abstract concept , so lets assume it 's toy cars . Timmy has 10 toy cars in his toy box . He plays with them and you leave the room . When you return there are only 6 cars left . It turns out one car is under the bed , other is in a drawer , and one in Timmys pocket . There is one missing , so you search and look for it and eventually you find it thrown out the window . All cars , however Timmy has played with them , are accounted for . If you one day find out that Timmy has 11 cars , then it will turn out an aunt gave him one , or if he is a bad boy - he stole it . However you 'll never find Timmy having car that just appeared out of thin air . That is conservation of energy . You can only get as much out of things as you put in . Some energy is always lost due to various reasons , like friction , or thermal radiation , but if we look for these loses , we find them outside the window , or under the bed . You can never get more energy , unless there is outside influence of an aunt .

torrent speeds fluctuate because of the finickyness of peers . If one of your peers starts downloading something full - speed , he only gets a certain bandwidth . Currency has to have certain attributes * Durable * Uncommon * Practical * Accepted Now why is gold especially suited for this ? Durable : Gold does does not chemically react with a lot of other stuff . Iron rusts , gold does not . It does n't ( or at least back then did n't ) have many uses besides jewelery . Imagine someone proposed blocks of bread as currency . It would mold or people would eat it . Uncommon : Gold was , and still is , not too commonly found and obtaining it can be ardous . If our ancestors had used twigs or pieces of rock , everybody would be rich ( theoretically ) so nobody would sell their goods for a worthless currency . Practical : Gold can be stamped into coins and is therefore easy to carry . Imagine a currency of big , intricately carved stone wheels . They would be durable and not too common but impractical to use . Accepted : Gold can be found all over the world . Since it contains the 3 attributes above , many cultures used it as currency and made cross - cultural trading possible . A Roman trader would 've gladly accept Greek gold coins .

Defining Existentialism as movement or school of thought is somewhat problematic from the very outset . Most philosophers casually known to be Existentialists in fact either rejected the label , or were co - opted into the movement posthumously . Upon analyzing their works we can see why many would reject being lumped together : their differences almost outweigh their similarities . Kierkegaard , the purposed " father " of existentialism , was arguing for faith in God , Nietzsche is an anti - theist if there ever was one , Heidegger was a Nazi , and Sartre was a Marxist . What seems to be crucial in all their philosophies , however , is the emphasis on human subjectivity , real human existence on a fundamental level , and a disdain for the lofty , overarching metaphysical abstractions that philosophy is known for . The existential movement hangs on Sartre . He is responsible for popularizing it and is , along with De ‘ Beauvoir , one of the few who took the label upon himself . All the other existentialists are recognized as so through their relation to him . The sort of existentialism that Sartre advocates can be summarized in the famous maxim " existence precedes essence " .

The Constitution . Article 1 of the US constitution outlines voting rights for Congress . Among other things , it says that only states are represented in the House of Representatives and the Senate . The District of Columbia is not a state ... ergo it does not get to vote in Congress . Under Congressional rules ( not the constitution ) , DC gets a non - voting " delegate " ( NOT a Senator or Representative ) who can vote in committee and participate in floor debate , but who can not vote on any legislation . Article 1 also permitted the establishment of a district * ceded * by state(s ) to be the seat of government , i.e. the capital city . Virginia & Maryland ceded the land that became the District of Columbia . This put the land under the control of Congress . The portion ceded by Virginia ( mostly Arlington & Alexandria , VA ) was returned to that state in 1846 . In other words , all of present - day DC was donated by Maryland . The really simple summary is that they take a fixed - size chunk of input at a time , and do a fixed set of bitwise operations on them , which will give you a different chunk of output afterwards . What output you get depends on what the key is . The operations that are done are relatively simpe , and they 're reversible if ( and only if ) you have the same key . Because a single application of the bitwise operations does n't mash the bits up unpredictably enough , we have to apply it many times - the input of the next being the output of the last . The individual operations in each round do n't need to be reversible , due to the way the ciphers are built . In each round , you have a left half of the block you 're working on , and a right half . You apply whatever transform you 're doing to the right half and XOR it with the left half , then you swap the halves over for the next round . Because XOR is reversible , and you have the other half , you can always work it backwards . If you want to encrypt something bigger than one block , then there are methods for doing this called " modes of operation " , which I 'll explain , if anyone I have n't bored to death asks .

While brushing ones teeth is excellent for the health of the teeth and surrounding gums , and certainly makes the mouth feel fresh , there are other considerations when it comes to morning breath . While lots of people brush their teeth , significantly fewer brush their tongue . Not much goes through the mouth and into the stomach without the tongue being a part of the process , so it picks up all kinds of microscopic bits and pieces of things over the day . The tongue is covered in small bumps , and things get trapped between them . Without brushing the tongue , and removing those bits , those specks basically get to incubate smells throughout your sleeping hours with the help of the warm , dark , moist environment the mouth provides . While brushing the tongue does n't eliminate all morning breath ( the mouth is n't going to stop being warm , dark , and moist unless you have a much more serious condition ) , it does drastically reduce what the mouth is able to incubate overnight .

Language is a form of communication , but not all communication is language . Language is a very specific type of communication that explicitely expresses thoughts , emotions , ideas , etc ... that is structured with a set of rules such as grammar and syntax . Communication is much more broad . A groan , a grunt , a scream , and crying are all forms of communication , but they never explicitely state the problem . Animals can communicate among themselves , as well as among other animals , but they do not have language because they do not have structured words , gestures , or symbols that represent very specific thoughts .

Every sound is a wave in a medium . That means , sounds are vibrations in the air . Like a wave in your pool . Also , a peak and a trough ( the dip ) , if they collide , they sort of cancel out . Astrophysics -- figuring out how things as big as planets , moons , and stars move -- is pretty much only based on gravity . So the basic problem is : if we have a bunch of big objects and they all have mass and so they all attract each other , and we know where they are and how fast they 're moving ( and in what direction ) , how do we figure out where they are going to be at any point in the future ? This is called the " n - body problem " . For very simple problems we can solve this exactly . For example , if the sun was concentrated into one tiny point ( but still weighed the same ) and the earth was another tiny point and the earth was the only planet , the earth would go around the sun repeating a kind of lopsided circle called an ellipse . But of course it is not that simple . We have two possible options . First , we can pretend that things really are simple , because it turns out the motion is very close anyway . That 's what we do most of the time , but it 's not quite accurate enough for aiming space probes and stuff .

If you grab your keyboard or guitar and pluck out out G major , C major and D major , you 're playing a really common chord progression . Now , we can explain a chord progression just by saying ‘ It goes , G major , E minor , C major , D major ’ , which is great , but not very useful when we 're talking in more general terms . What if I wanted the same musical effect , but with A major as the first chord ? I 'd need to say ‘ It goes A major , F # minor , D major and then E major ’ ( we 've moved the whole chord progression up a tone here ) . That would be pretty long winded . What we need is a way to explain the relationship between the chords no matter which chord we 're starting on . To do that , we use roman numerals . The form factor of the material matters as well - for instance , a huge cube of zinc would n't burn , but powdered zinc would burn .

The OSI model is just like everything else in computing - it 's built up in layers , on top of foundations that had already been laid . Let 's start at the bottom , and work our way up to the top . At the very bottom is the physical layer - all it takes responsibility for is sending bits onto whatever medium carries the data . That could be wires , or fibre optic , or radio , or shouting in to a tin can . When it receives data it passes it up to the layer above it to make sense of it . It knows how to take control of the medium it 's using , how to send data , how to tell everyone it has stopped sending data , and how to deal with problems such as someone else already sending data . It has no idea what the data is , though . As a comparison , this is " talking on the phone " . The next layer up is the Data link layer - This layer adds some basic detection of whether th edata got to the other end intact , and how to break it down into manageable chunks that can be reassembled at the other end . Comparing it to a phone call , this defines words , and knowing to speak again if the line is bad . The next layer above that is the network layer .

The search results will be in so - and - so format .

Your nervous system normally tries to keep a balance between being too revved - up and being too relaxed . There are different systems with different chemicals ( hormones , neurotransmitters etc ) in your body that accomplish these goals . When you need to run away from a dangerous situation , you activate your Sympathetic System , also known as " fight or flight " . When you want to relax in a hammock and take a nap in the sun , you activate your Parasympathetic System , also known as " rest and digest " . Getting an erection depends on the chemicals of the Parasympathetic , not the Sympathetic System . You do n't need a boner to run away from a lion , no matter how hilarious it might sound . However , if you 're in " rest and digest " mode ( like when you 're sleeping ) , you have a predominance of Parasympathetic hormones and neurotransmitters , and therefore you 're pretty likely to get an erection .

IQ tests test the " classical " intelligence : logical thinking and reasoning , and verbal skills . These are used because they are considered the more practical types of intelligence , intelligence being the ability to perceive patterns and apply them to different situations for optimum results . So an IQ test will , most of the time , tell you that yes , someone is intelligent in a general sense . However , IQ tests can not measure other relevant things . For instance , how is it possible that Albert Einstein had a measure IQ of around 164 ( high genius level ) but was widely respected by his peers , some of which had much higher IQs of 180 + ( profoundly genius levels ) , such as Wolfgang Pauli , Werner Heisenberg and Neils Bohr ? Because Einsten was incredibly creative and had a keen , profound intuition , things which can not be measured in IQ tests . Let 's go further and compare Einstein to another genius : Michael Jordan . Who knows more physics , Einstein or Jordan ? They are both capable of correctly interpreting the strength , speed and angle necessary for a ball to be thrown into a hoop , but through completely different means .

This analogy is n't perfect , but imagine that you are swinging a yo - yo like a pendulum . You start by holding the yo - yo string , yo - yo hanging down , perfectly still . Then you move the yo - yo to set it in motion , keeping the top of the string still . Unless you set it in motion very carefully , it will not swing around in a perfect circle . Because of the imperfections in the process of setting it in motion , it will swing around in a squashed round shape , like an ellipse . In the Solar System , the top of the string , the point that the yo - yo swings around , is the Sun . No matter how you swing the planets , as long as you do n't swing them too hard so that they just fly off into space , they will stay orbiting the sun . To get them to orbit in a perfect circle would require a perfect starting motion , which is impossible in the real world .

It has to do with two things : first , the temperature of the star , and second , our ability to see very faint things . So first , temperature . Very hot stars are bright and bluish - white , while cooler stars are dim and red . You can look at this in another example by looking at a candle . The further the flame is from the wick , the cooler it is . Very close to the wick , it is white ( or even blue , if it is hot enough ) . Further away , it is orange or red . The majority of stars are these cooler , dim , red stars . There are fewer and fewer stars as we get hotter and hotter . Second , our ability to see things . Most stars , with some exceptions like Sirius , appear white , as you 've said . But simply by numbers , dim , reddish stars outnumber white stars by far . So is there something in the atmosphere or some angular thing or whatever going on to make all the stars look white ? Nope . Remember that we have two different kind of cells in our retinas which detect light . Cone cells , which detect colored light , are actually not that sensitive . Rod cells , on the other hand , are sensitive to just light , but are much more sensitive in general .

Your eyes are only the very first step in what we call vision . For example , the image that hits the back of your eyes is flipped upside - down by the lenses that focus it . It gets corrected somewhere in the brain as a part of visual processing . The signals that your eyes send back to the brain are processed by a diverse array of what we 'll call " Vision Centers . " These chunks of your brain , among other duties , process these signals from your eyes and send the results " upstream " to other chunks . Some signals loop back and form circuits . It gets complicated here . Hallucinations and many optical illusions happen because this complicated process is under so many influences at any one time , and it has to make so many decisions with incomplete data , that the results it can produce , aka The Experience of Seeing a Thing , can be completely scrambled under the right circumstances . This is where Unicorns and little green Fairies come in .

Imagine there 's a pasture full of grass that 's not owned by a private individual . Farmers from around the area bring their cattle to this pasture to graze for free . The act of grazing slowly destroys the pasture . All farmers realize that if the pasture gets over - grazed that all of the grass will die and the pasture will be of no benefit to anyone . If one farmer takes his cattle away from the pasture to let the grass regrow , another farmer will just take his place and the pasture will get destroyed anyway . So what happens is that none of the farmers remove their cattle because the destruction of the pasture is seen as inevitable . One proposed solution to this problem is to allow private ownership of the land . The private owner can charge a small fee to each farmer who comes to the pasture . When the pasture needs to recover , the private owner will only let a few ( or no ) farmers in , because if the pasture is destroyed then the private owner wo n't be able to make money off of it anymore .

You can measure the gravity of a planet , a star , or a galaxy by how fast things fall into it . And that lets you work out how heavy they are . Well , when cosmologists looked at other galaxies and tried to work out how heavy they were , the numbers did n't add up . They had about four or five times more gravity than you would expect from the number of stars they had . So there must be something we ca n't see that accounts for the missing weight . Until we work out what it is exactly , we 're calling it " dark matter " . ( It 's also possible that the numbers do n't add up because gravity does n't work the way we think it does - that 's a different theory called [ Modified Newtonian Dynamics ] ( URL_0 ) ) Another thing cosmologists noticed looking at galaxies ( especially ones that are very , very far away ) is that they 're accelerating . Every galaxy in the universe is being pushed away from every other one , at a rate proportional to the distance between them . We do n't know of anything that could create such a force , but whatever it is it must have a lot of energy . Until we work out what it is exactly , we 're calling it " dark energy " .

It literally means what it says on the tin : the company is buying back the shares from their shareholders . Usually , they 'll buy it back at a price that is significantly higher than the current share price so that investors would be willing to sell . Usually , companies will buy back as many shares as they can up to a certain value ( in this case , $ 10 m ) . By doing the maths , theoretically , this would raise the overall value of each share ( not the total value of the company ) . By reducing the number of shares , this would strengthen the value of each share and make them more valuable ( since there are less of them to go around ) . It is also another way to raise the value of the share if the company feels that it is too low . Although , note that the value of a share is extremely subjective , and is really up to market forces ( and thus , people ) to decide how much a share is really worth . Reducing the number of shares also increases the dividend investors receive . While a few cents increase per share does n't seem like much , when you consider that people usually own at least a few thousand at any one time , the zeros start to add up .

The size of the eye does have a bearing on its function . I was just listening to a [ radio show ] ( URL_0 ) about squid eyes this weekend ( if you want to listen , go down to " Here 's Looking at you , Squid " and choose the streaming version or download the mp3 ) . Larger eyes improve an animal 's ability to see in the dark , up to a point . Once the eye is larger than an orange , there is no additional benefit to having a bigger eye in terms of accuracy of vision . Because of this , scientists were initially confused about why giant squid have such huge eyes ... but they figured out that even though the big eyes do n't help them see more accurately , they do help them spot very large objects ( like sperm whales trying to eat them ) in very dim lighting conditions . TL;DR : Hawks just have to see very well in the day , but bears often roam around at night or hibernate in dark caves , so they have to be able to see large objects in dark areas , requiring bigger eyes to let in more light .

A little history . When Pluto was first discovered , it was at limits of what we could see . Our best guess is that it was pretty big , like earth sized . Clearly something earth sized is a planet . As our telescopes got bigger , Pluto got smaller , Mars sized , then Mercury sized . Finally , in the ' 70s , we discovered the big smudge we thought was Pluto was actually two smaller smudges , Pluto , and its moon , Charon . That made it way smaller than even Mercury . So in the span of 40 years , Pluto went from looking like it was Earth sized to being something closer to asteroid sized . There was talk about whether it should still be a planet , but in the 00s , when other Pluto sized things were discovered ... Eris , Quouar , Sedna ... some of which could be even bigger than Pluto , things came to a head . It was clear Pluto was one of many trans - Neptunian objects , and these objects were different than the other 8 planets . So astronomers were faced with a choice ... keep Pluto as a planet , and accept that eventually there will be dozens of planets , or reclassify Pluto and the newly discovered objects into a category that makes more sense .

Much of the research on sleep involves EEGs , or Electroencephalography , which involves recording electrical activity on one 's head . Other electrodes can also be used to monitor other aspects of the body , such as heart rate , respiration , or skin conductance during sleep . We can physiologically characterize sleep based on different waveforms going on in the brain . When we are * * Awake * * , EEGs show two different patterns of activity , which we can call A activity and B activity ( short for alpha and beta ) . A activity shows up as medium - frequency waves , and occurs when we are at rest ( but awake ) , sort of just hanging out not really doing anything . B activity consists of irregular , low amplitude waves , and shows up when we are alert and attentive to things in our environment , or thinking actively . Now when we go to sleep , we start to get drowsy and enter * * Stage 1 sleep * * , characterized by T activity ( theta ) , which is really a transition from sleep to wakefulness . Close one eye , hold your arm out in fornt of you and use your thumb to cover something in the distance . Now , close your open eye and open the closed one . You 'll see that your thumb does n't cover the thing in the distance anymore , becuase where you 're looking from - your open eye - has moved and they 're not in line anymore . This is called parallax . The angle we have to look to see how far something has moved depends on how far away the thing is . The way we know how far away things are in space is by using parallax . We look at something and make a note of exactly what angle we need to use to see it , and then 6 months later when the Earth is on the other side of the Sun , we look at it again and see how much that angle has changed . If we divide 1 degree into 60 parts , like we divide an hour in to minutes , we can also call those minutes of degree . Just like dividing minutes of time in to seconds we also divide minutes of degree into seconds . Using the technique of checking the angle to an object and then seeing how the angle changes 6 months later , we know that for every second of angle is a known distance , because of how far we are from the Sun .

The important thing here is to not think about a dimension as if its some Star - Trek - type place you can go where Spock has a beard . A dimension is a degree of freedom , which is a fancy way of saying the ability to move in a direction . An easy way to think of it is how many pieces of information do you need to find something . To find something on the earth you need it 's : * Longitude * Latitude * Altitude So , three dimensions . But , we can also use time as a dimension . If I want to find something I need to know WHEN it was there . No sense showing up late . So we can add a 4th number , time . All we 're saying is that there 's a fourth piece of information that is required to locate something in spacetime . Nothing fancy about that . Nothing can ' exist ' or ' not exist ' in 4 dimensions . Something * has * four dimensions or , rather , we need to use 4 pieces of information to locate it . If I want to find the location of Paris , I only need two dimensions ( Longitude and Latitude ) . That 's because we can describe a globe as a 2 - dimensional object .

In your ear you have thousands of tiny hairs along a seashell shaped cochlea . The cochlea is shaped so different frequencies trigger the tiny hairs at different places allowing you to hear everything from deep sounds to high pitched sounds . When you hear a sound the hairs bend over and send a signal to your brain . When you hear a very loud sound , the hairs break and become permenantly on , sending a false signal to your brain telling you that you are hearing this sound . This is called tinitus or ringing in your ear . You can have temporary tinitus like after a concert where the hairs do recover slowly , or permenant damage where they wo n't . TL;DR : Tiny hairs in your ear pick up different frequencies , loud sound breaks them and permenantly sends a false signal to your brain . Source : uni engineering acoustics paper Edit : If you do have this , you should cut down on loud sounds and wear hearing protection . Hearing loss ca n't be repaired .

The 7 gears on the right move the chain on the cogs that are attached to the back wheel . The 3 gears on the left move the chain on the cogs that are attached to the pedals . If you turn the bike upside down , hold the pedal with your hand and start turning it , then twist the handlebar grip to change gear , you 'll see the chain move from one cog to another . It 's not a good idea to have the chain move too far diagonally between the pedals and the back wheel . In other words , if the pedal gear is on 1 ( the smallest cog ) then you 'll want to keep the back gear no higher than , say , 4 . This keeps the chain on the gears closest to the wheel . In the same way , if the chain is on the largest cog at the pedals , you want it to be on the smaller cogs at the back wheel , say anywhere from 3 to 7 . If the pedal cog is in the middle you might be able to use all 7 back gears , or you might be limited to using gears 2 - 6 . You will need to experiment with your bike to see how the chain moves and where it looks " comfortable " . As for actual riding , you want to start in a low gear and then move up to a higher gear as you get faster .

So , consider a planet in orbit . It 's got some energy from the fact that it 's moving around , call that K. It 's got some potential energy from being in a gravitational field , let 's call that one G. So then the total energy T = K + G. This total ca n't change , because the planet and star are n't losing energy . So if one increases , the other has to decrease . Now imagine that it 's in a perfectly circular orbit . This means both the energies , K and G , are fixed - because the speed and the distance from the star are constant . Give the planet a push . Now it 's moving faster , so it 'll move away from the star . But that means it has to increase it 's gravitational energy ( G goes up ) . The increase has to come from the kinetic energy , which means the planet slows down ( K goes down ) . Slowing down means it 's going to fall back closer to the star . Moving closer to the star means it 's decreasing in gravitational potential energy ( G goes back down ) - energy that gets converted into kinetic energy ( K goes back up ) . This means the planet speeds up , and the whole cycle begins over again .

things that are far away look smaller than things that are closer . If you put them next to each other the moon would be a little dot next to the sun . But if you move the moon nice and close and the sun really far away you can make them look about the same size . The technical term is * forced perspective * and it is used a lot in trick photography or movie effects ( like in the Lord of the rings , Gandalf stands close to the camera and all the hobbits stand far away ... it makes Gandalf look really big compared to them because your brain things they are next to each other ) Interestingly , this is closely related to the * moon illusion * where the moon seems huge on the horizon compared to when it is over head . Because of our experience with clouds , our brain thinks that " over head " is really close compared to " at the horizon " , the brain thinks this because overhead clouds look really big compared to clouds at the horizon ... the brain works out that the clouds are not changing size but changing distance and for clouds this is true , over head is just a couple of miles where on the horizon can be 100 miles or more .

Your body does various things to allow you to remain alive and move around . When it does these things , it produces heat . The heat leaves your body mostly through your skin 's contact with the air . If you did n't lose any heat , your body temperature would continue to rise until you overheated . The hotter it is around you , the slower you lose heat . So when it 's too hot , your body does n't lose heat fast enough , so you 're in danger of overheating . When it 's 98 degrees , your body temperature is actually higher than 98 ( I think ) , and wants to lose heat to get down to 98 . This is similar to the reason why water feels colder than air at the same temperature . Water is better at absorbing heat , so it takes heat from your body faster .

To understand this , it would be helpful to take a step back and understand that computers , instead of counting to ten ( 1 , 2 , 3 ... 8 , 9 , 10 ) like we do , only count to two , or more specifically , ZERO and ONE . Either OFF or ON . Each ZERO or each ONE is called a BIT . It 's essentially the building blocks of the computer world . When a bit is ZERO , it 's OFF . When a bit is ONE , it is ON , and that tells the computer what to do when there 's a string of OFFs and ONs in a certain pattern . Most computers can only count 32 of those BITS at one time . This is what a 32 bit string looks like : 0110 1001 1010 1100 1100 1001 0110 1001 There are 32 numbers in that line above . Some are ON , some are OFF . Remember above when I said that an ON is equal to 1 , and an OFF is equal to 0 ? When people write out a binary number , they usually put in a space every 4 bits , just like when you count normally and add a comma every three digits to make it easier to read . Now to understand how we get to that very large number , you need to understand how to " count " in binary .

There are a lot of different ways to describe this , and I 'll take a shot at it . Your stereo at -80db is telling you that it can go 80db louder . When you get to 0db , you 've maxed out the volume - and depending on the quality and configuration of your system , you are either rocking out or your speakers are smoking and about to catch on fire . But anyways , 0db is also called " unity gain " which is the point where the volume of your input equals the volume of your output . Not your output to the speakers , but the output of sound to the amplifier circuit inside your stereo * after * the volume control . If your amplifier amplifies any input by 80db , you want to reduce the input to make the volume quieter . Hence , when it is silent , you are at -80db . The reason all of this is necessary in the first place is because amplifiers are just fancy transformers that boost voltage at a constant ratio - with some capacitors to help smooth the demand for voltage when a sudden loud sound is fed into ( and out of ) the circuit . You need an attenuator ( volume control knob ) to lower the signal strength to the amplifier in order to lower the amplifier output to the speakers .

Think of it like this : you 've probably heard that particles are waves and waves are particles , right ? This is most obvious with photons , they can be treated as small particles when they have high energy ( like x rays ) or like long waves when they have low energy ( like radio waves ) . However nothing fundamental changes about the photon , it 's neither a particle nor a wave ( it 's probably something else we do n't understand ... yet ) . Anyways matter ( atoms ) does the same thing , only it 's a lot more " heavy " so most of the time we treat it as a particle and not as a wave . This is where things get interesting : when you cool down matter ( take away energy ) , just like a photon when it has less energy , it spreads out . If you get a bunch of atoms and you make them all really cold , their wave functions overlap , which means that they are indistinguishable from one another , and presto , Bose Einstein Condensate ( BEC ) . You can think about it as if millions of atoms ( most BECs have around 10 ^ 6 - 10 ^ 7 atoms in them ) are all behaving as if they were one giant atom .
