The filibuster has its roots in Ancient Rome : There was an occasion where Julius Caesar was at the head of an army , wanted to run for office , and simultaneously entitled a triumphal procession for his recent military victories . According to Roman law , Caesar was forbidden from entering the city until the triumphal procession actually happened , but he also needed to appear in - person if he was to file his candidacy for political office . Caesar asked the Senate if he could be given an exception . The Senate was supposed to vote on it , but one of the Senators , Cato the Younger , took to the floor and began to speak . And speak . And speak . The vote could not happen until Cato was done , but the vote needed to be taken before sundown , and Cato was planning to speak until sundown , preventing the vote altogether . The filibuster in modern terms pretty much means the same thing : * A US Senator is entitled to speak on any subject he desires for as long as he desires in order to prevent a particular bill / piece of legislation from being voted upon .

It 's worth also noting how [ heat pipes ] ( URL_2 ) work to carry the heat away from the small surface of the CPU and deliver it to the huge surface of the cooling fins . If you look at a [ cross - section of a heat pipe ] ( URL_3 ) you can see that it is hollow in the middle , and has a porous material on the inner surface . A small amount of liquid is sealed inside the heat pipe , and all air is removed leaving otherwise only vacuum inside . The liquid has a specific boiling temperature , so that the part of the liquid closest to the hot surface of the CPU boils into gas which then expands filling the middle part , carrying the heat with it . At the cooler end where the fins are connected , the gas condenses back into a liquid as it cools , and then gets carried by the [ capillary action ] ( URL_0 ) of the small holes in the porous surface material coating the inside of the pipe , which acts like a wick , back to the source of the heat . Since heat pipes used in typical CPU coolers rely on capillary action , and not gravity to move the liquid , they can work in any orientation , including upside down .

With multiple cores , a complex task can be divided down into subtasks , some of which can be executed simultaneously ( one task per core ) . This , in theory , allows you to be up to X times faster than a single processor , where X is the number of cores present . In practice , however , the actual speedup you 'll see depends on the type of work being done . Some tasks ca n't be broken down into subtasks , because task A ca n't be started until you have the result of task B , which ca n't be started until you have the result of task C , and so on . In the worst case , a multicore processor will handle a complex task in the same time as a single core processor . Think of it like the checkout lanes in a grocery store . The store is really busy , but they only have one checkout lane open . That might not be a problem if the cashier on duty is really super efficient at their job and can check people out super fast . However , in most cases , you 're probably better off opening more lanes even with mediocre cashiers so that you can check out several people at the same time .

There are some good answers here already , but here 's another answer in case you 're wondering about actual food sickness rather than pooping out food that just does n't digest well . Really fast food poisoning happens when you eat food that had bacteria growing on it for a while that produced toxins . The bacteria itself is n't making you sick , it 's the toxins that were already made and sitting in the food . So when you eat the food with pre - made toxins , you develop diarrhea very quickly ( it can even be less than an hour ) . The classic bacteria that does this is Staph Aureus , which likes things with mayonnaise and cream . So next time you 're at a picnic and everyone gets sick right after , you can blame it on the potato salad and the Staph living in it . This is different than food poisoning by something like Campylobacter jejuni . The bacteria have to get in by eating contaminated food , then they have to grow for awhile and produce toxins . It takes time for there to be enough bacteria to make enough toxins to cause you to get sick , so it may be up to 10 days later before you get diarrhea .

You know how you have different units for , say , measuring distance in metres or feet or yards , etc . ? Well you have a choice of two units for measuring angles : degrees and radians . Ill tell you how radians were thought up and why we use them . Imagine you take a slice out of a pizza . The area of a full circle is pi r^2 as everyone knows and i m sure you do since you have heard of pi , so the area of this slice of a circle is a certain fraction of what the area would be if it was a full circle . Call the angle in the middle of the slice theta . Then the area is theta/360 * pi r^2 . Now take the circumference of the circle slice . This is equal to theta/360 * 2pi * r because its a fraction of what the circumfence would be for a full circle of this particular radius . Now , lets say that instead of calling the angle of a full circle 360 degrees , we call it 2pi radians instead . Now the circumference of a slice of a circle is theta/2pi * 2pi * r. Ooh look ! The 2pis cancel out and we are left with theta * r.

Pretty much any surface reflects some light like a mirror does , but some factors make it hard to make out a picture in the reflection on most surfaces : - Some objects absorb a bunch of the light ( things that we think of as dark or dull ) . Only the light that did n't get absorbed gets reflected , so the picture in the reflection is very faint - If you look at a " flat " surface like a painted wall or a piece of paper up close , you 'll see that its surface is made up of many bumpy ridges , different parts of which are facing in all different directions . The direction light bounces when it hits a surface depends on the angle of the surface , so on these bumpy surfaces the light will be going in all different directions ( " diffused " ) . For someone trying to see an image reflected on the paper , the smallest size of the paper they can make out still has many different little bumps that are redirecting light from different directions , making the reflected image look blurry .

An integral of a function f over [ a , b ] is the area below the graph of f over [ a , b ] . An antiderivative of a function f is a function F such that F 's derivative equals f. Note that if F is an antiderivative , F + constant is also an antiderivative . Those are related : the function that sends x to the integral of f over [ a , x ] is an antiderivative of f ( this is called the fundamental theorem of calculus ) .

A GPS device does n't transmit anything to the satellites , it just listens to them . And they all listen to the same satellites . The [ simple wikipedia on GPS ] ( URL_0 ) has a pretty good explanation of how it works : > A GPS unit takes radio signals from satellites in space circling the Earth . There are about 30 satellites 20,200 kilometres ( 12,600 mi ) above the Earth . ( Each circle is 26,600 kilometres ( 16,500 mi ) radius due to the Earth 's radius . ) Far from the North Pole and South Pole , a GPS unit can receive signals from 6 to 12 satellites at once . Each satellite contains an atomic clock which is carefully set by NORAD several times every day . > The radio signals contain very good time and position of the satellite . The GPS receiver subtracts the current time from the time the signal was sent . The difference is how long ago the signal was sent . The time difference multiplied by the speed of light is the distance to the satellite . The GPS unit uses trigonometry to calculate where it is from each satellite 's position and distance . Usually there must be at least four satellites to solve the geometric equations .

This will be a simplified explanation , since you 're dealing with a somewhat dense topic . When water boils , it means it has enough energy to break out of the liquid phase ( away from all the other liquid molecules ) and get into the gas phase . The amount of thermal energy needed is the amount necessary to get the water to 100 degrees . This can happen in a very " localized " fashion ( a single molecule out of the whole puddle gets enough energy to evaporate ) or in bulk fashion ( boiling water in a pot ) . Logically , the closer the temperature of the water is to the boiling point , the faster both of these can happen . Bulk boiling is very obvious ; all the water is being pushed , thermally , over the edge . It is being forced to evaporate by the heat . Localized evaporation is more nuanced , but still possible because each molecule in a puddle is moving around and bouncing off of every other molecule . If one molecule gets a few lucky bounces , it can get enough energy to evaporate . This is because the temperature of a substance is actually related to the movement of the individual molecules .

I work with " the Internet " , meaning many small ISPs , and this is basically how it works : The " Internet " is not a single , monolithic thing . It 's like the " Economy " . All the Internet is , is a bunch of smaller networks hooked together . When it first started ( by the US Government ) , the main networks it connected were US Military networks , and Universities . Then the big companies ( think IBM , AT & T , etc . ) got in on it . These companies already had thousand - host networks in the 80 's . So naturally , they connected to each other and the Internet was born . When you connect your house to your ISP , you 're but one node in the network . Your ISP , made up of you and all your neighbours who also use that ISP , form your own little network . That network then connects into the broader network via interlinks and a number of protocols you 've never heard of . So your ISP might have connections to two or three other ISPs , forming a slightly larger network . If you keep expanding and interlinking networks , eventually you get the Internet : a world - wide network of smaller networks .

This can only happen if the angle between the side measuring 3 and the side measuring 4 is a * right angle * - it is like the angle between the floor of your house and any of its walls . Conversely , for any * right triangle * ( a triangle with a right angle ) , this property will also be true - the squares of the two smaller sides ( called * legs * ) add up to the square of the longer side ( the * hypotenuse * ) . When you restart a device , you reset the software , and it 's usually the software that causes these issues . There are numerous ( relatively common ) software bugs that may cause a device to stop working . One example is [ deadlock ] ( URL_0 ) . If you 're familiar with 4 - way stops , you know that the intersection is effectively blocked if four cars arrive at exactly the same time . It 's a rare enough event in real life , and human drivers will normally figure out a solution after a while , but computers do n't improvise , so if something similar occurs in a piece of software , the device will sit there doing nothing until the end of time ... or until you reset the software . Simple example : Subroutine A in the software reads data from the internet and then writes it to a file called log.txt . Subroutine B in the software does the opposite . It reads data from log.txt and then sends it over the internet . What happens if you start of both of them at the same time ? A will read data from the internet and then it tries to open log.txt , but it sees that the file is already being used by B , so A will wait until B is finished with the file .

As you almost said in your question , the act of evaporation involves the water molecules getting enough energy so that the water can take its gasous form . The key part here is " water molecules " . When water evaporates , nothing else gets " picked up " with it . Each molecule is always by definition pure H2O. Once up in the atmosphere this water vapour condenses again and forms clouds . Now that it has a tangible form ( i.e. it 's become liquid again ) , other things that are in the atmosphere can dissolve in it once more . This will usually be other gases such as carbon dioxide . Finally , when the condensed water vapour joins into drops large enough to fall due to gravity , we get rain . As the rain descends it might pass through dust and other solid pollutants , some of which will also dissolve into the rain . So by the time a raindrop lands back on earth it 's unlikely to be pure H2O , even though that 's how it started out when it first evaporated . Humans are social animals , and music is a social experience . Not everything comes down to survival instincts . Humans are not automatons , we are innately social and we generally abide by an instinctual social structure that has been around since long before we figured out how to walk standing up . We have a vested interest in helping those who belong to our social group because our survival is dependent on the success of the group , or " tribe . " The tribe provides you with food , safety , and sex -- in proportional amounts relative to the size of your tribe . You are aware of who belongs to your tribe and who does not -- this is the concept of social identity . Those who share your social identity are friends , those who do n't share your identity are ( at the very least ) approached with caution . The ways that this social identity is expressed becomes the tribe 's " culture . " For example , a tribe may adopt a shared visual presentation by marking themselves with or by wearing specific colors or patterns .

Triangular sails are held at an angle to the wind . So if the wind is moving west , it might push the boat southwest . Good sails can make the boat go even faster than the wind at a right angle to the wind . So if the wind is blowing 20 mph to the west , the boat might go 30 mph due south . Think about stepping on an ice cube . It will squirt out to the side faster than the speed your foot was pushing down on it . You might say a boat traveling at a right angle to the wind is " squirting " out from in front of it . Really good sails and hull combinations can harness wind blowing at a small angle . So if the wind is blowing west , the boat travels southeast . A boat can never travel straight into the wind , but always has to at least sort of be traveling across it . So , to go east into a wind traveling west , first you go southeast , then northeast . You 're always traveling across the wind . Switching back and forth like this is called " tacking " .

When visible light comes into contact with an object , the light is either absorbed or reflected by the object based on the wavelength of the light . The color we perceive is the combination of all wavelengths being reflected by the object . So , blue paint reflects a range of wavelengths of blue light , and yellow paint reflects a range of wavelengths of yellow light . When you mix the paint , the color perceived is the combination of wavelengths that are reflected by both the yellow and blue paints . For us , that color is green . Now , you might be asking , " What if the two paints do n't reflect any of the same wavelengths ? " This is possible , and results in black ! Black pigment is the result of no light being reflected , and all light being absorbed . Conversely , white is the result of all light being reflected .

A patent is a license from the government that says that no one can use your invention without your permission . You are allowed to make people pay you for the permission . If they do n't want to pay , you can ask a judge to make them pay . To get a patent , you have to show 1 ) that you invented something useful , and 2 ) that it did n't exist before you invented it . The whole debate surrounding the recent decision concerning the BRCA gene patent was over point 2 ) . Obviously the gene existed before the scientists at Myriad found that it was an important gene in breast cancer , so they ca n't have invented the gene , and they should n't get a patent on the gene , nor make people pay for permission to use or study the gene . However ... the gene as found in the human body is not " useful " , in the sense that unless you do something else to it you ca n't use it for a particular purpose other than it 's natural purpose . Just like you ca n't use a finger bone for anything else other than to be a bone in your finger . That is ... unless you take the gene out of its natural context and make it useful for something that it does n't naturally do , such as detect breast cancer .

Think of entropy as chaos . Disorder . If I took a pack of cards , there 's only one way the pack can be entirely in order , so the entropy is low . If I shuffle it a little bit , the entropy increases , and it increases more the more I shuffle it - that is , there are lots of possible ways for the cards to be arranged , so the entropy is high . This is also why your room seems to get messier ; a chaotic room is entropically favoured over a tidy , ordered room . It 's why your headphones always seem to tangle themselves in your pocket - they can only be tidy one way , and massively tangled in potentially billions of ways . The second law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of a system will spontaneously increase . Spontaneously here means ' without someone giving it a helping hand ' . Your room can return to a lower entropic state , if you put energy into tidying it . You can untangle your headphones , but this takes energy . A slightly more advanced example is that solids have a lower entropy than liquid , as the atoms are all stuck in place , as opposed to liquids where the atoms can flow around one another , like balls in a ball pit .

These are called Chladni Patterns . The plate is being vibrated by an oscillator at its centre . When the frequency of the vibration hits a harmonic of the plate , it creates a standing wave in the plate . This means that certain points are moving , while others are essentially stationary . The salt is pushed off of the areas where the plate is moving , and into the points where it is stationary ( called a node ) . In this way , the salt shows us the node pattern of the plate . It is like a more advanced version of standing waves on a string . Take a jump rope and secure one end , then wave the other end up and down to create a wave in the rope . By repeating this at a certain frequency , you can create a standing wave . [ This video ] ( URL_0 ) gives a really simple demonstration of this . The first standing wave he shows is called the fundamental and has nodes ( those stationary points ) at the ends of the string . When he doubles the frequency he creates what is called the second harmonic and has a node in the middle of the string . You can see that although energy is passing through the node , it is stationary .

There is none . Quantum mechanics is all about probability . Think of a bowling ball rolling up and down the sides of a half - pipe . Classical mechanics says that the ball will roll to the same height each and every time ( assuming no friction ) In quantum mechanics , replace that ball with an electron and we find there is some probability that the electron will just keep going and pop out of the half - pipe . The very same thing coud happen with the bowling ball but all of the atoms that make up the ball would need to jump out at the same time . So something " quantum " could happen to an electron maybe with the probability of flipping a coin and getting heads whereas something " quantum " happening on the classical scale happens with a probability of flipping 10 ^ 20 coins and getting all heads . So the answer is there really is no transition , its just that at most scales quantum behaviors are so unlikely that accounting for them would be a lot of useless math since you would see no difference in the result .

Question # 1 : The wing on an airplane is shaped so that the air flowing across the wing will travel faster over the top of the wing and slower on the bottom . For science - y reasons , the fast - moving air on top of the wing has lower air pressure than the air below the wing . As anyone that 's opened a carbonated drink before knows , things like to move from areas of high pressure to areas of lower pressure . The wing as a whole is pushed upwards as it tries to move towards the low pressure zone . The amount to which this happens is called the " lift force " . Question # 2 : Helicopter blades are sortof like little airplane wings , but instead of pushing air around the wing , a motor pushes the chopper blades into the air . The basic principle is the same - faster air on top of the blade = lower pressure on top of the blades = lift . There are some notable differences between the two , though . All those flaps and moving parts on airplane wings that help to control the precise amount of lift or drag caused by the wing do n't exist on helicopter blades .

* * Hair Growth Cycle * * Hair on the scalp grows about .3 to .4 mm / day or about 6 inches per year . Unlike other mammals , human hair growth and shedding is random and not seasonal or cyclical . At any given time , a random number of hairs will be in one of three stages of growth and shedding : anagen , catagen , and telogen . * * Anagen * * Anagen is the active phase of the hair . The cells in the root of the hair are dividing rapidly . A new hair is formed and pushes the club hair ( a hair that has stopped growing or is no longer in the anagen phase ) up the follicle and eventually out . During this phase the hair grows about 1 cm every 28 days . Scalp hair stays in this active phase of growth for two to six years . Some people have difficulty growing their hair beyond a certain length because they have a short active phase of growth . On the other hand , people with very long hair have a long active phase of growth . The hair on the arms , legs , eyelashes , and eyebrows have a very short active growth phase of about 30 to 45 days , explaining why they are so much shorter than scalp hair .

The story is your blood would boil , your eyeballs would explode , and your lungs would turn to red slush . But the medical literature suggests this view is exaggerated . Although your eardrums might burst I have never seen anything indicating your eyeballs would explode . It 's true that in the absence of air pressure your blood and other bodily fluids would turn to vapor . But that 's not as drastic as it sounds . Your soft tissues would swell , but they 'd return to normal if you were recompressed within a short time . It 's conceivable your lungs would rupture , since in a vacuum the air in them would greatly expand . But experience suggests this is rare even if decompression is extremely rapid . The chances are much greater if your windpipe is closed , making it impossible for the expanding air to escape . Death would not be instantaneous . It 's believed you 'd have 10 - 15 seconds of " useful consciousness " and it 'd be several minutes before you 'd die . If you were rescued within that time there 's a decent chance you 'd survive .

There are two types of " spies " - official cover and non - official cover . Official cover is much more common . Official cover spies work out of an embassy , typically with diplomatic immunity - although with a false agency ( eg : Department of State instead of CIA ) . If they get discovered , they get sent home at the host country 's request . Non - official cover spies are more rare ( for the US anyway ) and its riskier . If they get caught , they have no rights so the host country can do whatever it wants with them . Typically , they 'll be jailed and used to get back the host country 's captured spies in an exchange . Before we continue , its important to note that the US has never really been an " agents on the ground " country like other nations ( esp . Russia with the GRU and Israel 's Mossad ) . The US has always been infatuated with technology - this lack of human intelligence has been a huge sticking point over the past few decades . 9/11 was something of a wake up call and they 've been trying to ramp it up , but the institutional knowledge just is n't what it should be . Another side note - more agencies " spy " than just the CIA .

Imagine a cat . You 're probably imagining a little furry thing with four legs and a tail . Why ? Well , you 've seen a lot of things in your life that have been described to you as " cat . " You now have a general concept of what a cat is : it 's furry , has four legs , has a certain body shape , and behaves in a certain way . Without realizing it , your brain has performed a very difficult task : averaging all the cats you 've seen into a general understanding of " cat . " This particular brain function is impaired in the autistic . An extremely autistic person does not know what a " cat " is . At first they thought it was any small furry creature with four legs , but then they met their neighbor 's Yorkie which was described to them as a " dog , " and they had to start all over figuring out what a cat is . One major consequence of this cognitive impairment is a different approach to memory . When you see a cat , you will remember just a few details : * my aunt has a tabby cat . * An autistic person ca n't compress the memory down to broad terms such as * tabby cat , * so instead they remember every detail of the animal .

Ozone is too reactive to exist in quantity near the ground . But high up in the atmosphere , it is constantly being created as ultraviolet rays ( or was it cosmic rays ? ) split Oxygen molecules apart , and there 's not much else up there for the Ozone to react with .

It is found deep underground and typically locked off from the water table . If it is released into the water table or the ocean , or any other typically natural environment , it is toxic . To ask why something natural is toxic is not the right question , as many examples of this exist . Lead and mercury , for example are both naturally occurring and found in the ground . Both will kill pretty much any animal and most plant life in sufficient quantity . Back to oil , how does it pollute ? Aside from being a simple carcinogen to most animal life , it floats on water and coats animals that break the surface of water . Birds are heavily affected by this . Their feathers get coated and they lose their ability to fly , and stay insulated . Mammals can become overheated because they no longer have the ability to sweat ( not all mammals have the ability to sweat , of course , but many do ) . And all of this ignores the massive health hazard posed by ingesting it . In short , oil is simply a toxic chemical that is derived from decomposition and pressure over extremely long periods of time . It pollutes because it 's toxic .

Most types of audio files are compressed in order to make the file smaller . FLAC files are not compressed * , which is why they have better sound quality . Compression is a fancy way to try to recreate the same file , but use less data to do it . It 's sort of like what happens when you take a picture , shrink it down , and then blow it back up again , like [ this ] ( URL_0 ) and [ this ] ( URL_1 ) . What happened is that shrinking the image down reduced the file size , because there are fewer pixels . However , if you blow it back up to the original size , there was a loss of detail , which is why it looks bad . There 's less overall data in the grainy picture . The same thing is done with audio . The way they do the actual compression is * much * more elegant and complicated than what I just did with the picture , but the basic principle is the same ; you 're losing detail ( fidelity in audio terms ) in exchange for a smaller filesize . Now , for most people , the difference between a high - quality MP3 and FLAC are n't noticeable , which is why the format is n't very popular . Almost all audio devices / software can handle MP3 , whereas you have to use special stuff for FLAC .

When you push start a car , you hold in the clutch and push the car . Get the car rolling , and you can quickly snap the clutch and make the piston rods turn . Fridges rely on a thermodynamic process known as a [ Heat Pump . ] ( URL_0 ) A quick overview of how they work however : 1 . Electricicty from you wall outlet runs a compressor pump . This compresses the refrigerant fluid , creating a hot fluid at high pressure . - Remember when you compress a fluid , it gets warm . 2 . This hot fluid at high pressure goes through a condensor ( often called the radiator ) on the back of the fridge . This allows the hot fluid to cool down , by losing it 's excess heat to the ambient air . In doing this , the fluid condenses into a liquid . 3 . This high pressure liquid then goes through an expander / throttle valve . This essentially drops the pressure of the fluid : oposite to at point 1 , a decompressing fluid cools down . Because the high pressure fluid was at ambient temperature , the expanding fluid ( past the valve ) will chill below ambient temperature . 4 . The sub - cooled fluid is then passed through an evaporator ( a long coil burried in the body of the fridge ) where it absorbs heat from it 's surroudnings and vaporises the remainder of the refrigerant fluid .

I do n't know much about the New Testament , but the Old Testament authorship is best explained by a variation on the Documentary Hypothesis . The Documentary Hypothesis states that the first four books of the Old Testament ( or more specifically , the Five Books of Moses or the Torah ) was compiled based on several different sources by some sort of editor . The book of Deuteronomy was added at a later date . This theory explains how some Biblical stories seem to repeat , how different section emphasize different aspects of Judaism , and why there are multiple different names for God that reflect sections with different literary styles . The defining characteristic of a pyramid scheme is that there 's always an initial payment ( for buying into some kind of ' business ' ) , and because the business itself usually does n't work very well , the only way to recoup the money you put in is to recruit more people to make that initial payment and buy into the ' business ' , and you get a cut of their initial payment . Whether you 're supposed to sell magazine subscriptions or cat food does n't really matter , because recruiting is actually where most of the revenue comes from , and the ' business idea ' is just bait to get people to sign up . These schemes only work as long as they 're growing rapidly , but finding sufficient numbers of new recruits becomes harder with each level , which means the scheme will collapse at some point and those not at the top of the pyramid will lose all or some of the money they put in . The bottom line is , if the business idea they 're selling really worked and made money , those already in the business would be spending their time selling whatever product they have to sell . They would not be going around trying to get new people to join .

Suppose you have two zones , one with a 90 % white population , and another with a 70 % black population ( lets assume we only have white and black people for simplicity ) . The first 90 % white population is a bit larger than the mostly black one and gets 2 representatives , and the mostly black district gets 1 representative . Now , suppose we rezoned in such a way as to split the black population up between the two new districts . Now each district is about 70 % white and 30 % black , so all three representatives tend to vote along with the white majority . Or , perhaps we have a big district with 2 representatives and a smaller one with 1 representative and they are each 90 % black . We rezone the districts so that each district has about the same number of people , but that makes the first dip below the dividing line where you get two representatives , but does n't push the second over the line . The formerly three representatives are now two , and the voting power of the black majority in the area has been reduced .

This is n't the ELI5 answer but it 's a good question . For our purposes , the acceleration caused by gravity on the surface of a planet ( but also more generally ) is given by : a = ( g * m)/r^2 This is just Newton 's Law of Univeral Gravitation re - arranged a bit . " g " is a constant , " m " is the mass of whatever is doing the accelerating ( in this case , the planet ) and " r " is the the radius of the planet . At this point it should be clear that more mass will tend to increase the acceleration , but a bigger radius will tend to decrease it , even if it 's not exactly intuitive how that will play out in practice . Enter Density . Density is the ratio of the mass of an object to its volume , and for a spherical planet that means we can express the mass of the planet as follows , using the formula for the volume of a sphere : m = ( 4/3)(pi)(r^3)(d ) If you substitute that expression back into the first one , you 'll end up with : a = ( 4/3)(pi)(g)(d)(r ) Which is actually something that 's intuitively useful . 4/3 , pi , and g are all constant , so the only two things that affect the acceleration due to gravity of a planet are its density and its radius .

There is always some small amount of sweat glands that are active , even if you are not hot or moving around . This creates a tiny amount of sweat on your body and because sweat is made up of mainly water , which has a high heat capacity ( the amount of heat that something can absorb before it changes temperature ) , some heat from your body will be transfered into the water of your sweat . Then sweat does what it does best . The small amount of liquid evaporates off of your skin , taking some of your body heat with it . This lowers the amount of heat in your body , effectively cooling you down . But its not only sweat . Your body is always radiating heat because your a warm blooded animal . The heat from deep inside your body is usually carried by your blood to the skin , where it can be radiated out . Then the cooler air outside absorbs some of the heat and blows away with it , lowering the heat on your skin therefore making you feel colder . All raising something to a power means is that you 're multiplying it by itself over and over again . 5 to the 3rd power is 5 * 5 * 5 . 5 to the second power is 5 * 5 . 5 to the first power is just 5 . There are a couple ways of explaining why 5 ^ 0 is 1 , and I 'll go over two of them . * * The first way * * : * ( keep in mind this is ELI5 -- this is kind of an oversimplification which takes advantage of the multiplicative identity to simplify exponentiation up to a point ) * Understand that anything multiplied by 1 is that number . So when we 're looking at 5 ^ 3 , we 're really looking at 5 * 5 * 5 * 1 . 5 ^ 2 is 5 * 5 * 1 . 5 ^ 1 is 5 * 1 . And 5 ^ 0 is just 1 . * * The second way :* * * ( which is less ELI5 but more " correct " ) * So we know that 5 ^ 3 is 5 * 5 * 5 , and 5 ^ 2 is 5 * 5 . The inverse of multiplying is dividing : if you multiply by 5 , you can " undo " that by dividing by 5 . So to go from 5 ^ 3 to 5 ^ 2 , we divide by 5 . 5 * 5 * 5 / 5 = 5 * 5 . We can follow this down : 5 ^ 3 = 125 , 125 / 5 = 25 , which is 5 ^ 2 . 25 / 5 = 5 , which is 5 ^ 1 . 5 / 5 = 1 , which is 5 ^ 0 .

Pi is n't infinite - it 's between 3 and 4 . Pi does n't have a finite expression , because it ca n't be written as the ratio of two integers . That 's just a fact about circles . It 's best to think of pi as " the number which is equal to the ratio of a circle 's circumference to its diameter " . This tells you how to build the number to whatever precision you need to and what algebraic properties it 's going to have . ( There are other ways to define it , but this one is common . ) Some numbers are just numbers - like ' 5 ' or ' 3 ' . They 're the counting numbers . However , even by the time we get to the negative numbers , we have to have an implicit action or relationship associated with them - the negative numbers " take away " or " undo " what having a positive one does . Similarly , the next step up , in the rational numbers , are things like ' 1/2 ' or ' 4/7 ' - numbers that say " multiply by the top and undo multiplication by the bottom " . To get beyond that , you need even fancier constructions - like " every possible string of digits " .

Darwin published the Origin of Species in 1859 . It was based on a series of simple observations that he made , as he was a naturalist ( which , at the time , meant mostly that he went about studying nature and cataloging what he learned about it ) . He noticed the following : * * OBSERVATIONS * * * Given enough time and no constraints , species will produce a potentially unlimited number of offspring . ( This is intuitive ; creatures make more creatures . 1,000 elephants , left to their own devices , will eventually become 10,000 elephants , and so on . ) - Resources are limited . ( Food , water , shelter ; these are finite ) . * * INFERENCE * * : - Competition for resources exists . * * OBSERVATIONS * * : - Individuals vary . - Some proportion of this variation may be inherited . * * INFERENCES * * : - Individuals whose natural variation makes them more suited to the environment are more likely to survive . - Individuals who survive are more likely to pass on their genes , including those genes that increased their likelihood of survival . In this way , the environment creates pressure that favors certain traits , some of which are heritable .

The rules are simple , yes . 1 . Place a stone anywhere on the board that does n't immediately cause a capture ( No suicide ) 2 . First , the board . A 19 by 19 board has 361 spaces in it , each of which can have a black , white , or no stone in it . From the math , this means that there are ( theoretically ) 361 ! * 3 = ( 361 * 360 * 359 * ... * 1 ) * 3 possible states , though many of them would lead to captures and thus collapse . In more plain numbers , that is around 4.3 * 10 ^ 768 , or 4 followed by 768 zeros . Theoretically every game of go is thus unique . Next , the basic strategy . The entire game is spent building the most you can while exploring peaceful coexistence . Balancing stability and strength with fluidity and expansion .

Your speed can be determined by timing you as you pass through sets of blocks . In fact , there 's a device called a VASCAR that is a dedicated device for making these speed calculations . After setting the device for the correct distance , an operator just toggles a switch as you pass the first mark and then pass the second , and the unit calculates and displays your average speed over that span . These units are designed for mounting in patrol cars , motorcycles , and ... you guessed it ... light aircraft . In practice , though , the cost of paying for a pilot and an airplane ( in addition to the ground officers ) is simply too high for airplanes to be used with any regularity . The time based system is still sometimes used from the ground though , particularly by officers stationed on overpasses . It has the advantage that no radar detector can tell a cop is just looking at you , but the disadvantage that you need someone with a suitable vantage point ( which usually makes this a two - car operation ) .

Okay I will give you a very long answer . The first thing is to decide what it means for a set to be bigger than another set . For finite sets , the definition of " bigger than " is so obvious intuitively that it hardly seems worth talking about . Consider the sets A={a , b , c } and B={e , f , g , h } . Which set is bigger ? Well obviously B is bigger . How do we know that B is bigger ? Well , B has more elements , right ? So we might be tempted to define " bigger " as follows : > For two sets A and B , we say that the set B is " bigger than " the set A if B has more elements in it than A does . And this might seem like a satisfactory way to define it , but it turns out to just be sweeping the problem under the rug : we 've defined what " bigger than " means , but what does it mean for a set to have " more elements " ? We have n't really solved anything at all ! We would like to have a precise mathematical definition of " bigger than " , but all we 've done is defined " bigger than " in terms of some relation " more than " which is not precisely defined .

5 year old explanation ( paraphrasing from Sagan 's Cosmos series ): Imagine a chunk of clay . Now imagine that you set it on a desk , and push down hard on the top with your hand . Now flip it to the side , and do the same . Flip it another angle , and smash it again . Keep doing this , and over time , you will be left with a sphere . This is why spheres are common , because everything with mass has gravity , and that gravity is pulling everything on the surface down towards the center ( this has the same effect as smashing clay with your hand pushing down ) . So , the more mass something has , the more of an effect gravity has , and hence the more it ends up like a sphere . Compare that with say , an asteroid , which does not have as much mass , and as such , can retain its odd shapes , like a potato or such .

Then this 13 year - old kid comes along , sacrifices his Knight ( which Byrne did n't take ) and then even his Queen ( which Byrne DID take ) and just crushes Byrne ! How did that happen ! ? Fischer taught us many things about the game , and this game shows what he taught us very well . [ Here 's a link ] ( URL_0 ) if you want to see someone analyse the game . In case you 're interested , here are the lessons to learn from this game : 1 . Developing your pieces out into the centre quickly . Every piece is better in the centre of the board . ( e.g. A Knight can only move to 2 different squares if it starts from the corner , but to 8 different squares if it starts in the centre . ) If you do n't get your pieces out quickly and your opponent does , you can often get attacked quickly . 2 . Having a safe King . Simple really , if your King is not protected , it can be checkmated easier .

In most locations this is not a big deal as the city annexes surrounding suburbs . In Detroit , due to some complicated legal / political reasons , they could not do this . Depends how much and where . If its into an artery , it 'll travel down until the vessel gets too thin , at which point it will obstruct blood flow . This is called an ' air embolism ' . What happens afterwards is the same as when any blood vessel gets occluded , the tissue fed by that blood vessel can become necrotic due to oxygen deprivation unless it can get blood flow from other blood vessels . If its a small amount of air , the occlusion might be somewhere where the tissue can be blood flow from elsewhere . Nothing bad will happen as eventually the air will dissolve into the bloodstream and be reabsorbed by the surrounding tissues . A larger amount of air , however , and it can obstruct an artery that feeds an entire organ , such as a cardiac artery , a cerebral artery , or your mesenteric artery ( feeds blood to your bowels ) . This can cause bigger problems depending on what organ becomes ischemic ( oxygen deprived ): a heart attack , stroke , etc . Air getting into the arteries is n't very common because arteries tend to be deeper into the tissue and rarely involved in injections ( which are the leading cause of air emboli ) .

So , the original definition of a circlejerk is where a lot of people get together , and literally begin to masturbate the people next to them . Metaphorically , a circlejerk is a self - congratulatory discussion or community . In other words , like - minded people come together and tell each other how great they are . The term gets tossed around a lot on reddit because the very way the voting system works tends to reinforce circlejerks . Both comments and posts get voted up or down based on popularity . On something like , say , /r / politics , the most likely things to be voted up are things which are popular opinions among the readership . Unpopular opinions , even if they 're well - formed , tend to be voted down , because people do n't want to hear something that contradicts what they believe . The result is that you get a community that is very enthusiastic about certain opinions which , compared to the general population , are a little bit out there . But if you spend enough time reading a circlejerk , you start to think their opinions are completely mainstream , and that people who think differently than the circlejerk are just weird . That 's kind of the danger of them .

Passive voice places the focus on the thing being acted upon , rather than the agent performing the action . * In general * this is bad , but there are cases where the actor is n't really the focus . Basically you want to determine what is important and keep your focus on that . Let 's take these two sentances : > " The man walked into the room carrying a briefcase . " or > " The briefcase was carried into the room by the man . " The subject of the first sentance is the man . The subject of the second is the briefcase . Which do we care about more ? In most cases , the man is going to be the focus of what s going on . The man has agency . He can do things . The briefcase is an animate object . In general inanimate objects should never be made the subject via passive voice , because you want to focus on what is most important , which is the actual agent performing the action . We can also add more detail here : > A sharp dressed man confidently strode into the room carrying a briefcase . Adding this detail while the briefcase is the subject is more difficult and awkward . > The briefcase was confidently carried into the room by a sharp dressed man . It just does n't sound right .

First , we must define what " 0.9999 ... " means . The ' ... ' at the end means that you should take the limit of the behavior before that . So we want the number that is reached by starting with 0.9 , and then 0.99 , followed by 0.999 , 0.9999 , 0.99999 ... etc . The number we want is the number that this process has as a limit ( if such a number exists ) . Well , now we need a second fact : if two numbers are n't the same number , then there has to be a definite distance between them . That is , if you give me the two numbers , I must be able to tell you a positive number such that they are at least that far apart . But what about the limit of 0.9999 ... and 1 ? Well , if you give me a distance , I can find some number of 9s in a row such that 1 minus that number is less than the distance you gave me . So we ca n't name a distance between the limit of 0.9999 ... and 1 ! Since we ca n't say they have any distance between them , they 're the same number . tl;dr : " 0.99999 .... " is a statement about a process , like " 3 - 2 " , and is just another way to specify the number " 1 " .

In the 1970 's Unix introduced the forward slash ( / ) as the directory separator . In the 1980 's Microsoft began using backslash ( \\ ) because they had already been using the forward slash ( / ) to introduce command line options . In a Unix environment ( actually , due to the behavior of the shell ) you ca n't insert a space between two words without using an escape ( two - stroke ) character . The backslash is part of that escape ( two - stroke ) character . So you have filesystems that look like : /home / user / Pictures , but not /home / user / Vacation Pictures , unless you use a backslash : /home / user / Vacation\ Pictures where " \ " ( backslash space ) is the escape ( two - stroke ) character . The internet is built around Unix systems , so it follows Unix conventions . Basically , the internet is a really big * nix system . An easy way to think of this is like a pharmacy . You walk in , ask for something ( Service Request ) and the pharmacist verifys your information ( Request Parsing ) then goes to get your medicine ( Data Retrieval ) . A DDoS attack would be like getting a huge group of people to all go to the pharmacy at the same time and demand things all at once and over and over that may or may not be something they actually have ( Junk Data ) . Eventually the pharmacy gets overwhelmed and they have to stop all incoming requests meaning that it shuts down . This is usually accomplished through things called " Botnets " which are vast non - centralized computer networks , most of which have no idea that they 're being used as such , they 're hijacked for this purpose through spyware and viruses .

Let 's say you decide to represent all numbers using little square tiles that measure 1 cm long on a side . ( Or inch , or whatever . ) 1 is one tile . 2 is two tiles placed next to each other in a line . 3 is three tiles in a line . You could carry on like this , so that 4 is four tiles in a line , but you notice here that you have a new option . You could put four tiles in a line , or you can make a little 2x2 grid instead to represent 4 . Either way , the area is the same , and that 's the visual thing you 're going for with this system ... you want to be able to judge how big a number is compared to another number by looking at the area its tiles take up . However you arrange the tiles , the area for 4 is the same , so no difference right ? Well , let 's compare 4 to 2 . You line it up and say its twice as big . Cool ! But now think about how this is going to work for really big numbers .

The " joke " is that 2 + 2 = 5 for extremely large values of 2 . It 's referring to the fact that you need to take precision into account . 2.4 + 2.4 = 4.8 . If you round all the numbers involved you get 2 + 2 = 5 .

It certainly is n't stupid , radiation is not something intuitive or widely understood . Radiation refers a process where particles are given off by some source and travel out , away from the source , without any material to carry them , or without the help of whatever material they 're moving through . For example , electrons moving in a wire are * not * seen as radiation , because they need the help of the circuit they 're in to move , where as light moving through space * is * radiation , because it is n't being carried by any material . There are two types of radiation , ionizing and non - ionizing . Non - ionizing radiation refers to things like low energy light ( photons that have a long wavelength ) or neutrinos ( which also come from the sun , but pass harmlessly though us without us ever even noticing ) , and it 's not very dangerous , but what people normally mean when they talk about radiation is ionizing radiation . Ionizing radiation means any kind of radiation that can break up atoms when it hits them or passes nearby , normally by separating the atom from one of it 's electrons .

It 's just a placeholder for some " thing " , like a number or a string . It 's the same concept as a variable in algebra . Say you write : int n = 5 ; You 've just defined the variable " n " to be an integer that holds the number 5 , so if you use " n " in an equation or something later , it 'll represent 5 . Of course , you can change variables , so if you later wrote : n = 10 ; Every time you used " n " after that , it would be 10 instead of 5 . Notice I did n't have to prepend that line with " int " , because you 've already declared that " n " is an integer in the first line . In fact , if you tried to write : n = " apple " ; you 'd get an error , because Java is what 's termed a " strongly typed " language , meaning when you declare a variable to be a certain " type " ( and integer , a string , etc ) it has to remain that type as long as it 's in scope .

In an automatic car , when you 're in drive , the engine is always connected to the transmission . When you come to a stop , the transmission automatically shifts to first gear so you can accelerate away easily afterwards . Your car has to idle ( 600 - 900ish rpm ) to keep it from stalling . When you remove your foot from the brake , since the engine is connected to the transmission , it 's the power from that idle pushing you along . Alternatively , the idle does the exact opposite when traveling at speed . If you to let off the accelerator , the drag from the driving gear slows down the car . But if you let off , then shift to neutral , you simply coast .

There are lots of chemical reactions going on inside your body at any given time , and most of them generate heat . In fact , since your body is thick and solid ( as these things go ) , and made mostly of water ( which holds heat very well ) , you generate enough heat raise your body temperature above 98.6 easily . Much like a computer , you need a heat sink to keep yourself from warming up beyond what you 're designed to handle . That heat sink is your skin . But in order for a heat sink to work , there has to be a pretty big difference between the temperature it 's trying to cool and the temperature it 's bleeding that heat into . The body is designed to function most easily at around what we call ' room temperature . ' We set it at that * because * it 's easy to maintain without extra work , and it 's therefore comfortable . Below that , you start getting cold , and your body kicks into gear to produce more heat . At the extreme it will cause you to shiver , because muscle contractions produce a * lot * of heat . One of the jobs of the Federal Reserve it to help set monetary policy for the United States . One of the main ways it does this is by setting the Federal Fund Rate . This is an interest rate that banks pay each other for interbank loans , but more importantly , almost all other interests rates ( home loans , credit cards , etc ) , directly or indirectly , are related to this rate . The lower the interest rates , the easier it is to get a loan , which makes expansion ( personal or business ) easier , which generally increases growth . When the economy is going along good , the Fed raises interest rates , which slows things down a bit , and when it 's going poorly it drops interest rates to give things a boost . What it 's attempting to do is avoid boom / bust cycles ( which obviously it ca n't eliminate given we are still recovering from a giant economic bubble bursting ) , and provide steady continuous long term growth . In the wake of the housing bubble collapse , the Fed dropped interest rates from around 5.25 % to it 's current rate of 0.1 % .

It 's a measure of how long it takes for data to get from your computer to the hosting computer . When data gets exchanged between your computer and another one somewhere on the internet , it 's not a direct connection between them . Each packet has to be routed and it will pass through a bunch of different " hops " across a bunch of different physical networks before it reaches its destination . Depending on the number of hops and the speed of each network , a packet will take a certain amount of time to get there . It 's important in games , because the server is trying to make sure that each individual player 's computer has up to date information on what all the other players are doing . If it takes half a second for packets to travel between your computer and the server , then all of the data in your game ( for example , where the other players are ) is going to be half a second behind . In a fast paced game , a lot can happen in half a second .

Gravity follows an inverse square law - for each unit of measure , the force of gravity goes down by the distance from the source squared . So if you 've got gravity at a particular point , 1 mile from the source ... at 2 miles , it 's going to be 1/4th of the original strength . At 3 miles , it 'll be 1/9th of the original strength . At 4 miles , 1/16th of the original strength , etc . These forces are enough to pull a ( solid ) planet into a roughly round shape . Keep in mind though , this just means round " on the average " - you 're not going to get a planet perfectly round unless it 's made of gas . Just think of Earth in that sense . That said , you 'll actually get a minor effect if you 've got something planet - sized in close proximity to another planet , but it is n't much - the Moon counts for this , and you 'll get a couple of feet of difference IIRC . Without that proximity though , you wo n't get an effect - the force simply weakens too much at distance . Also keep in mind that planets are n't perfectly round . They tend to be " oblate spheroids " - in other words , squished spheres . The Earth , for example , bulges in the middle by 42.72 km ( 26.54 mi ) .

Legally , there are different ways to organize a business that have their advantages and disadvantages . The most simple is a sole proprietorship , which is a business owned by one single person . The downside of a sole proprietorship is that the owner can be personally liable for all of the business 's debts , which can be way more than one person can afford . To avoid the problem of liability , different business associations were created in the law to , among other things , limit a business owner 's personal liability . Some examples of these business associations include the : General Partnership , Limited Partnership , Limited Liability Company , and Corporation . The differences between them are fairly nuanced , but in general , they have different rules for how they 're formed , operated / controlled , and taxed . There 's also varying rules on how easy it is to sell your share of the business if you no longer want to own it . With respect to the " bad reputation " that corporations get , much of that may come from the fact that the largest companies are pretty much exclusively organized as corporations .

When computers run programs , all the information they work with is stored in the computer 's memory , or " RAM " ( which is short for random - access - memory ) . It 's called random access because the program can quickly access information from anywhere in the memory , in just a single instruction . Now , inside a computer program , everything is a number . That 's how computers represent all the information they hold . Well , when a program needs to access some information from memory , it needs to issue an instruction that tells the computer to fetch it from a particular part of the memory . How does it tell the computer what part of the memory to fetch it from ? Well , the memory in computers is represented as a very bit list of boxes , each of which can store a small number ( from 0 to 255 ) . We call these boxes " bytes " . A byte is a little box of memory which can store a number between 0 and 255 . The program can read ( look at ) , or write ( change ) the number inside any byte in memory . But to do that , it needs to tell the computer _ which byte _ to read from or write to . To enable this , every byte in memory has an _ address _ associated with it .

The computer itself does not get slower . As you use your computer , you will over time adjust settings , install new software and update existing components . In addition , your data storage devices may become cluttered with old data . The usual way to " fix " this problem is to reinstall the operating system . However , since you will likely wish to add the software you were using before back , you 'll still be faced with reduced performance . In the end , as software gets better , it takes more processing power . Your computer does n't get faster unless you update it in some way , so it seems to get slower over time as you do more with it .

" The legal pad got its start with Thomas Holley in 1888 . Holley was 24 and working at a paper mill in Holyoke , Massachusetts . Every day , he and his co - workers threw out a lot of scrap pieces , called sortings , left over from cutting paper into the right sized sheets . He knew there had to be a use for them and eventually hit on the idea of cutting the sortings to the same size and binding them into small notepads . Since the paper was essentially trash to the mill , they could sell the pads at low prices . The first few batches of pads sold so well that Holley quit his job at the mill and started his own company to collect scraps from the local mills and manufacture and sell his pads . The pads that Holley made probably were n’t yellow , and that is n’t the only color they come in today . The only thing that technically sets the legal pad apart from every other notepad , says the American Pad and Paper Company , is 1.25 - inch , left - side “ down lines , ” or margins . Holley added these lines in the early 1900s at the request of a loyal customer , a judge who wanted a space to write comments on his notes .

A long time ago , people thought that the fundamental building blocks of physical objects ( stars , chairs , armadillos , grapefruits , whatever ) were earth , water , air , and fire . More recently , we learned that things are actually made of molecules . Still more recently , we learned that those molecules were made of atoms . Even more recently , we learned that those atoms were made of protons / neutrons / electrons . Even more recently , we learned ( but are still not totally sure ) that protons and neutrons are made of quarks . Currently , particle physics is based on a theory called " the standard model " , which is more or less a list of a few dozen extremely tiny particles which are assumed to be the actual fundamental building blocks of reality ( as in , they are not themselves composed of smaller objects stuck together ) . Various physical properties ( like mass , charge , etc ) of those particles govern how they work . This works very nicely , and seems to fit very well with a lot of experimentally observed results . However , there 's still some things that are n't explained .

In order to float it needs to be lighter than the water it displaces . That means the floating ability of an object is determined by its whole mass and its whole volume . The fewer mass is dsitributed over a larger volume , the easier an object can float . In other words it depends on the average density ( mass per volume ) of the object . The trick to make a ship made of steel float is not to use a solid block of steel without an empty interior ( which would not float ) , but just cover the volume with a rather thin layer of steel . Then the average density is much much lower than the density of steel and water and the ship can float .

Additional to previous answers ( the screen flashing black then making an area around each enemy white , which the ' camera ' in the light gun detects ) , there is also another factor which allows the game to know * which * enemy you hit . Old TVs ( CRTs ) update the screen by scanning a beam horizontally one line at a time , from top to bottom . Any point on the screen is brightest when first hit with the beam , then slowly fades out until it is scanned again the next frame . The console knows which part of the screen is being updated at any given time . When you click the trigger the light gun watches for the point in time that the area it is aimed at gets updated , and the console can then work out where on screen you were aiming . As all modern TV technologies ( LCD , Plasma ) do not scan the screen in the way that old ( CRT ) TVs did , proper light guns do not work on them . Any ' Light Gun ' that works on newer TV types operates in a different way , normally by placing IR lights around the screen that can be tracked , like a Wii - mote .

Fix the prize behind door A and suppose that your strategy is to not switch . How can you win ? Well , you win if and only if you select door A in the first place , right ? Because you pick a door and then Monty asks you if you want to switch and you say no so you end up with the door you selected at the start . Assuming that you 're equally likely to pick any door , the probability that you win under this strategy is 1/3 , exactly equal to the probability that you select door A in the first place . Now fix the prize behind door A and suppose that your strategy is to switch . How can you win ? Just work out what happens in each case : Case 1 . You picked door A in the first place . Then Monty either opens door B or C , and you switch to whichever one he did n't open . You lose . Case 2 . You picked door B in the first place . A law is a fact and usually a very specific one . It usually does not explain * why * it is a fact . A theory is kind of like a collection of facts that individually explain a larger , more encompassing phenomenon . Take the theory of evolution for example . It 's important to know that the entire theory of evolution is that allele frequencies change over time . The facts in this case are things like migration . It is a fact that migration changes allele frequencies within a population . Genetic drift is another thing that changes allele frequencies , as is mutation and natural selection . Each of these things change allele frequencies . These are facts . When you combine them , you do n't call it the Law of Evolution because there 's lots of smaller facts that support the overall idea . You call it the * theory * of evolution . It 's also important to know that theories do not " graduate " to become laws .

Being born in the Soviet union couple of months before it broke down , I think I 'll try and answer your question . If you have a basic understanding of economy ( production cost of the manufacturer , vs. willingness to pay of the customer ) , it 's easy to understand that the equilibrium price is where producer and consumer reaches a concensus for a certain price for a certain quantity of product . In free market , every business is free to set a price for their product . It can be lower or higher than the equilibrium price ( higher means product is more expensive and customers will search for alternatives , lower and you 're losing money ) . Setting an adequate price is labour intensive , as you need to know the customers willingness to pay for your product ( by using for example surveys ) . In soviet economy , central bureau of economic affairs would calculate the price for each and every item the country was producing , taking into account the production cost and the market for the item . The price was stamped on the item , so that a factory director / reseller could n't ask a higher price ( that would be a black market , which did exist due to huge shortages ) .

Electricity that is not used is not put into the grid . Power plants send away electricity on demand . The thing is this : You can imagine electricity to be like water . As long as you have no need for water , you just clog the end of the pipe . In our electrical case : There is nothing running inside your house that uses energy . Now you need water , so you place the end of the pipe inside let 's say your bathtub and unclog it . At that moment your water supplier has to send water through the pipe to keep it full . He will let water flow in until you clog your pipe again . And that 's what power plants do , too . The power lines are always energized and ready to send charge into whatever you plug into your power outlet , but as long as there is nothing to take the charge , the power plant does n't refill them , so they do n't have to send any power into the grid . Now there is actually unused energy . Since you do n't have to send a message to the power plant whenever you want to turn on your computer , they always have to have a potential of offering more energy than is used right now .

First off , relativity is hard . It screws with everything you know , it makes distances shorter and time longer and things heavier . If I throw a ball at you with 30 km / h , you see it coming with 30 km / h. If I 'm also running towards you at 10 km / h , you see the ball coming with 40 km / h and if I 'm running away from you at 10 km / h , you see the ball coming with 20 km / h. So far , so good . Now , light is different . If I shine a beam of light at you , you think it has the speed of light . Duh . If I also move towards you at half the speed of light , how fast is the beam to you ? * still the speed of light * . Our universe just works that way . Now , that just ca n't work normally . Einstein said " you know , if this really works that way and physics still applies here ( conservation of energy and other things must still be true ) , then we must probably have the following other effects : " . So it 's just a rigorous derivation based on an observation , namely that light always travels at the same speed .

" Dark matter " is a blanket term for matter that we can not directly observe . For example , it would n't show up if you photographed it with the Hubble telescope . For example , lets say you observe a million kilograms of dust in a certain region of space , but gravity is behaving as though there were two million kilograms of matter there . It stands to reason that there has to be another million kilograms of matter in that region of space that I can not see . After all , gravity does n't just decide to work a little harder in some places than others . And just as there is dark matter , there is " dark energy . " And there 's quite a lot of both , as it turns out . In fact , ( depending on who you talk to ) a substantial majority of the universe is composed of dark matter / energy . Wild , huh ?

The origin of our " special relationship " with the UK comes from the Monroe Doctrine . In 1823 , James Monroe said that if any European nations try to colonize or meddle in the affairs of North and South American nations , it will be treated as a hostile act - and we , the US , will intervene . At this time , most Spanish / Portuguese colonies had become independent . The United States , however , could n't prevent other European powers ( such as The Holy Alliance(Prussia , Russia , Austria ) ) from trying to colonize the Americas all alone . They needed help from Britain , and Britain obliged because they knew that any other European power would screw up the trade and markets overseas . In fact , for some time Britain was the only one of the two capable of enforcing the Doctrine because America did n't have the naval power to do so . Twenty - three years later , Britain and America would co - operate once again during the Second Opium War in Hong Kong . The British needed help during a battle between a couple boats at a Fort . We assisted and that would be the first time US and British soldiers fought together .

Based on random chance , your genetic code has multiple encoding errors . Some of these errors are going to be bad , potentially crippling , genetic defects . Luckily for you , you get two copies of each gene , one from each parent . In most cases the good gene you get from your other parent is dominant , meaning it covers up the defective gene . So imagine you get an extremely rare genetic mutation that causes a crippling disease . Also we 'll say you have 4 kids , two sons and two daughters . Each of your kids get a copy of each gene from you and one from your spouse . If they happen to inherit the defective version of a gene from you , your spouse will likely give them the good version and they 'll be all be okay . Based on random chance , there 's a 50/50 chance that each of your kids gets the bad gene from you . So odds are that two have it . Let 's say 1 son and 1 daughter each get it . Now those two siblings have a child together . The child has a 50/50 shot of getting the bad gene from the mother and a 50/50 shot of getting it from the father . So a 25 % chance of exhibiting the trait . This is much higher than the chance from non - siblings .

" there are 11 spacetime dimensions " is too strong a statement . We have no evidence for this at all ; the reason you will most probably have heard of it is because an 11 dimensional universe , combined with string theory , is one of many things which could explain the way our universe is the way it is . To take it back to basics : What are you made of ? Your body is made of tissue , like bones and muscles , which in turn are made of cells . Cells ( and , indeed , everything around you ) are made of atoms . Atoms have a positive nucleus , surrounded by negative electrons , because positive charges attract negative ones . The electron is called a " fundamental particle " because it can not be broken down into anything smaller , as far as we know . It is a type of fundamental particle called a lepton . There are 6 leptons , in three families ; electrons , muons , tauons , and their accompanying neutrinos . The nucleus is not a fundamental particle . It is made of protons and neutrons , but they are not fundamental particles either . Protons and neutrons are made of quarks , " up " and " down " quarks to be specific .

Money is n't a physical thing , it 's an idea . It does n't have objective existence . * Cash * is a physical thing with objective existence , but cash is n't money , cash is * worth * money . We 've got a lot lot lot lot more money in the world than there is cash , though . When the stock market crashes , the amount of money in the world is reduced . That money does n't " go " anywhere , mostly , it just ceases to be . Say you buy ten shares of FOO for $ 10 / share , so you spent $ 100 . A month passes , and the FOO company is in the news with some cool new product , and now people are willing to pay $ 20 / share for FOO because they believe it will make a big profit in the future . Your ten shares are now worth $ 200 because people are willing to pay more for them . So we say that that $ 200 exists in the stock market , even if you do n't sell your shares . You hold on to these shares , and a few months later there 's a recession . Now , not only do people no longer believe FOO will make as big a profit , but fewer of them have money to spend to buy shares anyway .

It 's only really noticeable for very heavy things like stars and planets .

You left you the all - important middle man that makes the entire thing possible : The computer itself . The computer draws the image , called a user interface , on the monitor by telling it which pixel ( tiny dots that make up your screen ) should be which color . Different parts of the image are associated with additional programming code that make them interactive when the user clicks on them or what have you . The positions of these things are tracked like things on that coordinate plane from Math Class ( X and Y axes representing sideways and up - down ) . All of this is done by the computer . The mouse sends movement information and button press information to the computer . The mouse moves in two axes interpreted as X and Y. It is worth noting that the mouse DOES NOT tell the computer what its position is . The mouse does not know where it is in relation to the screen ( if you pick up your mouse and move it , save for little hicks caused by lateral movement of the mouse while you pick it up and set it down triggering the movement detection , the cursor will not follow your movements nor " snap " to a spot on the screen ) .

The really like your five version : Your cars engine runs by mixing air and gasoline in a special chamber called a cylinder . And that 's really what it is , a hollow cylinder drilled out inside the main chunk of metal that is the engine . This chunk of metal is called the engine block . The number of cylinders in a given block varies , as well as how they are layed out . So when you hear someone say a V6 they mean the engine has 6 cylinders , and they are in a [ V - shape ] ( URL_0 ) . Inside the cylinder , there is a piston that slides up and down , and a set of valves . The piston fits very tightly in the cylinder and does n't let any air get by it . So , everything that goes into or out of the cylinder has to go through the valves . As the cylinder moves down , it pulls in air and fuel . Then the valves close , and the piston moves up . This squeezes the fuel and air mixture , which is ignited when the piston reaches the top of the cylinder . This burning of the fuel - air mixture pushes the piston back down with a lot of force . Then , once it reaches the bottom , a valve opens and the piston moves up , pushing the burnt fuel and air out of the cylinder .

Now yes , a politician is probably going to be influenced by big donors , but not always . If they do n't side with you , then you can decide not to donate again . But you ca n't ask for your money back , or threaten them because you paid them and they did n't do what you wanted . Thus the only incentive to side with you ( aside from your incredibly persuasive intellectual arguments ) is that you MAY donate to their campaign again . Oppositely , once you 've made a contribution , they have your money and can do what they please . You ca n't get it back . 2 ) The money is tracked . Campaigns are required to disclose who gave them money .

Back in the day , when music was primarily sold on physical media , you 'd often be able to buy just the one song ( usually with another song on the ' b - side ' ) on a record or cassette . When CD 's came out , CD singles would usually have remixes and whatnot . The record companies would only pick the songs that they thought would sell well and sell them as ' singles ' . These songs would be aggressively marketed to radio stations and , frequently , are the only songs you hear on the radio . While sales of physical media are down and almost nobody buys singles - if they want a single song , they 'll get it on iTunes - the business model is still the same . Certain tracks that have a wide potential appeal are promoted off a record . This makes sense , in a way , because the radio stations are only interested in playing music that a lot of people will like . The downside is that they 're not really giving people the opportunity to like other songs , creating somewhat of a feedback loop . The ' deep cut ' comes in when a station " digs deeper " into the album and plays something that was not released / promoted as a single .

Bias is your inclination to one side or the other when talking about a subject based on your experiences . Whenever you give an opinion , there will be some sort of bias involved . When a teacher says " Teachers should be paid more " , there is an amount of bias involved . Of course he thinks teachers should be paid more , he 's a teacher . But if a teacher can accurately list a set of pros and cons without letting the fact that he 's a teacher get in the way , and then conclude that yes , teachers should be paid more , then he is not being biased . Or at least , the bias has been reduced . It is extremely hard to talk about a subject without bias . This usually involves speaking using facts and facts only . Unfortunately , this is a problem because we all look at the world around us in terms of our own life experiences . For example , if I say the PC is a better gaming option , and only have a PC at home , then I 'm biased . I have not tested all the gaming options out there , all the consoles , etc and deduced , from all the facts , that the PC is the better option .
