Computers do n't necessarily " produce " 1 's and 0 's in the sense that they do n't manufacture them . Rather , they " present " hardware states that are interpreted as numbers . By state , I do n't mean a state like Texas , I mean a particular condition that a hardware piece is in at a specific time . For example , think of a light switch . It can be in either two states : up or down . For the sake of this example , consider up to be on , and down to be off . The state ( or condition ) of the switch is determined by the physical position of the switch . Now , flipping the switch does n't produce 1 's and 0 's , but we can interpret the position of the switch such that on=1 and off=0 . An item that can only have two states can be considered binary . In computers , a single binary unit is referred to as a bit . Multiple bits can be grouped together to store numbers larger than 1 . When this happens we are using base - two ( binary ) counting . When you count with your fingers , you 're essentially using base-10 ( decimal ) counting that you 're familiar with . A lot of mammals have a uterus shaped more like a V , or more precisely more like a Y. This allows eggs to implant along both arms of the Y , effectively increasing the surface area allotted for each zygote to implant and develop . Many mammals other than humans have a longer estrus period . During this time the female will discharge a smelly bloody fluid through the vagina that helps to signal fertility to males . During this period the female also will release multiple eggs over a longer course than humans . So even if a female gets all of her eggs fertilized at one point , a different male may come along a while later when more eggs have left the follicle and fertilize this new batch in addition to the already fertilized ones

OP is probably asking " what is the difference between an F double - sharp and a G natural ? " The idea that these would be the same note is derived from equal - tempered keyboards . For people who have full control over the pitch they produce ( e.g. string players ) , these are two different notes . In the key of C # , the G - natural is probably going to be properly interpreted as a G - sharp - flat ( a bit of notation which I do n't think is ever actually used ) , i.e. a leading tone to the dominant G - sharp as part of a modulation . On the other hand , an F - double - sharp would probably be a suspension to resolve down to the subdominant F - sharp . Accomplished string players will generally be mindful of such things and play different accidentals slightly differently according to context . A B - flat in one piece might mean something slightly different than a B - flat in another piece ( or even in a different place in the same piece ) .

It varies from campaign to campaign . It also varies in terms of robustness . Usually the best way of measuring the impact that an advertising campaign has is with a process called econometrics . Basically econometrics tracks a companies sales over time , usually a year or more , including the period their advertising ran . They then attempt to eliminate all other possible variables e.g. weather , distribution gains , seasonality , promotions so they can get to the point where the remaining uplift in sales is only attributable to the advertising . But econometrics is time consuming and expensive . You can use other methods . For example , if you ran advertising in one geographical area , but not another , and then compared the sales of those areas , if all other variables are equal then it must have been the advertising that was the difference . In short you try and use the principles of scientific method to eliminate the impact of all other variables to establish what impact your advertising has .

However , it can create pseudo - random numbers , which is basically a sequence of numbers generated from a seed number ( you may have heard of it in creating random maps in Age of Empires , etc . ) Having a seed is nice because it helps you reproduce a sequence ; you and your friend can both fire up AoE 2 map editor and put the same seed number in it , and get the same map . So basically the pseudo - random number generator ( PRNG ) is a function that takes a number and outputs a sequence . But here 's the nice part : For all practical intents and purposes , you can not distinguish a good PRNG from a true RNG . A possible definition for this is that if you are given the first n numbers of a PRNG sequence , you do n't gain a significant advantage in guessing the ( n+1)th number . Say that the PRNG generates 0 's and 1 's , and I 've given you that the first 8 bits are 00101010 . If the probability that you can guess the next bit correctly is not significantly larger than 50 % ( probability you will guess the bit correctly if the sequence was truly random ) , you 're good to go .

This is a handwavy explanation and a hard core physicist would find lots to object to , but I find that it gives an intuitive feel to the answer . OK its is important to note that time is only relative - e.g. if all the clocks in the universe slowed down by half , you would not notice anything ( because your clock has slowed too ) - there is no absolute time . Second - if one type of clock slows down then they all will ( more on that later ) . So lets look at a simple clock - say a light beam bouncing between two mirrors that are on a spacecraft are moving very fast ( close to light ) . Lets call the time taken for a light beam to make a round trip a " mirrsec " . If you are travelling with the mirrors then you will not see anything unusual . But if you are " stationary " looking into the spaceship then you will see something different . One half of the lights trip will be very fast , but the return trip will appear very slow as it is struggling to catch up with the mirror . The net effect is that you think that a " mirrsec " on the fast moving spacecraft takes a long time - e.g. their time has slowed compared to yours .

Keeping things ELI5 as much as possible : C4 has energy stored in the form of chemical bonds . Those bonds release energy in the form of heat when they are broken , in addition to converting the solid C4 into a gas ( which takes up a lot more space ) . If this happens all at once ( or at least very quickly ) , you get what you would define as an explosion : Lots of heat and pressure in a single small point , which expands very quickly as a shockwave . If this happens slowly , it 's more like a traditional fire : Heat and gas separate off of the burning mass at a rate ( which is actually controlled by how quickly the substrate heats up in the presence of its own fire ) . C4 does not require oxygen to burn so as it heats up the fire intensity will increase . So to answer your question , you have to understand that there are two ways to break the bonds in C4 . A significant impact ( ~~a bullet~~ apparently probably not a bullet , but definitely a priming charge ) will do the trick , and so will heat . The heat permeates the C4 slowly , resulting in a fire . The shockwave from a priming charge however permeates the entire mass very quickly , releasing all the bonds at once : Boom .

When you move a file to the Recycle bin , you 're not deleting the file , you 're removing it from the usable files . The computer still fully remembers the file , but sets it aside . When you empty the recycle bin , it still does n't delete the file . It simply " forgets " where the file was . This means that later on down the road , the place where the data was at will be overwritten . This is where defragmentation comes into play . When you hear that , it 's a process of reorganizing the data on your machine to have it fit properly and therefore be more easily accessed . Some programs such as CCleaner and DBAN have the ability to fully wipe drives by going through deleted files and copying " blank data " ( Random 1s and 0s ) over them over and over and re - wiping them , so if you tried to get access to the original files , at most you could only find the blank data .

This is going to be a long one . A clutch is designed to * slip * , and if you can imagine it , works similar to how a disc brake system works but in reverse . In a vehicle , a clutch is used to separate the engine from the transmission for a few purposes like gear changes and starting the damned thing . Why do we even * need * a clutch ? To protect the transmission and ( at times ) the engine . When you 're just driving around , the clutch is pressed against the flywheel of your engine and locked up onto it . This allows the engine and transmission to work as one unit , they 're both physically linked to each other . Step on the gas and you go . Easy . With the clutch in , you step on the gas and the engine roars but you go nowhere . Why ? The engine is disconnected from the transmission due to the clutch being disengaged . This is where things get tricky . Say you need to shift gears because you want to go faster . You press in the clutch and shift , then let the clutch out . What you did is separate the engine from the transmission , to unload the engine torque from the transmission . This allows an easier shift , and keeps your transmissions synchronizers happy .

The reasoning is this : The [ Articles of Confederation ] ( URL_0 ) , which were the governing rules of the United States before the Constitution existed , declared the Union to be " perpetual " - i.e. everlasting . The Articles of Confederation were replaced by the Constitution , and the Constitution does n't say anything like " perpetual " . However , it does say that its purpose ( in part ) is to make the Union more perfect . And the Articles of Confederation were not " the Union " ; the fact that they were replaced as the operating rules of the Union does not imply that the perpetual Union was replaced along with them . In fact the Articles themselves , along with saying * the Union * is perpetual , say that the Articles can be replaced . Lincoln claimed " the Union " actually predates even the Articles of Confederation . He said : > The Union is much older than the Constitution . It was formed , in fact , by the Articles of Association in 1774 . It was matured and continued by the Declaration of Independence in 1776 .

It 's not a sixth sense ; it 's one of your five senses . It 's your hearing . Even the most quiet room has small amounts of ambient noise ( in film , they even have a name for it , called " room tone " or " presence " ) . Our brains are evolved to detect the direction of sound and how it " wraps " around us . When someone is near you , their presence disrupts the subtle sound reflections , causing a stereophonic " hole " . The room tone will sound slightly different to each ear , having the brain sense something is there in that hole , with 3D precision . Bats use a more evolved version of this to see in the dark . They make chirps and hear the reflections to determine their surroundings . Blind people tapping their canes can " see " by using two senses : touch ( feeling the vibrations in the cane ) , and hearing ( noting the sound of the cane sound , but also how the reflected echo sounds ) . The first thing to note are the wooden planks between and perpendicular to the tracks . These are called " railroad ties " , or " sleepers " . The purpose of these ties is to transfer the weight of the train from the track and into the ground , and also to make sure that the train tracks are separated by a consistent and correct distance . The crushed rock is then called the " ballast " . The purpose of that is to receive the weight that 's transferred by the ties . Since they 're crushed rock , they can shift a little as the weight of the train comes in and passes . Since they 're crushed rock , they 'll also drain of water instead of retaining it .

You have essentially two kinds of rod when it comes to flexibility . Through action and tip action . In a through action rod the whole rod is flexible , in a tip action rod its usually only the top third which is flexible . In fly fishing through action rods are more common because they allow better roll and forward casting ( that s the back and forth one ) . Its also advantageous given the way the line and reel set ups work . A metal rod would be much heavier than current fibre glass or carbon based constructions . It would be bad for casting and would require line with a very high breaking strain . On the upside you could bully fish to your hearts content and just drag them to the side of the water ( which is not really a good thing to do ) . Although flexible it would take a lot , a lot , of strain to break a fishing rod . Usually the whippings on the ring seats go long before the rod itself would , and I 'm yet to break a whipping . The line will most likely break long before the whippings in any case . Course fishing is where you 'll more typically see tip action rods .

It 's basically the ( a ) " final step " in elementary physics . Everything we see today , every force , energy , reaction , can be narrowed down to 4 fundamental forces . Electromagnetism , Gravity , The Strong force , and The Weak force . Scientists are looking for ways to unify these into less forces . The electromagnetic + weak forces could be merged into the Electroweak force , for example . Then merge that one with the strong force , and eventually gravity for a Theory of Everything - which would basically " solve " the universe . It would answer any question of physics you might have - what was before big bang , what the hell big bang was , if there are many universes , how our universe will end , are there worm holes , etc etc . String Theory is a candidate for a Theory of Everything . String theory suggests that the fundamental building blocks of the universe are tiny strings , much much smaller than elementary particles and the quarks they are made of . These strings would vibrate at different frequencies , in 10 or 11 different dimensions , resulting in different particles and forces . Practically all high - end physics today involve string theory .

If you want to know what exactly complex numbers are , [ here is a comment I wrote about that a little while ago . ] ( URL_0 ) To understand what they are used for , you need to understand sort of how they work . A complex number has two parts : a * real * part and an * imaginary * part . So , in a way , a complex number is really * two * numbers . But those two numbers work together in such a way as to make it sensible to treat them as a single object , which we call a complex number . The usefulness to engineering comes from the weird way that complex numbers multiply together . The real numbers are one dimensional — that is to say , you only need one piece of information to pin down where a real number is on a number line . Multiplication between two real numbers can be thought of as stretching . That is , when I multiply a number by two , it stretches from looking like this \--------- to looking like this \------------------ For multiplication between complex numbers , we keep the " stretching " interpretation for the real part , but the imaginary part causes a * rotation * .

Capacitors are a sort of elastic barrier along a conductor . In the water pipe analogy , they would be like an elastic sheet that has been trapped between two pipe fittings ... it stops water from flowing , but with enough pressure you can stretch the elastic and get a little bit of movement - as soon as you relieve the pressure , the water flows backward until the elastic returns to neutral . They work just like an insulator , except instead of stopping flow completely , they impede flow by building voltage . Large capacitors work like batteries - you can " pressurize " electrons into them , and purposefully relieve that pressure ( voltage ) when it is needed . Smaller capacitors are useful components in oscillators , isolation circuits and noise filters . - You can get the elastic effect to oscillate by applying an AC current . - You can communicate pulses across the barrier , * moving * electrons , even though no electrons cross it . - You can absorb electrical noise , as the capacitor will absorb increases in outside voltage , and provide return voltage when the outside voltage drops .

I apologize for the length , it 's tough to turn medical jargon into a simple description and this is not a fully inclusive description or explanation . Allergies are the body going haywire to a normal part of the world . It is the immune system interpreting something that is normally harmless as a potential pathogen and trying to eliminate the danger by activating its defense system . This is called an allergen . The body " learns " what is an okay part of the environment and what is not , otherwise every food we eat would cause the immune system to react so hard it would kill us . Our bodies have special cells in the lining of the gut that samples the building blocks of what we eat and " teaches " our immune system not to freak out when it sees these later on . Still , there are backup mechanisms our bodies use to ensure that pathogens can not get by this one step so easily . What usually causes the problem in food allergies is that one of these backup systems triggers a response from one of our immune system cells .

To really understand the answer to this question , you need to have an idea of how graphics work in a video game . To start , graphics of a video game are constructed real time . In computer programming , this means that the graphics are calculated based off of the immense amount of data that the game is processing in the background every single frame . But what is a frame ? Think about those [ animation flip books ] ( URL_1 ) where each different page has the same scene , but slightly modified . Flip them really fast and you get the illusion of animation . This is basically what happens in video game code , where each different " page " is a frame . Each frame must be calculated by the computer 's hardware based on what has changed within the game world . This includes what input the user has given , as well what the program has determined should happen next . These calculations take time . The more advanced the graphics , the more time these calculations will take . This is where we hit a problem . In order to fool the brain into thinking it 's seeing continuous animation , the frames must be delivered to the monitor anywhere between 30 - 60 frames per second .

There are a few major differences - Typically a mutual fund is actively managed which results in larger fees than an ETF which is a passive instrument designed to track a benchmark ( say S & P 500 ) . You are paying a money manager to try to " underweight " or " overweight " the stocks he or she thinks will under / over perform in the applicable index . An ETF is simply designed to track the index , without a manager actively trying to generate alpha ( returns that exceed the benchmark return ) . Next is on tax efficiency - When you go to sell an ETF , since it is exchange traded , it 's basically like selling a stock . There are prices quoted throughout the day and you can sell it at any time for the quoted price . You can also sell ETF 's short , which you can not do with a mutual fund . ETF 's have " in kind " redemption which means that when you sell your shares , behind the scenes the basket of securities that comprise the ETF unit are exchanged to satisfy the sale . This differs from a mutual fund where when you place a sell the fund most sell underlying shares on the open market , resulting in a capital gains tax , that ultimately will flow through to the unitholders .

I 'm a pilot , not an aeronautical engineer , but I can tell you that flight like that is n't something you can sustain for very long . We are taught to think of vectors when taking turns . The airplane will generate more lift by flying straight and level and upright -- so think of an arrow pointing upward from the floor of the airplane representing its direction of lift . You can do things to make it longer , to generate more lift . You can use speed and deflection and adjust the wing chord . As you turn , you will always lose lift and the vertical component drops . So , we increase our angle of attack to maintain altitude . At a 30 degree bank , we have to pull bank as well as maintain the turn to keep level . At 60 degrees bank , you feel close to or around 2 G 's continuously . As you near 90 degrees bank , the airplane would not physically or mathematically be able to increase its lift enough to fly perfectly level . It is possible to use yaw to hold onto some lift , but even that wears off . It is possible to appear level and complete a major arc at 90 degrees , losing only a small amount of altitude , but it requires significant speed .

However , it is technically still possible to " claim " land that is not yours and eventually sell it . The process is called adverse possession . This probably is n't what your question is referring to , but it is interesting to note . It does n't require rampaging the land and killing all those who are on it . Rather , some states allow a person to takeover land if certain requirements are met . These requirements can vary from state to state , but generally , a person who wants to " claim " land has to have 1 ) actual possession 2 ) without the permission of the true owner , 3 ) be open and notorious about his use of the property ( i.e. the use must be visible to give notice to the legal owner who can make a claim against it ) , and 4 ) the use must be continuous for a defined period of time ( e.g. 20 years ) . If you can fulfill all of those requirements without the true owner taking it back or suing you , you can legally become the owner of that property . Like I said , it varies from state to state , and there are exceptions .

There are tubes called [ Eustachian tubes ] ( URL_1 ) that connect your nose / throat to your middle ear behind the eardrum . Often when the outside air pressure changes quickly ( driving down a mountain , descending in a plane , etc ) the tubes are held closed by the increased pressure . When you hold your nose closed and try to exhale , the air is forced into those tubes . The idea is to open up the tubes so air pressure can equalize between the outside world and the inside of your ear . Be careful when doing this though , because if you push to hard when trying to breathe out you can damage your ears . A multitasking operating system ( read : all modern operating systems ) normally only freeze when a privileged program is hogging all available resources for some reason . So what 's a " privileged program " ? A program that has been , for one reason or other , assigned special priorities . All things in multitasking operating systems are governed by a component called scheduler , which chooses what programs are running and how important they are . Most of the programs usually run on lower priority so they * should n't * be able to freeze anything at all , because the scheduler reserves some of the resources for really important things . But , for example , games and multimedia programs may request higher priority so that they get all juice they can . Likewise , the GUI is usually higher priority so that it can respond to user input . And here 's an important sidenote : device drivers are generally * really bloody important * . In many operating systems , if something goes wrong in a device driver , the operating system is going to have a really hard time coping with that .

Centuries ago , European farmers would seal the wood on their barns with an oil , often linseed oil - a tawny - colored oil derived from the seed of the flax plant . They would paint their barns with a linseed - oil mixture , often consisting of additions such as milk and lime . The combination produced a long - lasting paint that dried and hardened quickly . ( Today , linseed oil is sold in most home - improvement stores as a wood sealant ) . As for the red , there are two predominant theories : * Wealthy farmers added blood from a recent slaughter to the oil mixture . As the paint dried , it turned from a bright red to a darker , burnt red . * Farmers added ferrous oxide , otherwise known as rust , to the oil mixture . Rust was plentiful on farms and is a poison to many fungi , including mold and moss , which were known to grown on barns . These fungi would trap moisture in the wood , increasing decay . Regardless of how the farmer tinted his paint , having a red barn became a fashionable thing . They were a sharp contrast to the traditional white farmhouse . As European settlers crossed over to America , they brought with them the tradition of red barns .

The goal of your local parks and rec service is not only to build a park quickly , it 's also to be efficient with taxpayer money and avoid any type of misuse . Generation X were the children of the Baby Boomers . When Generation X grew up , the Baby Boomers , who made up the Woodstock generation , began to fear losing the limelight to a new group of people who were young , setting new trends , and moving popular culture in a different direction . So naturally , the Boomers sought to dismiss the up - and - comers by labeling them with an X , figuratively crossing them out . As Generation X began to have children , the Boomers who by now were middle - age , gleefully noticed that their children could also be labeled with a letter , the one following X in the alphabet . And so they were called Generation Y , as in " Why ? " , or " What 's the point ? " It was doubly satisfying to the Boomers because they could also say they held them in so little regard that they could n't be bothered coming up with any more original name than to use the letter following X. As Generation Z approaches , however , trouble lurks over the horizon . If you adopt the same convention of using letters , then after Generation Z you 'd either run out , or you 'd have to wrap - around and call them Generation A.

Tor has two functions : [ a ] it lets you browser the ( normal ) web anonymously by masking your IP address ; and [ b ] it lets you browse an exclusive deep - web network ( called the onion network ) which can only be accessed through the tor proxy service . Basically , the onion network is like a whole new web on top of the Internet that is exclusive to people running Tor . There are websites on the onion network that look and act just like other websites on the normal web , but which are completely hidden to users who are not running Tor . Who uses Tor ? Lots of people . People who value privacy . People who want to protect freedom of speech ... but also people who want to use the Internet for criminal activity . Because of the way Tor is designed , the network is completely anonymous . It is , for the most part , not possible to track which users access which websites on the onion network . This means that the network operates like the wild west with no concern for laws . For this reason , in some ways , Tor can provide a safe haven for criminal activity ( e.g. illegal drug trade , terrorism , child exploitation etc . ) .

Spoken language changes a lot more easily than written language . For example , English 's writing standard has its roots back around the 14th century - 600 - 700 years ago - and since then spoken English has changed a lot . Case in point : the silent * gh * in * night * was actually pronounced like German * ch * , and the * i * was pronounced like the * ee * in * seen * instead of the * ah - ee * sound it is now . As for those examples you have - all those words are taken from French , which has a very different spelling system to English . That does n't quite explain the pronunciations , though . More specifically : * colonel * was originally * coronel * and pronounced like that : the spelling changed to use an * l * due to the Italian * colonella * , but ultimately the old pronunciation kept . * lieutenant * is an odd case : no one knows for sure why it 's sometimes pronounced that way . There are cases of it being spelt like that back during the 14th century , so it 's not a new thing by any means . I 've never heard * envelope * like that , but I imagine that would be an attempt to mimic the way * enveloppe * is said in French , where * en * does sound somewhat like * on * .

Ratings have been around for a while , starting with radio in the 1920s . The numbers are estimates from the viewing logs of sample audiences , originally as paper diaries , today they 're collected with these : URL_0 . Nielsen is the oldest company in the space ; now it competes with Rentrak , comScore , Tivo and internet analytics companies like Adobe and Google . In the industry , you 'll commonly hear the term " shares " used . Shares are the percentage of homes using TVs ( HUTS ) , the percentage of TVs on that are tuned to a specific broadcast . Ratings are a percentage of viewers from the total amount of homes , including those that have their TVs off . Advertising costs are determined using the ratings in terms of CPM ( cost per thousand ) ; the cost of the ad divided by the share per thousand . They do n't yet directly affect ratings , but analytics from the internet are starting to play a big role . While more accurate , they pose a problem for companies that rely on the current model for cable revenue shares . You 're cable bill is currently divided up between the content providers ; ESPN for example is likely a big chunk of your bill .

If I understand your question correctly , basically you 're asking why you see shadows with night - vision enabled cameras as you would with a normal camera that had a regular light on it ? The answer is that night - vision enabled cameras use infrared light for filming . Our eyes can not see infrared light , but certain camera equipment can . Night - vision enabled cameras basically have an Infrared ( IR ) flash - light on them that is basically invisible to the naked eye but floods the area with IR light just as a normal flash - light would do with visible light . The IR light casts shadows just like how regular visible light would . The camera then simply translates the infrared light information into frequencies in the visible portion of the electromagnetic ( light ) spectrum that we can see . One problem with using the Infrared portion of the spectrum for recording video is that there are no colors associated with Infrared light , so when its translated to visible light we only get one color ( e.g. everything looks green ) . Note that there are also night - vision cameras which employ a different method of filming .

Gravity is technically not the same all the way to the ground . Near the surface of the earth , it 's around 9.8 meters per second , or 32 feet per second per second if you 're American . If you go up higher , it 's less , but the effect is generally negligible until you 're miles and miles up in the air . Anyway , that 's not what matters , really . Gravity is an * acceleration * ( force , technically ) , not a * velocity * ( speed , for our purposes ) . An acceleration is a change in velocity . For example , if your car goes from 0 mph to 10 mph in a second , it * accelerated * by 10 mph per second . Acceleration is caused by * force * . Force is , loosely , a " push . " When a force acts on a mass , it causes an acceleration . Weight ( ie pounds * ) is actually a measure of force , specifically the force due to gravity , which is why you weigh less on the Moon even though your mass is the same . When you push on something , you 're applying a force to it . You change its velocity , which is an acceleration . Similarly , gravity pushes ( really , pulls ) on everything with mass , so it is applying an acceleration .

Night vision in cameras and night vision in eyes aim for the same thing . In both cases , the goal is to widen the dynamic range available to view the environment . However , cameras and eyes work in very different ways . The he camera sets one exposure level for the entire scene , but each minute portion of the retina ( the eye 's " sensor " ) sets adaptation level independently . For example , suppose the scene has a small light at night . The camera will meter an entire photo ( normally at a number of points ) and the resulting average will probably be pretty dark . So the exposure or ISO are pumped up , which means any light in the picture will be over exposed , and noise is added . On a quick aside , ISO is basically the " volume " of the light hitting the sensor ; the circuit amplifies the light hitting it but as you amplify the digital signals interruption from radio waves , heat etc can make light be registered when it is n't even there . thus the random little dots . Meanwhile , the eye will measure 120million different points of the environment , sensing the amount of light available in each and exposing it accordingly .

Most touch screens with a hard surface , like on phones etc , use an effect known as ' capacitive coupling ' ( hence the name capacitive touch screen ) to sense a press . The surface of the panel forms a capacitor with your body and the circuitry senses this . It requires a slightly conductive pointer , hence why a hotdog will work but an insulating pen wo nt . A resistive touchscreen ( they are * slightly * squishy to press ) relies on physical pressure , so any pointer will work with them . Then there 's infra red touchscreens too , which line up a row of sensors and IR transmitters ( like a row of tiny versions of your TV remote ) along the edges of the screen and sense your finger blocking the light from travelling from one side to another . They can use anything that is n't transparent to work .

Pyrocumulonimbus clouds are clouds that form under a large fire like a wildfire , volcano or nuclear explosion that contain large amounts of particulate matter , i.e. dust . Because of the heat generated under these clouds due to the fires the Pyrocumulonimbus clouds can get up to 6 - 9 miles high where sunlight will help the dust rise even father up into the stratosphere . At this point there is nothing that nature can do for the dust to come down quickly . This dust will linger up in the stratosphere for years before it will fall . Active PA systems have the amplification built in to the speaker cabinets . Passive systems use an outboard amp . Actives can be thought of as being simpler , since you can get them bundled with a matched mixer and you 're ready out of the box . These systems are great for speeches , presentations and modest DJ gigs if you add a subwoofer . You can also get them separately and use them with as much sound processing gear as your heart desires . The built - in amp comes with a price , though . You will have to supply each monitor ( speaker ) with signal AND power cabling . Quality varies with price , but in general you 're paying for the convenience and ease of use . Passives require more gear to go with them , which drastically increases the amount of training required to use them . A mixer and amp are the bare minimum , but a simple rig can be less useful at higher power levels and in weirdly - shaped rooms , outdoors , etc . You really should also add some sound processing , which will require you to spend some time familiarizing yourself with some truly arcane knowledge .

Amps are a measure of electric current ( a measure of how much electricity is flowing through the wire ) , Volts are measure of Voltage or ' electric potential difference ' , and Watts are a measure of power . Power is calculated by Voltage ` x ` Current . So a device that uses 2 Amps when plugged into a 120 Volt electrical outlet uses 240 Watts of power . You can reorganize the equation to work out the other values . For example , you can calculate that a standard 60 Watt incandescent light - bulb must use 0.5 amps if it 's connected to a standard ( North American ) 120 Volt power system ( Current = Power / Voltage ) . When it comes to safety , both voltage and amperage are important . The human body can generally survive high voltage electric shocks so long as the amperage is low . For example , a ' taser ' may produce a 50,000 Volts shock that temporarily incapacitates someone , but the electric current is so low that the victim of the shock is unlikely to die . At the same time , an electrical outlet ( which has a much lower voltage ) definitely has the potential to electrocute you to death if you are not careful because of the much higher current .

It 's the * way in which it vibrates * that counts . Different sounds are made from different pitches and amplitudes . Pitch is determined by how fast the speaker vibrates , and amplitude is determined by how " hard " it vibrates . When your computer pumps music to your speakers , it is really pumping a voltage waveform . This waveform represents the sound of the music ( it 's what the music looks like on the computer , with the wavy lines ) . The waveform represents different sounds with changes in frequency ( pitch ) and amplitude ( loudness ) . Now , inside the speaker is the cone , a solenoid ( solenoids turn into magnets when current runs through them ) and a permanent magnet . When a voltage is applied to the solenoid , it becomes a magnet , the solenoid and permanent magnet move each other , and the cone ( attached to the solenoid ) moves . In fact , if you wanted , the computer could send a signal to the speaker that would make it move the cone once , then hold this position . Whatever voltage waveform is pumped to the speaker , the speaker will move accordingly .

People often refer to entropy as the " disorganization " of a system . I think this is somewhat misleading . Systems often evolve to be more * consistent * rather than * disorganized * . Entropy really involves probability . In statistical mechanics ( kinda like thermodynamics ) , a system is described by its * microstates * , the possible states the system can be in . Take , for example , a row of 5 boxes and 20 distinguishable balls ( assume any box can have any number of balls ) . A possible microstate is 20 balls in the 1st box ; another microstate may be 4 balls in each box . How many total microstates are there ? Well , each ball has 5 choices of box to be placed in . You have 20 balls , so the total number of microstates is 5 ^ 20 ( a huge number ) . Now let us * only consider microstates where all 20 balls are in the same box * ( i.e. , 20 in box 1 , 20 in box 2 , etc . ) There are only 5 of these microstates . What is the probability one of those microstates occurs ? That 's just 5/(5 ^ 20 ) ( about 0.0000000000005 % ) . Hopefully you can see this has low probability of happening , hence there is low entropy .

* * I originally posted this [ here ] ( URL_0 ) * * Well , let 's start with talking about cryptography for a bit , along with a bit of other vocabulary : * * * Symmetric Encryption * * - This is classical encryption the way most people think of it . A key is used to encrypt data , and then that same key can be used to decrypt it . * * * Asymmetric Encryption * * - Instead of a single key , you 're dealing with a pair of two keys . One key is used for encryption ( called the public key ) , and the other is used for decryption ( called the private key ) . An example may help : You see a balloon rise into the air . There are two possible explanations ( actually more , but we only need two to demonstrate ) ; 1 ) balloons are less dense than air and therefore rise or 2 ) a wizard is levitating the balloon . In order to accept hypothesis 1 , all we need to assume is true is that the balloon is less dense than the air . ( We can prove this experimentally , but for the Razor argument we do n't need to . ) In order to accept hypothesis 2 , we would need to assume that there is a wizard , which means assuming that magic is real , which means that all of the observed laws of physics align with reality for some whimsical reason other than necessity . Hypothesis 1 requires one small assumption , Hypothesis 2 requires 3 large assumptions . Therefore , if we ca n't test either hypothesis directly , we should go with Hypothesis 2 .

To understand it , first you have to understand escape velocity . If you throw a ball straight up , depending on the velocity the ball it has some velocity . It will be dragged on by the gravity of the Earth to slow it down and eventually it will stop and then fall back . However , the farther the ball gets from Earth , the weaker the gravity . If you throw the ball fast enough ( faster than you can throw ) gravity will get weaker faster than it can slow down the ball and in that case , the ball will never stop and fall back , it will just get slower and slower and slower forever . The minimum speed to achieve this from some distance from a gravity well is the escape velocity . The stronger the gravity , the faster the escape velocity . We already had evidence for super - dense stars which we would later call neutron stars . The question just became , what would happen if a star was so heavy and so dense that the escape velocity from its surface was greater than the speed of light ? Even light would be unable to achieve escape velocity , so anything which passed this ' event horizon ' would be lost from the rest of the universe forever .

Eels create electricity the same way we do , just to a much higher level . Take our neurons for example , you have your cell membrane which forms a sort of insulation barrier where charges can build up . The membrane has certain proteins inserted throughout that serve as pumps or channels for ions to cross . An important one is the Na / K pump . This pumps out 3 Na+ for 2K+ . The uneven pumping of positive ions creates a negative charge inside and the large ( - ) ions can not cross the membrane . At rest , our neurons are mostly around -70mV. We can then open different channels and create a movement of electrical charge when different ions flood in or out of the cell . This is how we fire our neurons . Eels do this , but basically to a much larger extent . They have tons of cells packed with mitochondria to create the energy to pump these ions and hold a charge . Then , when they want , they can release the charge of multiple cells all at once to create a powerful discharge . The Pythagorean theorem states that the square of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is equal to the square of one leg plus the square of the other leg . So , let 's get some definitions in place . Right triangle = A triangle with a right angle ( 90 degrees ) , just like the corner of a square . Hypotenuse = The longest side of the triangle , the one opposite the right angle . Leg = One of the two smaller sides of the triangle . Square = A number multiplied my itself . In this case , we multiply the distance of a side of the triangle by itself . The Pythagorean theorem is often shortened to a^2 + b^2 = c^2 a is the length of one of the smaller sides , b is the length of the other small side , and c is the length of the longest side , the one opposite the right angle . A common example is a right triangle with side lengths of 3 , 4 , and 5 . 3 ^ 2 + 4 ^ 2 = 5 ^ 2 3X3 + 4X4 = 5X5 9 + 16 + 25 The Pythagorean theorem is really useful for finding the side lengths of a right triangle ; if you know two sides , you can find the third . It is also the basis of more complex geometric laws , since any polygon can be divided into multiple triangles .

What is it ? It 's an organic molecule unique to living things . Both eukaryotes ( complex - celled beings like plants and animals ) and prokaryotes ( simple celled like bacteria ) possess double stranded DNA as their genetic material i.e. their material for storing information of how to operate and create progeny . Where is it found ? The center of the cell . Prokaryotes have a " nucleoid " region where their DNA is kept compressed and eukaryotes have a nucleus , which is a walled organelle believed by many to be created by a eukaryote ingesting a prokaryote cell . What does it do ? It 's a cookbook for making proteins . The process goes DNA - > RNA - > Protein . This allows cells to keep their DNA unmodified , but create different proteins . Your cookbook is protected in the nucleus / nucleoid . If you want to make a protein you go to the gene and make a copy in the form of RNA and RNA can be modified if needed to make a unique protein of that type . Think about any recipe you may know ; sometimes you add more sugar maybe , or leave out a teaspoon of salt - this occurs in your cells sometimes .

Social darwinism is an attempt to use Darwin 's idea of natural selection , or " the survival of the fittest , " to explain or , in my experience usually * justify * , the mistreatment of one group of humans by another . In normal polite discourse , it is almost never a good thing to be accused of being a Social Darwinist . Social Darwinism has an ugly history of being used to justify mistreatment of groups of people and even genocide . People who may subscribe to some ideas of Social Darwinism usually do n't like to use the term because of the ugly connotations . Here 's an example : why are some people poor ? The Social Darwinist would say some people are poor because they are dumber , lazier , or otherwise not as capable of competing with smarter , harder working , * richer * people . Similar to how natural selection causes less fit types of organisms get outcompeted by more fit ones , the Social Darwinist would believe that poor people will over time be removed from the gene pool because they can not compete with the people who are more fit . Basically , survival of the fittest for humans . Here 's where it gets really ugly .

Hedge funds and Mutual funds are " pooled " investments among many investors . You buy a share of these investments , and receive gains or losses proportional to the money you invest . Depending on the fund , this pooled money will be invested exclusively in stock , bonds or commodities , or a combination of all of them . A Mutual fund will be very explicit about what it can and ca n't invest in . A Hedge fund wo n't . Mutual funds are regulated , traded on an exchange , are very liquid ( easily bought or sold ) , and are usually very well described as to what their investment strategy is . The company who manages the fund can advertise to attract new investors . They are required to publish their investment holdings within the fund frequently . The numbers before mm = focal length , the fact that there are two indicates that this is a zoom lens . It is always a ratio to the focal length . A small number ie f/1.4 is a big hole which lets in lots of light . A big number ie f/22 is a small hole which lets in not that much light . As indicated before , since this is the maximum aperture , the lens is actually capable of something like f/4 - f/22 . f/4 being the most light the lens can let in . As a side note , aperture controls how much is in focus . at f/1.4 ( big hole ) there is only a small distance set which is in ' acceptable ' focus . at f/22 ( small hole ) there is a large distance which is ' acceptable ' focus . ( Full disclosure : I 'm not terribly knowledgeable about engine design and the numbers were just pulled from quick Google searches , but I hope this helps ) There are a lot of factors including engine design , suspension , handling , etc . etc . etc . that determine whether a car will " out perform " another on a given course ( dragstrip , autocross , etc . ) , but the biggest one if you 're considering small vs. large cars is the power to weight ratio . A Honda Civic Coupe ( 1.8L , or 1800cc ) making 140 horsepower will do 0 - 60 in 9.1 seconds . It has an 1800cc engine , but weighs 2700 pounds . That 's a power ( HP ) to weight ratio of around 103 horsepower per ton . It has a sizable engine , but it 's moving a lot of weight . A Honda CBR1000RR motorcycle ( 1000cc engine ) making 178 horsepower will do 0 - 60 in 2.9 seconds . It has a 1000cc engine , but weighs only ~430 pounds . That means it has a power to weight ratio of 827 horsepower per ton , around eight times that of the Civic . Even though the engine is significantly smaller , it 's moving much less weight and so it can do so faster .

A black object , in day - to - day life , is one that absorbs * most * of the light that hits it , and all of the colors of light in pretty much equal proportions . It reflects back some light ( otherwise it 'd be invisible ) but very little . Theoretically , a special kind of object called a * blackbody * would absorb * all * the light that falls on it and reflect none , emitting light only in proportion to its temperature . But such an object is n't the kind of thing you can just stumble over . You can build one , if you 're very careful , by constructing a box made out of platinum , dividing up its interior with baffles and coating them with iron oxide . Put a hole in the box , and that hole will act like a blackbody . It wo n't reflect any light ; all the light you shine into the hole will end up scattered and absorbed by the box 's interior . But you can make things that are what the nerds call * near - black * pretty easily . There are tons of widely available near - black pigments . Carbon 's the most common , usually in the form of charcoal . Black ink can be made from nothing but charcoal and water , for example .

Car batteries ( conventional lead - acid batteries ) have shrunk , actually . At one time batteries had thick glass cases and used solid lead plates suspended in acid ; they were extremely heavy and reliable . We call batteries like that " marine " or " deep cycle " batteries today . They were design - optimized for producing steady lower rates of current and they can have much of their capacity discharged without damage . Nowadays they have plastic cases so they 've gotten a little lighter but deep - cycle batteries are basically the same as they were in the early 20th century . But somebody figured out that if the lead plates in the battery had more surface area , all other things being equal , a battery could discharge far more amperage in a shorter period of time . They developed ways to make battery plates that were " foamed " instead of solid lead , so they weigh less but have far more surface area . These batteries were ideal for starting cars , which requires a huge jolt of amperage all at once but no significant demand after the car is running .

A mortgage is when somebody else owns a house and you want to buy it , so you go to a bank and borrow the money . As part of the deal , the bank retains a limited ownership claim on the house until the loan 's paid off . If you fail to pay the loan back on time , the bank can take possession of the house and sell it to cover their losses . A * reverse * mortgage is where * you * own a house , and you want to borrow money to do something else . So you go to a bank and offer to * give them * a limited ownership claim in your house in exchange for borrowing their money . You then take the money borrowed and spend it , and repay the loan over time . If you fail to repay it on time , the bank can take possession of your house and sell it to cover their losses . It 's actually quite a bit more complex than that , with regard to interest capitalization and whatnot , but that 's the gist of it . Basically reverse mortgages are really bad ideas for the borrower in almost all situations . They should be thought of as a kind of loan - of - last - resort . If you ca n't get the capital you need in any other way , you can pay the excessively large price to get it with a reverse mortgage .

Conditions that have more biological causes to not mean that it does not count as a ' mental illness ' as the person 's cognitive processes are affected . The cause of a disorder is usually most pertinent when discussing treatment , however , not classifications . Personality disorders are difficult for many reasons , but it is correct for them to be in the DSM . They have specific markers and occur often enough that there is a definite trend , and most of them qualify for all four of the D 's . It is n't necessarily an allergy as much as it is a contact dermatitis . In order to be an allergy , the reaction would need to be mediated ( caused by ) a particular type of antibody : IgE. These are called a type I hypersensitivity . Contact dermatitis is an example of a type IV hypersensitivity , but is not an allergy . This can also be called a delayed type hypersensitivity because it requires different mediators ( such as T cells ) that will take longer for you to see the effects . Now , to answer your question . Many times , metal molecules will mix with proteins present on the skin to form what is called a hapten . Immune cells recognize this molecule as not being " self , " ( a healthy immune system will only target foreign thugs , for the most part ) , and begin to send chemicals into the blood that will cause more fluid to leak into the skin areas and bring other immune cells to attack the hapten . This causes the dermatitis that you notice . Super simplified : it is caused by a type IV hypersensitivity in which your immune system will target something that is n't necessarily harmful , but not an allergy because it is not IgE mediated .

With television and movies , it 's because of the frame rate . The Nyqyist - Shannon Sampling Theorem states that to accurately sample an oscillating object , you need to sample it at twice the frequency it 's oscillating at . As an example , let 's say I have a regular 12 hour clock . If I want to watch it with a video camera , in order to accurately see what it 's doing , I need to take a frame more often than every 6 hours . Let 's say I take a frame every 5 . First frame is 12 o'clock , next is 5 o'clock , next is 10 o'clock , next is 3 o'clock , next is 8 o'clock , and so on . The clock is moving forward normally in my video . However , let 's say that I only take a frame every 7 hours , which is n't fast enough according to the theorem . First frame is 12 o'clock , second frame is 7 o'clock , third frame is 2 o'clock , fourth frame is 9 o'clock . Because I 'm not sampling fast enough , instead of appearing to move forward 7 positions in 7 hours , it actually appears to be moving backward 5 positions in 7 hours . Video cameras record at a constant frame rate , so that 's why you 'll see wheels do really weird stuff in videos .

Water freezes at 0 ° C . ( Or close to it , depending on the other stuff dissolved in the water . ) Ethanol stays a liquid down to – 114 ° C . Your freezer does n't get anywhere near that cold . So if you put pure ethanol in the freezer , it would never solidify . Liquors are not pure ethanol . They 're a mixture of ethanol and water ( and some trace compounds ) , usually in around a 40/60 ratio . That is , by mass 40 % of the mixture is ethanol and 60 % is water . Water freezes into ice through a process called * crystallization . * That is , crystals of water molecules form , taking the water from a liquid to a solid state . But when ethanol is mixed with the water , the ethanol molecules get * in between * the water molecules and prevent crystallization from happening except on very small scales . That 's why when you put a bottle of liquor in your freezer , it often * thickens * somewhat . It 's because the water in the bottle has crystallized , but the ethanol has gotten in the way , preventing the water from forming macroscopic crystals . So you end up with microscopic ice crystals suspended in an ethanol matrix , and that behaves like a viscous liquid .

Difference : C++ and C are a layer on top of the assembler , so you can know exactly what assembly code you 'll get when writing . This means maximum possible perf ( in the hands of experts ) and maximum possible security ( because there are less possible exploits in between you and the CPU , again in the hands of experts ) . Java is a language that is quite similar in syntax ( looks similar ) but is actually interpreted by a virtual machine-- which then converts the interpreted code into assembly ( on any platform the VM supports ! ) , so you * do n't * know what assembly you 'll get . Implications : If you 're writing system level code that has to be fast , C / C++ . If you want something to run on the web , or on many devices , and you do n't care that much about performance ( or security ) , obviously use Java . You 're less likely to be hassled by system specific bugs . If you 're not an expert in low level programming and do n't want to become one , choose Java . Data on a hard drive does n't actually take up physical space . When you save your 1Gb file , your hard drive actually sets billions and billions of extremely tiny magnets to different positions ( each representing either a " 1 " or a " 0 " ) , and then it creates a little " index card " to say that " all of the data between position X and position Y is being used for a file called ' mine.doc ' " . When you delete it , two things happen : First of all the " index card " is removed , but the billions of little magnets do n't change . That 's why you can do an undelete if you do so straight away -- all you need to do is recreate the index card and everything 's OK . Later on , if you save other things to the disk , the computer will say " OK , I can see there 's no index card telling me something 's stored between X and Y , so I guess I 'm free to use that space for saving something else " . It then sets the relevant magnets and so it overwrites some ( or all ) of your old file . So the data does n't " go " anywhere , because it never really existed in the first place . All that happens is some extremelly small magnets change direction !

Radiation is a broad term used to describe things that ' radiate ' from a source . Most people are familiar with X - rays . This is a type of radiation known as electromagnetic radiation , or gamma radiation ( not to be confused with gamma rays , which are a specific type of gamma radiation ) . Radiowave , microwaves , and visible light are also gamma radiation . There are other types of radiation . Alpha , Beta , and neutron radiation are probably the most commonly known . Alpha radiation is basically high energy helium nuclei ( helium atoms without the electrons ) . They move very , very fast , and can cause damage to things when they collide with them . The are positively charged . Beta radiation is electrons / positrons being radiated . Positrons ( positively charged electron anti - particles ) usually annihilate quickly , and send off gamma radiation afterwards . Electrons can travel for awhile , however . They are negatively charged . Neutron radiation is where a source radiates neutrons . Neutrons are particles that have no charge , so they can travel for quite a ways in normal circumstances .

Most web content follows a standard set of rules , called web standards to tell the browser what the content is , and how it should look . Every browser runs on a layout engine . They also use a Javascript engine , which interprets code the web site sends to your browser to run . This uses another set of standards that browsers follow . Internet Explorer , due to Microsoft being a very proprietary company , decided that they would create their own proprietary standards , and web content would need to conform to them to look good in their browser . So for a long time there was a set of rules for good browsers , and a set of rules for IE . So basically everyone hated IE for making them maintain two sets of code . Also , their were looooots of bugs in earlier versions of IE , where , even if you followed the rules , things would be rendered incorrectly , frustrating developers even more .

When you write a piece of software , you basically are making a list of instructions for a calculator to perform . You have your operations : You can Add , Subtract , Multiply , Divide , or MOD ( Obtain the remainder of a division ) , two numbers . ( There are also lots of operations that modify the bits inside of these numbers , that are useful for talking to hardware , or optimizing certain operations ) You then have control pieces : A mechanism to LOAD , STORE , GOTO , IF , BRANCH IF 0 , and you can do a lot of complicated things . A machine that can do this basic set of things is known as being Turing Complete . Pretty much anything that can be algorithmically represented or modeled , can be modeled with a Turing Complete machine-- this includes video games . Doing so at a low level is really difficult though- so people made programming languages , which can use simpler terms , and then generate a bunch of the above listed instructions which accomplish the same thing . Computers then need to talk to hardware . In the early days it was just TTYs , basically terminals that you could communicate with via serial .

For the same reason it does n't stop rotating : the conservation of angular momentum . See , the whole solar system formed out of a vast cloud of what was essentially dust and gas . That cloud was made up of * particles , * many as small as individual molecules , some rare ones perhaps as large as a grain of sand . Because the cloud was incredibly sparse — it would be considered a hard vacuum in any laboratory — the particles were essentially on free trajectories . They did n't interact much . Each one moved through space in its own direction and with its own momentum . But over time , the cloud began to collapse under its own weight . Nobody knows for sure why . It could 've been a spontaneous thing , or it could 've been provoked by the shockwave of a nearby supernova or something . Whatever the cause , the cloud began to fall into itself . But each individual particle still had its own momentum . Very few of these particles were either moving straight toward or straight away from the cloud 's center of mass . Most were moving at some angle to it . That means that each particle had , relative to the cloud 's center of mass , some angular momentum .

Harmonic series . Essentially , sounds are waves . Sometimes , two different wavelength waves can overlap in such a way that they line up somehow . This sound comes off as naturally harmonious to us . Say you have two sounds . One has half the length of the other , and so fits inside the other twice nice and snugly . The two sounds are an octave apart , with the shorter wavelength being higher . If two wavelengths of one sound line up with three wavelengths of another , the sounds are a fifth apart . If it 's 3:4 , it 's a fourth . These sounds are still harmonious to us even though not as much as the octave sound . This is why they are ' perfect fifths ' and ' perfect fourths ' . 4:5 gives us a major third , 5:6 gives us a minor third , 6:7 gives us something between a minor third and a major second ( which we usually approximate to a minor third ) and 7:8 does the same ( which we usually approximate to a major second ) . Beyond that the intervals are no longer really harmonious enough for our ears to pick them up , and they just sound clashy . So because a minor third is more clashy than a major third , we perceive it as a little more off and this can translate into sad .

There is a fair bit of debate about but for the most part it looks like it 's a combination of nature ( genetics ) vs nuture ( How you were raised ) . As an example consider your height ( not personality I know , but run with it ) . You had a tall dad and a tall mum , genetics has given you a blueprint for being tall . However , you were malnourished as a child and as a result you ended out an average height - it was a compromise between your genetics and the environment you grew up in . It 's likely you will never be short , and you will probably be a bit taller than usual , but you wo n't be as tall as the blueprint said . The same goes for someone who has the blueprint for short - they could have the best diet in the world , but at best they will be average and they will never be tall . This is how we get a mathematical ' normal ' curve of heights . If genes were the only forces at play we would expect to see distinct ' height ' catagories - we do n't so we know there is something else at work . Now lets look at personality . There are many studies out there in animals that say certain ' personailty ' traits , called in this case behavioural syndromes , are inherited .

The simple answer is that x^n * x^(-n ) = x^(n - n ) = x^0 = 1 because x^n * x^(-n ) = x^(n)/x^(n ) But that 's sort of circular , because it relies on using the rules of exponent multiplication and division ; I 'm proving that x^0 = 1 by assuming that x^0 = 1 . The fancier and more rigorous way of showing it is by using * sets * . A set is a grouping of mathematical objects , in this case numbers . So , for example , { 1 , 2 , 3 } is a set that contains the numbers 1 , 2 , and 3 . We can define exponents by using an operation called " prod , " short for " product . " It 's defined like so : prod{1 , 2 , 3 } = 1 x 2 x 3 = 6 So , it 's just the product of all the stuff inside the set . To define an exponent , then , we can just do something like 3 ^ 3 = prod{3 , 3 , 3 } = 3 x 3 x 3 = 27 or , more generally , x^n = prod{x , x , x , ... , x } , where there are n x 's inside the set ( curly brackets ) . So , what 's x^(0 ) with our new fancy definition ? Well , there should be zero x 's inside the brackets , so x^0 = prod { } which is called the " empty product , " because " { } " is the " empty set .

I 'll give it a shot at a scientific explanation . Studies have shown that the brains of extroverts and introverts are different . Introverts are found to be more sensitive to dopamine release than extroverts . They tend to pay attention to small things and so details will usually stimulate introverts just as much as a new changing things . Because of the sensitivity to dopamine , prolonged exposure to it is mentally draining and highly stimulating places will overload introverts . You can liken it to standing next to the heater on a cold day . a small heater is nice . It feels really good at first . with more stimuli more heaters are added and it gets comfortable . With even more stimuli it 's like you 're surrounded by heaters and it becomes unbearable and you just need to get away because you ca n't stand the heat any more . It 's mentally exhausting to be in a place where there is too much stimuli for a prolonged period of time . The need to get away ( recharge ) that introverts feel is the need for their brain to rest from all the dopamine released . They can enjoy social situations just as much as anybody can but it 's the duration that makes the difference .

Hash functions produce a hash with a fixed length , so there are a finite amount of hash values . But inputs can be of any length , so there are an infinite amount of them that result in each hash value . I ca n't automatically work backwards from a hash to an input , because which of the infinite inputs should I work backwards to ? To end up with a fixed - size output , hash functions mix the incoming bits into the fixed sized state , overwriting what is there . They do this with operations like " xor " , which are not reversible .

The reason is that your urine is based on your blood filtering through your kidneys . This is a constant process , so you are always producing urine which needs to be emptied . Pretty much any time , day or night , if you said to yourself " I am going to go pee , even though I do n't need to , " you would manage to pee at least something . Your stool , unlike your urine , is based on the food that you eat . You eat food in short time segments , in between which are long periods of not - eating . The food you eat has a VERY long path to travel from your mouth to your bowel , so long that when you pass stool , it is probably from food you ate the day before . Since food passes through your digestive tract slowly , the individual food - remains stay separated , and the urge to pass each stool only arises when the fecal matter comes into the area of the anal sphincter , which your brain interprets as a need to use the toilet . The release of stool and the release of urine both require relaxing sphincters in your pelvic region . So when you need to poo , it is simply convenient also to pee ( as you are pretty much guaranteed to have urine waiting to be expelled ) .

Imagine dragging that dot in a particular direction , and it traces out a line segment of length ` s ` . Now we have a line . Let 's grab that line and drag it in a direction that is perpendicular to the direction we dragged the dot . As we do that , let the points at each end of the line trace out two more lines of length ` s ` . There you have it , a square ! Ok , now can we follow that same process again ? You bet ! Grab the square , and drag it in a direction perpendicular to * both * directions we 've used so far . Let each corner of the square trace out 4 more lines of length ` s ` . Now we have a cube . If I fire a bullet perfectly horizontal to the ground , it will go a long ways but then eventually fall to the ground . If I use a higher power rifle that shoots bullets faster , it 'll go farther before hitting the ground . Now , the earth is n't flat -- what if I had a gun powerful enough that by the time it had fallen 1 inch , it had gone far enough horizontally that the curvature of the earth had caused the ground to " drop out " by exactly an inch ? They key to understanding live vaccines , as with so many things in biology , comes down to evolution . Take a nasty human virus , like mumps . This thing is well adapted to infecting and wreaking havoc on human tissues . Now expose a bunch of non - human tissue culture cells in a laboratory to mumps . Mumps is n't so great at infecting these , so it grows pretty poorly . However , some of the viruses will contain mutations that allow them to grow better than the others in the non - human animal tissue . These guys will have a selective advantage in replication ! Keep doing this for multiple " generations " of viruses . As you keep cultivating these viruses in non - human cell lines , you are basically exerting artificial selection for viruses that infect non - human cells really well . You 're forcing the lab strain of virus to evolve down the road away from specializing in human infection . Now let 's take a sample of that laboratory virus . It 's still alive , but it has specialized in infecting some tissue other than human cells . They still produce an infection in humans , just really poorly .

The vast majority fulfil one of several fraudulent roles : * DDoS : Your computer is opened up to receive attack requests , in which it will join a larger effort to drive massive traffic at a server to prevent it from responding to legitimate queries . * Spam : Your computer is opened up to send out spam emails , covering the identity of the origin of the message . * Trojan / Rootkit : Usually a more script - kiddie oriented virus , it is usually used to pester or torment the user needlessly . The reason that your key fob does n't open other cars is because the chip inside your fob and the receiver in your car are programmed using the same pseudo - random number generator . The keyless entry system works by transmitting a 40 - bit code to the receiver in your car . If it receives the expected 40 - bit code , the car will unlock . If not , it does nothing . Each time the key is pressed , it chooses the next number in the sequence . Each time the receiver receives a 40 - bit code , it also chooses the next ( since they are programmed using the same generator , they should , in theory , be picking the same 40 - bit code ) thus the fob and receiver are normally " synced up " . Obviously if you 're pressing your fob while out of range of your receiver , the fob and receiver will be out of sync . To compensate , the receiver actually will accept any of the next 256 expected 40 - bit codes , so you could " accidentally " press your fob 256 times while out of range and your car will still unlock on the 256th time .

This was just asked , but here 's my answer : When people sing , they drop a lot of consonants . Singing is done with the mouth wide open , and consonants are sounds that involve blocking the air passage at some point , which limits how loud you can sing . We 're smart , so we add in the missing sounds subconsciously , and we tend to insert the sounds we would use ourselves . It 's the same reason why a song can be nonsense until you look up the lyrics and why John Fogerty can say " there 's a bad moon on the rise " and " there 's a bathroom on the right " at the same time . He 's not actually singing either , just the vowels and the first letters mostly . There are some exceptions . American southern accents and Irish accents make their vowels a bit nasal - y , which is often noticeable when they sing . Folk singers often sing with more consonants in tact , because they do n't need to open their mouths up wide and sing loud like an opera singer would ( especially before electricity and microphones ) . Bing Crosby was famous for using newer recording techniques to capture a softer , more spoken singing style , and Bob Dylan later did the same thing with folk rock .

' Stopped responding ' means a lot of different things . Programs crashing and freezing happen because there is some sort of unhandled exception that happened . For example if your program is waiting for an input while it 's also waiting to draw some text , and neither of those can finish because they 're both waiting for the other , then the program eventually crashes . Specifically not responding is your operating systems way of saying ' I 'm sending messages to the program and not getting the correct response ' . Those messages range from keyboard input , to allocating memory for something to trying to reserve access to a device . There are a LOT of things going on in even very basic programs if they spawn windows and have menus and so on . The thing is : sometimes the operating system is just not waiting long enough , and the program will respond . Think of it like this . You want to create a window . So you send a message to the windowing system saying ' create me a window 1024x768 ' . The windowing system sends back ' ok I created it , here 's where to find it ' ( a * pointer * to the object ) , and then it waits for the program to say ' got it thanks ' .

Pilgrims is a word referring to people who go on a long journey for religious reasons . Puritans were a subgroup of European Christians who had a different philosophy about how to practice Christianity than those in power at the time . So , some groups of puritans organized voyages to settle in " the new world " , where they could run their own affairs and practice religion the way they thought it should be done . Since they were going on a long voyage for religious reasons , you could call them pilgrims , so that 's how those settlers got the name " the Pilgrims " . Plymouth was the first colony founded by puritan pilgrims from Europe . They were scrappy and relatively poor and did it for their idea of religious purity . Several years later , a much wealthier group of puritans came over and founded Massachusetts . Later on , those two colonies merged .

Often these companies are bailed out to avoid the spread of a financial contagion throughout the economic landscape . To understand this , think of a company ( Company A ) worth in total $ 100Bn . Now unless Company A was extremely conservative in its borrowing , and had been over the vast majority of its life , a large part of this $ 100bn would likely be made up of debt , i.e. money it has borrowed from various sources like banks , hedge funds , other companies and so on ; the remainder of the companies value would be , by definition , made up of equity financing , i.e. money raised by the sale of shares / reinvestment of retained profit . Let us now assume that the ratio of debt to equity of 2:1 - for every $ 1 of equity they have $ 2 of debt . Now , what this means is that company A owes approx . $ 66bn to various sources . To these ' sources ' , this $ 66bn represents an asset - they will eventually receive this money back , and will earn interest on it in the interim . These expected cash flows from this repayment will subsequently be incorporated into the value of these ' sources ' .

Redlines are arbitrary figures worked out by engineers and possibly tweaked at times by the marketing people . ( A higher redline might seem sexier to a young male customer ) You can throw a rod ( catastrophically break a connecting rod ) at any RPM , but the statistical likelihood that it will occur increases with RPMs . Engines wear out eventually , regardless of RPMs , but they wear out much faster if the average RPM is higher . There is also the question of torque and horsepower . Horsepower = torque X RPM . In theory , more RPMs mean more horsepower , which is why racing engines run at much higher RPMs . That 's also why they wear out faster and sometimes blow up during races . There is an RPM point at which any piston engine will start to lose torque . Beyond that point , more RPMs produce less horsepower , not more . The most common reason would be valve " float . " The valves can not open and close fast enough to keep up with the engine rotation . Before they snap closed , the cam is starting to push them open again . The engine will sputter and falter . Stronger valve springs and lighter valves make higher RPM limits possible . These are used in racing engines .

You ever heard of the Schrodinger 's Cat thought experiment ? It 's like that , but from the cat 's point of view . I 'll explain the Schrodinger 's Cat thought experiment and everything else in more detail : it basically describes what would happen if you put a " cat " ( basically a metaphor for a quantum system ) into a box in a way that would not allow you to observe it , along with a bottle of poison rigged to break when a detector observes an electron and finds that it has a certain spin ( a completely random quantum event ) . If the detector does n't trigger the poison , it 'll try again after an arbitrary length of time ( for the sake of argument , let 's say it does this once every second ) . Now , from the outside , the cat is both alive and dead until the box is opened . In other words , it is in a superposition of alive and dead , and that cat 's wavefunction will collapse upon the opening of the box , making it either alive or dead . That 's what the Schrodinger 's Cat experiment is .

Working out your body really hard creates a buildup of lactic acid in your blood and muscles . Basically , you work so hard that you deprive oxygen to your tissues and they start doing what 's called anaerobic metabolism . Anaerobic metabolism allows your body to making energy with limited oxygen , but it also creates a byproduct called Lactic Acid . All that lactic acid can make your blood acidotic ( as compared to basic ) . Acid is also in your stomach . By throwing up , you purge some of the acid in your body , and it helps relieve the acid / base imbalance created by anaerobic exercise .
