If you heat iron to about 900 degC ( dependant on purity ) it will switch the way its atoms are arranged . When you cool the iron back down again , it tries to switch back . Now , if you put some carbon into the iron ( making it a steel ) , the iron gets a bit of a problem when trying to switch back during cooling . The iron now wants to reject almost all of that carbon , preferably by making small carbide plates or particles . When cooling is too rapid however , the iron does n't get the time to do this , and thus forms what is known as [ martensite ] ( URL_1 ) instead . All of that excess carbon is now trapped inside a rather distorted structure , which will be more or less hard depending on the carbon content of the steel . This rapid cooling from high temperature is * hardening * ( or quenching ) . By adding elements such as chromium and nickel to the steel in moderate amounts , which are big atoms that replace iron atoms in the crystal structure , you will not need to cool as rapidly to get the martensite transformation . This is because things get more complicated for the metal , which thus need more time to complete its preferred transformation .

For all you folks talking about the muscles being tightened on one side of your neck and over stretched on the other , stop . You 're wrong . The muscles on one side of my leg or arm do n't tighten up while I sleep . Physical therapist here ( or a " physio " for you English blokes ) and here 's the deal : The neck or cervical spine , is comprised of 7 bones , called vertebrae , that are stacked one on top of another . Between the bones are small , spongy shock absorbers called intervertebral discs . The discs are made up of two parts : the outer part is like a stiff cartilage , like your ear , and the inner part is like a jelly - type stuff . Think of having a small jelly donut between the bones in your neck . There is a small forward curve in your neck called a lordosis . When you sit slouched or bend your head forward , the lordosis straightens . This puts stress on the front side of the discs in your neck , and some of the jelly can push out of place if you stay in this forward bent position too long .

Defendants who get such sentences have often been convicted of multiple crimes . For instance , someone convicted of murder , robbery , burglary , and possessing illegal firearms may be sentenced to life ( for murder ) plus gazillion years ( for rest of the crimes ) . What 's the point ? Three come to mind . First , defendant may be eligible for parole , depending on the jurisdiction . Let 's say that the defendant is convicted in a state where parole is possible after serving 25 years of a life sentence ( and there 's no life - without - the - possibility - of - parole sentence ) . The judge may think that the defendant 's crimes are so heinous that he does n't deserve to ever get out of jail . The judge can issue a life sentence and tack on a long term sentence to follow consecutively to ensure that the convict will die in jail . Second , a conviction can be overturned . Say that our hypothetical defendant managed to get his murder conviction overturned , but still remains convicted of the other crimes . By issuing a life + term sentence , the judge can ensure that even if the murder conviction is overturned , the convict will have to serve out a long prison sentence .

While an operating system ( Windows , Linux , OSX , etc . ) is running , the most core piece of the system is called the " kernel " . The kernel is responsible for controlling access to the hardware by the software running above it . ( Aside : " Linux " is just a kernel ! Everything else , even the basic shell and utilities , are separate . ) The kernel has special access to the memory , as it is the facility that allocates it to applications , and it can read and write every location in it ; same with the hard drives , etc . When a program ( if configured to do this ) or the system , crashes , the kernel has a special function that can be called which will dump all of the relevant memory from the RAM to the Disk as a file . This is the " memory dump " . The point of this is so that a programmer / sysadmin / tech guy can look at it , and attempt to decipher the cause of the crash . These dumps are pretty messy ; they 're effectively just the contents of the RAM in the form of a file , and often extremely hard to read . But if you can , you can use this to find the cause of the problem .

Since you mention breaking the fourth wall , I 'm going to assume you 're talking about postmodernism in fiction / literature . Yes , there 's quite a bit more to it than that . So basically , modernism was a movement that came out of the 19th and 20th centuries . Modernist authors and artists wanted to reject the old traditional ways of writing novels and poems , and making art of any kind . " Make it new " was the motto . They did things like have books where the narrator does n't tell the story in a linear fashion , but jumps from topic to topic , trying to make it seem like everyday human thought . POSTmodernism took many of those same concepts , but tweaked them a bit . Everything still needed to be new , but often " new " came out of remixes of the old . So you have comic books like Alan Moore 's * Watchmen * that throws in symbolism and high - brow literary techniques while telling a story about superheroes ( and then * Time Magazine * called it one of the best books of the century ) . You also have a lot of " metafictional elements , " such as breaking the fourth wall . This is what the show * Community * is talking about when they call things " meta .

Ooh boy , okay . It came into law in early 2002 , and is essentially a law made up of a huge list of legislature intended to increase education standards . It essentially made every state set standard tests that all state - funded schools would have to issue , and if too few pupils passed it , the school would be penalized , possibly by lose funding or teachers losing jobs . The controversy around it is a few different factors . First , teachers were no longer teaching what they felt their pupils needed to learn , instead only teaching what the government said they must . Second , it led to all pupils being taught at the rate of the slowest pupil - there 's no reason and no finance for teaching brighter pupils above and beyond what was needed to pass the test . Third , it led to " teaching the test , " rather than actually teaching a pupil a wide range of skills in a field , it just taught specifically the skills needed to pass the test for the school to continue getting money . Educators were understandably largely upset . They were no longer being trusted to know their pupils , understand what level they were at and teach them appropriately .

In a friendly takeover , both sides meet over lunch , discuss terms , shake hands , assets are exchanged , and everyone 's cool . That much is simple . In a hostile takeover , both sides meet over lunch , and one storms out of the room . The other does what it can to take the other side over . Pretty obvious , right ? An example ... So Big Mega Corp ( BMC ) wants to buy Joe Schmo Co. Joe Schmo takes one look at BMC 's offer , laughs , and says " no dice . " At this point , any takeover effort will be described as " hostile " -- there is no mutual interest in the takeover , just the interest of BMC . Joe Schmo Co. is a publicly traded company -- you can buy and sell Joe Schmo Co. stock on the New York Stock Exchange ( NYSE ) under the ticker " JSC " . BMC tells its stock brokers to buy every share of BMC they can , and so they do . Now , a fork in the road . Scenario A : BMC was able to buy 51 % of all available shares in JSC , and so has a clear majority of interest in the company . This means that when decisions are put before the shareholders , BMC owns 51 % of the vote .

If it 's software that uses a registration key , it probably contains code to check that key . A skilled cracker can find that code and use it to make his own key . That 's not possible if the key is checked online , but then the software needs to contain a statement like this : if ( keyisValid ) continue ( ) ; else showError ( ) ; And a cracker could simply change this to : if ( keyisValid ) continue ( ) ; else continue ( ) ; The software could also contain a self - check to see if it 's been modified , but that too is something that can be diabled in a similar fashion . Finding and disabling all these various checks can take a tremendous amount of time and skill , because the cracker does n't have the original human - readable source code and is just looking at machine code intended to be read by CPU , which is much harder to make sense of , but ultimately there 's always a way to keep the parts of the software you want ( the ones that make up the actual program ) and get rid of the parts you do n't want ( the anti - piracy stuff ) , if you can identify what 's what .

A cancerous cell is one that goes crazy and mutates , and then very quickly begins to spawn more mutated cells that attack the body . Different cells in your body grow at different speeds . " And since hair cells grow fast too , the chemotherapy sometimes ca n't tell the difference between hair cells and cancer cells . So in the process of killing cancer cells , it kills hair cells too , and that makes your hair fall out . As for the eyelashes and eyebrows , it depends in the person . Sometimes they fall out , and sometimes they do n't . Often times chemotherapy is done in phases , and each phase changes how strong the doses are , and sometimes what kind of chemotherapy is being used to fight the cancer . There is time between each phase and sometimes your hair will grow back .

It 's certainly real . For example , if you 've ever heard of a PET scan , it stands for " positron emission tomography ( topography ? ) . " Positrons are antimatter , they 're " anti - electrons . " As for what it is ... well , every particle has an antiparticle . An antiparticle is just the opposite of the " regular " particle that it corresponds to , for the most part . There are certain " internal " properties that any particle has , like its electric charge , and the corresponding antiparticle just has all the signs flipped on those properties ( they 're really numbers ) . Some particles ( like photons ) are their own antiparticle , which is why I 'm allowed to say every particle has an antiparticle . So , for example , the positron is the antiparticle of the electron , and it thus has positive charge . The " external " properties of the antiparticle are still the same as the internal ones . So , for example , the mass is the exact same . Other than the fact that it 's weird to us , antimatter on its own does n't really have any special properties that regular matter does n't have . It 's perfectly stable , all the forces and reactions are pretty much the same , yadda yadda .

In one case the government accidentally released a document that showed they had been spying on the plaintiffs but then got a court to order the return of the document and prevented them from using it in court . Due to the plaintiffs not having proof they were being spied and and unable to get proof via subpoena the cases largely died because courts would rule that the plaintiffs did not have standing . Standing is a legal concept which means that a party has to show a connection to the action 's harm in order to challenge it in court . Without proof that their rights had been violated by being spied on the courts threw the cases out .

It 's actually not a one - way mirror , it 's just a semi - transparent glass . It reflects a certain part of light back , no matter which side you 're looking from . But then how does it work as a mirror , you may ask ? Well , if one room is really bright and one is really dark , then the glass will reflect 50 % of the light from each of them back inside . In a dark room there is no light , so there 's really nothing to reflect . As a result , you do n't see reflections . Meanwhile , in the bright room there 's a lot of light . If the glass reflects 50 % of it ( or 80 % , I dunno what 's the standard ) , then that 's more than enough light to make the glass look like a mirror . However , part of the light still goes through , so the people sitting in the dark room can still see you . Now if the brightness in both rooms was the same , then it would be simply a slightly tinted glass , that 's all .

The more massive a thing is , the more gravity it has . A baseball does n't have much gravity . The Earth has a lot of gravity , and we 're super near to it , so it pulls really hard on us . The Sun has way more gravity than Earth , but it 's far away , so it is n't able to pull very hard on us . When an object is so heavy that anything close enough ca n't get out , it 's called a black hole . It 's called that because light itself ca n't get out of it , which means you ca n't look inside and see what 's in it . The whole area that light ca n't get out of is called the black hole , but the object inside of it generating all of that mass is pretty small . The ball in the middle could be smaller than a walnut and weigh about as much as the moon . The reason that the sun is n't a black hole is that it 's so large . The closer you are to an object , the more it can pull you in with gravity , but if you stand as close as you can get to the sun , you 're actually still pretty far from most of the sun . If you stand inside the sun , the gravity is actually less because different bits of sun are pulling you in different directions .

You 've probably heard of the term " decomposition , " which is when your body " rots " after you die . This happens because of two reasons : * * autolysis * * and * * putrefaction * * . * * Autolysis * * is your body 's own enzymes breaking your body down . " Lysis " means " to break down " and " auto " means " yourself . " Just about every cell in your body has " trash cans " called lysosomes into which it throws away its molecular garbage to be degraded . The lysosomes break down proteins , but they do n't break down the cell because they 're contained in little pockets . Well , when you die , these pockets break ( because the cells are dead and there 's nothing to maintain them ) , so all the nasty stuff inside the lysosome gets out and eats your cells . * * Putrefaction * * is when the bacteria that live inside you start eating you . You have about 2 - 6 pounds of bacteria living in you ( and that is a lot ) . The only thing stopping some of them from eating you is your amazing immune system , which stops working when you die . Both of these processes produce gasses .

A CPU gets instructions and data from the outside world ( usually through the RAM memory ) telling it what to do . It does this by requesting the RAM to send the next instruction / data to it , and then reading the result to its internal storage locations . As it operates on those , it asks for the next , and the next , and so on . As it gets results , it sends data back out in the reverse of the process . Those instructions and data are sent to the CPU in " chunks " . The size of the chunk that the CPU can read each time depend on the " architecture " of the CPU , both how " wide " its internal storage locations are , and how wide the bus of connections between it and the memory are . Way back when CPUs were first invented , that size was as small as 4 bits at a time . Over time , that size has been increased to help increase performance , to 8 bits , 16 , 32 , now 64 and even larger . Changing the width of the instructions / data has two big impacts on performance . Since the processor has more bits to work with , it has a larger variety of different instructions that it can execute , and each one can be more powerful .

This is really about relativity . More importantly , " relativity of simultaneity " . It 's essentially this : picture a plane representing spacetime , with a bunch of dots on it representing particular events . The major question at this point is " which direction is space ( i.e. beside me right now ) , and which direction is time ( where I am , but in the future ) ? " And this depends on your point of view ! The part of spacetime that I consider to be happening " right now " is different from yours if you 're moving compared to me , because we 're calling different parts of spacetime * time * . So my * lines of constant time * ( the whole universe at 1,2,3 etc . seconds into the future ) are different from yours . In your reference frame , these appear * slanted * compared to your time direction : i.e. they extend into your future * and past * ( if you go far enough ) , while they were all entirely in * my * future . The speed of light barrier prevents this from actually getting out of hand : Even if we disagree on " how far into the future " something is , there are events that we can both agree are " in the future " or " in the past " , and this will be true for everyone .

Rail cars have restrictions on their center of gravity , both vertically and horizontally . If a railcar was loaded improperly , with very heavy objects at the top of the car , or on one side of the car , it could topple over . The wheels , trucks , and coupling equipment is all very heavy / strong , and low down on a car to help keep it stable . A single steel wheelset ( just two wheels and the axle between them ) weighs 2500 - 3200 pounds , about as much as a small car . High speed tracks usually have some banking , like a NASCAR track , to help the cars get around the curve too . Also , when a locomotive is pulling on cars around a corner , the force wants to pull the cars to the inside of a curve . Imagine dragging a piece of chain in a circle , holding on to one end . Each chain link does n't follow the path of the link before it , it slides to the inside of the circle . The same forces are at play in a train , and can cause a derailment if the engineer is n't careful .

Muscle is striated , that means it looks sort of like hamburger in a package at the grocery store ( like long strands , all going the same way , stacked atop one another . ) Muscles are wrapped in stuff that 's like cellophane ( Saran Wrap or cling film , if you will ) . That stuff is called fascia . When you move , each little muscle strand moves and works together , it causes the fascia ( cellophane ) to rub . That friction causes the fascia to get stuck to itself and the surrounding fascia . If you get enough friction , the fascia causes the muscle to not move properly . This may cause discomfort or pain . Massage can sometimes break up these areas of knottiness . You can have someone massage the area or you can use tools like foam rollers to help . If you start with soft , light pressure , you may be able to get the muscle to relax and then through patience , get the fascia to not cling and relieve the problem . If you are too aggressive with the pressure to the area , you may cause the muscles to contract and not want to let go . Your body is smart and senses an area already under strain and to protect the damaged area , it will tense up and spasm more .

There are two teams with 18 players on the field . The goal of the game is to kick the ball between the goal posts at your designated end of the field , this is worth 6 points . On either side of the goal posts are 2 smaller posts . If you get it inside the smaller posts you score a point which , as its name implies , is worth a point . You also only score a point if it goes between the two goal posts but the last touch of the ball by a player was not a kick . For example if an opposition player touches it on the way through . You may not throw the ball at any point . To transfer from player to player you must either kick the ball or do a ' handpass ' . A handpass is holding the ball in one hand and punching it with the other so it flies in the direction you want . Because you punched it you get around the rule of no throwing the ball . If the ball is kicked and then caught without touching the ground it is called a ' mark ' and the player that marked the ball has the option to stop and kick the ball without the opposition trying to stop him . If a goal is scored the ball is taken back to the middle of the ground by the umpire and thrown in the air .

When you clock a single core processor past ~3.4 Ghz , you start running into significant thermal issues ; the chip starts to get dangerously hot and may become permanently damaged or not function correctly . You typically need specialized liquid cooling systems to keep the processor running at such clock rates within acceptable temperature limits , and this just is n't feasible for consumer grade electronics . Instead of trying to increase the clock rate higher and higher , companies like Intel have instead focused on designing multi - core processors . These processing chips essentially have multiple CPU cores built - in . Although each core may be clocked at a low rate ( e.g. 2 Ghz ) , they can work together to provide very large amounts of processing power ( far better than a 3.8 Ghz single - core processor [ for example ] ) . Multi - core processors also have other advantages over higher - clocked single - core processors ... most notably the fact that multi - core processors can process more than one operation simultaneously whereas single processors process each operation in series , one after the other .

Since you 're referring to the Voyager Plasma Wave experiment I 'll explain about that . But first we have to make a small detour into how a microphone here on earth works : When you listen to a recording of sound that 's been created using some electronic process , something did capture an electrical signal . That something is a microphone . In a microphone you have a thin sheet of material that gets moved by waves of sound pressure , called the diaphragm . Attached to that diaphragm is either a magnet or some electrically charged foil . Either way , the movement of the magnet or the electrically charged foil creates a changing electromagnetic field , which can be picked up by a kind of antenna ( a magnetic coil , or a capacitor 's plate , which are in fact antennas ) . After amplifying the signal it can be recorded and/or transmitted . Say you had a really , really sensitive radio and a very good antenna , then you could pick up the signal from a microphone that 's not even plugged into anything and that has no electronics whatsoever built in at all .

Since no one is explaining what " CG trickery " is , I 'll explain a simple version . If you 're doing a lock - off shot ( i.e. , no camera movement ) , you could shoot a street with cars and people moving normally , and just let the camera run for a while . Then you can build up an empty frame by stepping through the footage frame by frame and taking different parts of the frame where there are no cars or people . So , in frame 1 , car is at point a , but by frame 10 , it 's moved onto point b. Use a bit of frame 10 to cover up point a in frame 1 . For parked cars and other elements that do n't move and need to be removed , you either clone bits of nearby elements ( walls , street , etc . ) , or you use bits from photographs that you took while on set from different angles , where you could see the bits of the buildings behind the parked cars . If the camera is moving , it gets a little more tricky , but the principle is still the same . You still create an empty plate by combining the techniques I 've described above , but then you have to track that frame to match the camera movement .

Cloud computing means different things to different people , mainly because it has become a buzzword to sell a vague product to confused people . In a technical sense , cloud computing means that as a customer , you use ( and therefore pay ) a variable amount of computing power according to your needs at varying times . You can compare it to consuming electricity from the grid . At daytime , you are away from home and only need enough power to keep your freezer going , and perhaps some other things that are always switched on . In the evenings , you need more electric power to make your lamps light up , watch television , maybe cook a meal in the microwave , run a bath if you have an electrical boiler . So the amount of electric power that you need and consume varies from hour to hour . Much so the same with cloud computing . At the end of the month , you 'll maybe need to run a payroll or assemble a monthly statement for tax purposes . Things which you do not do every day .

As for how long they can fly , every plane has what is called an ETOPS rating . This is the number of minutes they are allowed to be away from a diversion airport . For instance , the Boeing 787 has an ETOPS rating of 330 minutes , meaning it is allowed to be in a place that , if an engine failure occurs , it has 5 and a half hours to reach a diversion airport . However , that does n't mean you fly to that maximum duration . There will be a specific airport to defer to for any given location on your flight , considering both how far you are from the airport , and how suitable that airport is to handle your passengers . As an example , Cold Bay Alaska is a diversion airport for trans - pacific flights , but airlines also need a plan for how to get the passengers away from there ( as well as housing , meals , etc . ) .

You know how there exist algorithms for computing pi and the like ? The ones people use to get the 100000 - zillionth digit of whatever ? Well , almost every number we normally use is like pi , in that there is a program that can calculate it to any accuracy you want . Even if the digits of pi never end , you can calculate pi up to any digit with no problems . Using mathematics , people have been able to show that there exist other numbers that do n't have this feature . By that I mean , there is no program that can compute them like pi can be computed . There is no program that will give you every digit of the number if you run if for long enough . It can not exist . These numbers are practically inaccessible . I could never give you a way to enumerate the digits of one , because that would mean the number is computable . This is proven by basically showing that there exist * more * numbers ( real numbers , including numbers like 0.34234451231 .... that never terminate or repeat and go on to infinity ) than there exist programs . It 's true that there is an infinite amount of programs , but it turns out the way numbers are infinite is bigger than the way programs are infinite .

Slide the sharp thing along the straight thing and you get a perfect cylinder . The HARD thing is threads . You can hand cut threads to a fair tolerance , but there will still be outside - of - tolerance variation . You can cut other identical threads by gearing the thing that drives your cylinder to your OK thread , and using the OK thread to drive your sharp thing . To make your thread more accurate , you construct a scissor , that averages between two separate places on your OK thread . By averaging the difference , you get a thread that 's closer to perfect . After a few generations you get a thread that 's perfect , ie , within tolerances .

Contrary to popular belief , an airplane does n't turn with its rudder . The rudder 's function is to keep the airplane in * coordinated * flight . To turn the airplane , the pilot rolls the airplane in the direction he / she wants to turn by operating the ailerons ( little up / down flaps near the wingtips ) . Using the rudder ( which is attached to the vertical stabilizer [ tail ] ) , the pilot keeps the airplane 's nose pointing into the air stream . When the airplane 's nose is pointed directly into the air stream , the apparent force of gravity acts in a direction opposite the angle of bank . In other words , if the pilots rolls the airplane thirty degrees to the right , and coordinates the turn with the rudder , the apparent gravity through the airplane will point directly out of the bottom of the plane at an angle thirty degrees from a vertical line referencing the earth . If the pilot uses too much rudder , passengers will feel like they are being pulled to the outside of the turn , as if on a merry - go - round . This is called a skid . If the pilot uses too little rudder , the passengers feel like they are being pulled into the turn .

Diesel engines use the heat from compression to ignite the fuel . The problem with gasoline vs. diesel in this scenario is gasoline is far , far more volatile , and it burns too quickly . The engine was n't designed for this , the pressure is supposed to be relieved by being in a position where the piston can be depressed . Contact lenses are simply lenses that are * on * your eyeball ... hense , * contact * . Like any lens , they work by * refracting * ( bending ) light . The first contact lenses were hard plastic , and were uncomfortable to wear . The human eye detects a contact lens as a foreign object , and so tries to coat it in protein to isolate it . This makes it less clear to see through , and can also harbour bacteria . So , you need to keep them very clean by regularly cleaning and disinfecting . The other problem is * oxygen * . Your cornea ( the transparent front of the eye ) has no blood vessels ... so it gets it 's oxygen directly from the air . If it 's covered ( by a contact lens ! ) it can become damaged . Modern disposable contacts fix both of these problems . First , you toss them every day ( no worries about cleaning ) and second , they are made of modern oxygen - permeable ( air gets through ! ) plastic .

Mathematicians are a precise bunch , and nobody would say a probability of 0.16 when you can write it precisely as 1/6 . The bible is n't a single work , it is a collection of books , which can be assembled in various ways to form * codices * ( singular , * codex * ) . Note this was before the printing press , so each work had to be laboriously copied by hand , and each book was a literal book or scroll , separate from the others . Because of the significant effort involved , and because some books are more theologically important than others , people would pick and choose what to include in their codex . Early on , there really was n't a sense of a " bible " , just which scrolls your church had in that codex , and that more was better . In particular , there was the Hebrew Bible , which closely corresponds with the modern Old Testament , and the Latin Vulgate , a 4th Century translation that became the basis of official - ish versions for centuries . The Vulgate was a translation effort by St. Jerome and others , who did not set out to make a new version of the bible .

For sexual reproduction to occur , you need the sperm and the egg from the parents ( the two are collectively referred to as gametes ) . Gametes are produced in a process called meiosis , and the chromosomes of the animal have to pair up to another similar chromosome for this process to happen . Usually within one species , healthy individuals have similar chromosomes , but also the same number of chromosomes . The offspring inherits the same number of chromosomes from the father as from the mother . So the chromosomes can pair up easily to allow meiosis to take place . But different species have different chromosomes and also different numbers of chromosomes . For example , a horse has 32 chromosome pairs , whilst a donkey has 31 chromosome pairs . So when the two interbreed to give birth to a mule , the mule will inherit 31 chromosomes from the donkey parent and 32 from the horse parent . To top this off , the chromosomes are very different . This means that the chromosomes fail to pair up so gametes can not be made by the mule .

When a movie is recorded at 24 fps , that 's the highest frame rate it can be played back at . When played on equipment that refreshes at 60 Hz , the frames have to be duplicated , so you 're seeing each frame two or three times . It 's " two or three times " , because if you simply double each frame you get 48 frames a second . If you triple each frame , you get 72 frames a second . To get 60 fps , you have to double some frames and triple others . That 's if you 're using the NTSC system common in North America and some other countries , which works at a fraction less than 60 fps . If you 're in Europe , you 'll be using the PAL system , which has better colours but a lower frame rate : exactly 50 fps . Movies shot at 24 fps are then simply shown with each frame doubled . This means that an average movie , when shown on TV , will run a few minutes shorter . The sound track will also be speeded up to match so that it does n't go out of sync : this does mean that the sound is very slightly higher in pitch , but if that 's a problem modern digitial sound processing means it can be artificially lowered back to its original pitch .

A monolithic kernel runs the operating in " kernel space " , a privileged position , and defines all the virtual interfaces over the hardware . When you write a program , you do n't tell the hard drive to open a particular file , let alone how to do it - file - open is an abstraction provided by the OS , whether it 's a hard drive , CD drive , or other device . A microkernel is very small by comparison , and handles few essential services like memory management , and has few generic interfaces which drivers and protocol stacks can interact with . Drivers and protocol stacks are n't run in privileged as the kernel itself is , they 're ran in user space , which has a different set of permissions and access control over the system , dictated by the kernel . User space has to cross logical barriers and get permission to do certain elevated tasks . Monolithic kernels have kernel space vs. user space , too , it 's just with the micro kernel , more is in user space . The advantage is anything in user space can crash or get dumped and replaced without taking down the whole system . In a monolithic kernel , if there is a bug in the file system code , it effects the whole system .

In the US that is an area of land that is not an incorporated municipality . To form an official town residents must go through a legal process called " incorporation . " Each state has its own requirements , but generally it involves a petition to the county or state government , and meeting a set list of criteria . If the wannabe - town meets all the criteria the state legislature will officially incorporate it , and authorize it to exercise the powers of a city like having a police force , creating a charter , writing regulations , levying taxes , etc . Any area that has not gone through the legal process of incorporation , or been legally annexed by an incorporated city / town / village , is considered " unincorporated " territory and generally governed by the county / parish in which it resides .

A markov chain is a mathematical approach to disentangling several possible events that depend on outcomes before it . To stay topical , take a look at March madness brackets . You have a pretty low chance of getting your bracket right . But if we apply some really simple logic , we can increase that chance . If you fill out the bracket as a set of unorganized fill in the blank boxes , you wo n't do well . For instance , you could have a team that you eliminated in the sweet sixteen winning the final four . That does n't make sense . Instead , let 's create a chain of causes that predict the inputs into the next block of causes . If a team does n't make the first round , they ca n't end up in the later rounds . Better right ? But if we have even more information , we can do even better . We could fill out our bracket * as * the tournament is happening and expect to do really well . A player who lead scoring got injured in the elite 8 ? We can use that information to reduce the team 's chances in the final four . That 's why a Markov chain is so.good at making predictions . It refined it 's approach as it gets information . In real use , Markov chains get much more sophisticated .

Grass has too much cellulose and other tough and indigestible parts . The ruminants have a multi - part stomach that allows the food to be chewed , swallowed and then fermented . The bacteria in their gut will work breaking the food down . They also regurgitate the tougher parts as a ' cud ' and re - chew it to break it down even more . The gut bacteria will convert the grasses to usable nutrition components and waste gases . The animals release the waste gases as burps and farts . This is the methane they complain about with cows . ( Buffalo were also ruminants and there were estimated to be millions more buffalo than the cows we now have ... ) Your stomach does not have a rumen to ferment the grasses . It also does not have any of the same bacteria that specifically do the fermentation in ruminants like cows , goats , buffalos , and sheep . Horses are not ruminants and can not get anywhere near as much protein and nutrition from grasses as cows . This is why you could feed cows exclusively on grass , but horses need to be supplemented with some grains in their diet .

Electrical outlets are typically set up ( in the US ) with a “ hot ” side ( carrying the actual voltage ) and a neutral side ( which is essentially no voltage and the same as ground ) The third pin ( if present ) is also ground and 0 volts . However , the “ polarized ” plugs you ’re referring to wo n’t have this pin . The blade width difference is to control which wire of the two carries the actual power . ( Old - school plugs have blades the same size ) It is typical for manufacturers to tie the neutral to the chassis of the device to save on wiring costs ( for two - wire devices ) . The danger is if the chassis is “ hot ” “ as a result of flipping the plug - you could get a shock just by having your body in between the device and any ground channel ( I.e. a plumbing fixture ) . The narrow blade of the plug is specified to be the “ hot ” in this case ; and allows users and manufacturers to consistently ensure the connection is made without energizing the chassis .

Nearsightedness usually arises because the eyeball has the wrong shape . It 's too long for light to be brought into focus from faraway objects , as if you 're trying to project a movie on a screen that is too far away ( and you ca n't compensate with the projector 's lens any further ) . Farsightedness in young people typically has the opposite cause : the eyeball being too short . Obviously these two things can not happen at once ( at least in the same eye ): your eyeball is either too short or too long . But mainly in older people , farsightedness can also have a different cause . With age , the lens of the eye becomes stiff , which makes it harder for the focusing muscles in the eye to pull the lens into a ~~flatter~~ more spherical shape to bring ~~faraway~~ nearby things into focus . So when you get older , it 's possible to be both nearsighted , due to the shape of your eyeballs , and farsighted , due to having a stiff lens . Although in that case , the terms ' near- ' and ' farsighted ' are a bit misleading because they normally describe what you _ can _ see , whereas the point is actually that you ca n't see either very well .

It 's usually a synonym for " I agree " in common speech , but there 's a little nuance there : " I agree " means " I believe you 're right . " " I disagree " means " I believe you 're wrong . " " I do n't disagree " means " I do n't believe that you 're wrong , but I might not be convinced that you 're right . " It 's sort of the equivalent of a court finding someone " Not guilty . A rocket has two different rotational centers . The center of mass is the point where the rocket balances . The is the point it would rotate around if it were in a vacuum , and as the fuel burns from the back of a solid fuel motor it moves the center of gravity slightly forward . The center of pressure , on the other hand , is the point where air forces on the rocket are equal . Adding even a tiny fin moves the center of pressure backwards . Think of it like that gaudy rooster wind vane on a rural farmhouse . Air presses on all of the structure if the structure when it is n't pointed into the wind . The center of pressure only depends on the shape , so it does n't change as the fuel is burned . Small fins are put on the bottom of a rocket so the center of pressure is behind the center of mass . This means that the force of air on the whole of the rocket 's shape turns the rocket if it is disturbed to return it to going in the direction it was launched . Solid fuel rockets become more stable as they fly faster .

Visualize a helicopter with two rotor blades , just to make it easier . And let 's just ignore the tail rotor and the engine for now . Focusing only on the rotor and how it controls the movement of the helicopter , there are two controls the pilot uses . One is called the collective , and one is called the cyclic . The rotor blades on a helicopter are wings . Another term for helicopter is " rotary wing aircraft " , as opposed to " fixed wing aircraft " . The blades spin through the air , and their * angle of attack * can be adjusted as they spin . You can think of " angle of attack " as simply tilting the blade . If you increase the angle of attack , or tilt the blades down , they push more air down , generating lift . Back to " collective " and " cyclic " . " Collective " means increasing the angle of attack of both blades simultaneously , and throughout the entire rotation . This can be thought of as simply pushing air down to make the helicopter go up . " Cyclic " refers to making an adjustment to the angle of attack at a certain point in the blade 's cycle .

What people are n't telling you enough is that longer is better than shorter . Suppose a password had only 8 upper/ lower case letters in it . That would give 52 ^ 8 possibilities , or 53,459,728,531,456 . Adding in 10 special characters ( @#$ _ & -+ * ! ) for example , gives you 62 ^ 8 or 218,340,105,584,896 . Better , but not remarkably so ( 4x ish the size ) , considering how many guesses can be made per second . If you had simply added another letter , you would then have 52 ^ 9 or 2,779,905,883,635,712 which is literally exponentially better . For a fun way to visualize this , I recommend xkcd . Hey , Ph . D here working on light induced degradation ( LID ) in solar cells . Essentially , you need to think of the efficiency of a solar cell as its ability to generate but also collect electrons as useful energy . Now in the body of the solar cell , which we call the bulk , you can get many things that will steal that electron and stop it from being collected . These include metallic impurities ( Iron , chromium , copper ... etc . ) , crystallographic defects and usually anything that has a charge that can capture an electron or a hole ( which we call charge carriers ) . The more of these defects you have the lower your effective efficiency . So what happens out in the field over time ? There are many things that can happen that can cause a module to degrade . On the macro level , standard deterioration from corrosion , UV exposure , humidity , etc as mentioned by others in this thread . We also have a few such as PID ( potential induced degradation ) and LID ( Light Induced Degradation ) . LID for example in monocrystalline solar cells is largely known to be due to the Boron - Oxygen defects .

To put it super simply ; seizures are when neurons in your brain get hyperexcited and start firing off ( and often different pathways nearby that should n't be activated get excited too ) . Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant . When you chronically drink alcohol , it increases the activation / release of GABA , which is an inhibitory neurotransmitter . Again , in simple terms this just depresses the function of pathways and makes it harder for neurons to fire off . After a while , your body gets used to operating under such high levels of inhibition from all the GABA released from drinking alcohol . This manifests in the form of neurons becoming super - sensitive to any signal that 's going to excite them . So on the one hand you have them being depressed by GABA , and on the other you have them being hypersensitive to whatever activates them . This balances out to basically normal function . When you finally stop drinking , suddenly you 're no longer getting that excessive GABA release and so they 're not being inhibited / depressed any.ore . * But * , the neurons are still hypersensitive to activation signals .

Formulas are n't magic . They 're a way to communicate ideas the same as English language . The difference is that mathematical formulas enable you to describe precise relations between things , while natural languages , like English , are more suited to describing things like emotion , intention and such . When you write down an equation , you 're simply writing down an idea you have , in a precise manner . Formulating that takes some practice but not really that much . Understanding those ideas then is about as complex a task as understanding ideas others have , after you know how to read the language . Finding ideas that work , which you can then communicate with formulas , is a much less precise art . You can have just a fun idea about how things are connected . Maybe you start from some known connection , and then use it as a base which you use figure out much more complex connections . Mathematics is essentially an art of studying connections concepts have , and this art is then codified into very precise and exact statements made using its language . The search for those ideas itself is pretty freeform , devoid of any particular structure .

TL;DR It 's just lots of calculations that get easier over time as hardware gets more advanced and cheaper so you can do more calculations in a shorter time , and better algorithms / engines are made that limit the number of calculations needed to get a nice - looking render . Rotating models : For something very simple , take a model of a person . The model is made up of points , each of those is made up of 3 numbers ( x , y , z ) . Depending on how realistic you want the person to look , the model could be a thousand points so that you get very fine details . That 's already 3,000 numbers just for that person . Now to do something as simple as rotating the person a bit to the left , you have to multiply all 3,000 of the numbers by something called a " rotation matrix " made up of the cosine and sine values of the angle you want to rotate them by . So you have to get the cosine and sine values of the angle you 're rotating by , then go through all 3,000 of the numbers and multiply them . Another minor problem : the rotation matrix rotates the points around ( 0,0,0 ) .

≡ is used in several different contexts . If can be used to denote identity between two mathematical expressions . For example , if I were to write ( a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^(2 ) , one could mistake this for an equation ( ie I 'm looking for a , b which will satisfy it ) . However writing ( a + b)^2 ≡ a^2 + 2ab + b^2 emphasizes that the two expression ( a+b)^2 and a^2 + 2ab + b^2 are identical . It can also be used to denote an [ equivalence relation ] ( URL_0 ) . Elements can be equivalent , even if they 're not equal , in which case we can treat them as equal in the context of the equivalent relation . For example , lets look at modular arithmetic : given a number N , we define two numbers a , b as equivalent if ( a - b ) is divisible by N. In this case , we write a ≡ b ( mod N ) , or simply a ≡ b for short . For example if N=5 then 6 ≡ 11 , even though 6 ≠ 11 .

" Grounding " in electrical circuits just means a reference point , to which everything else can be connected . For example , in a car , one side of the battery is connected to the car 's body / chassis . This provides a convenient way to complete an electrical circuit . So , if you want to connect a headlight . You do n't need to connect 2 wires - one taking current from the battery to the bulb , and one taking the return current from the bulb to the battery . Instead , you can just use 1 wire to take current from the battery to the bulb , and the return current can go via the car 's chassis . The same principle is used in marine craft , aircraft and spacecraft . The metal structure serves as a convenient method of connecting multiple things together to allow circuits to be completed . If two spacecraft need to dock , then the bodies can be electrically connected together to form a single " ground " zone covering both craft . Each craft retains its own electrical system , but the two systems share the same reference point .

Time is being defined as " what we 're experiencing here on Earth right now . " Hence the use of the word " years " , which is an Earth - orbit related unit . If you 're wondering HOW they arrived at the " 13.5 " number , [ this Wikipedia article ] ( URL_0 ) explains it in some detail . Briefly , there are two assumptions : * That the rest of the universe , even the parts that are too far for us to observe , behave like the near parts of the universe that we CAN observe , so that we can generalize what we see . * That the current behavior of galaxies moving away from us at the observed rate and acceleration , is not some recent phenomenon , but has always been happening ( this is the Big Bang theory ) . So they look at what they 're seeing right now , and they assume that the forces of gravity etc . always behaved the way we currently observe , and predict backwards how long it could have taken to get to where we are right now . And they 're using " size " and " time " in Earth terms .

But in the context you are asking about , " philosophy " is not simply a way you do things , it is a way of organizing ideas . Some factors philosophers consider might be : * Is it more important to act on ideas our emotions push us to ? Or to act on the fact of the situation and ignore emotion ? * Is it smarter to let nature take its course , or to challenge nature ? Why , and under what conditions should you practice the opposite ? * Do ideas we act on originate from our imagination ? Or does imagination and experience create new ideas ? Or are they a circle ? * How do we know what is truth ? How do we know the facts we use to support truth are themselves true ? * Is an action or idea valuable in its own right ? Or is it necessary to reference a source outside ourselves to know what is good or right ? These are by no means the only questions . There is also the construction and testing of logical sequences .

Simply put , energy is the capacity to do work . Doing work is giving off your energy and putting it into something else . Potential energy is basically the energy you have due to where you are . An electric charge in an electric field has some potential energy . When it is at a point where it has a high energy , it will be drawn toward a point with lower energy . By crossing this path , it can do work equal to the * difference * of potential energy between where it starts and where it ends up . Now , how much potential energy a charge has depends on two factors . One is the charge itself , measured in coulombs . The other is the location at which the charge currently is . If you remove the charge from the equation and just take the influence of the location on potential energy , you are left with what is called a potential . You can place any charge in that space and can know from just the potential and the charge how much potential energy the charge will have at any given point . And you can again take the difference of two potentials to know how much work a charge can perform based on just the potential difference between the end points and the value of the charge itself .

There is a network of VLF ( Very Low Frequency ) radio receivers around the world . These receivers listen for the radio signature of a lightning discharge . You can actually make a primitive slope measuring tool for very cheap , and by doing so it might help you understand the principles behind why a golf rangefinder can measure slope and use it to change distance . First , you could use a plastic protractor , or [ print one online ] ( URL_0 ) . Next , tie a piece of string with a weight on the end to the center of the long , straight part . If you put the long edge right at eye level , then look at an object above or below your eye level , you 'll notice that the string will hang and align with a number . That number is a measure of the angle from level of the object you 're looking at . So if you 're looking at a flag pin that 's 10 degrees lower than you , the string will align with the number 10 on the protractor . The angle is essentially the slope of the hole . Now imagine that there 's a triangle formed . When you 're looking out from the protractor ( or the rangefinder ) , your gaze essentially forms the hypotenuse of a right triangle . By knowing the angle of that hypotenuse and knowing the distance of the hypotenuse , it 's very easy to calculate what the length of the hole is .

Oh boy . I 'm not sure where to start . Urine , which is what gets excreted into the bladder is not connected to feces , which is what gets excreted be the colon . Your bladder is basically just a bag that the kidneys fill up with wastes . The water part of it is pretty much there because the kidneys use it to flush the waste products out . Diarrhea is from the colon . The colon , or large intestine , is the final section of the digestive system . One of the jobs it has is to regulate water in feces . It is very good at absorbing water from digested waste as well as adding water to it . Most of the time diarrhea happens when the body needs to get rid of the waste quickly . If you have an illness , or contamination of food , you do n't want it staying in the body , so the colon flushes it out with extra water and stronger contractions ( cramps ) . If things are normal , the goal is to keep just enough water in your feces to help it move easily , but preserve the rest in your system . That 's why it is n't runny all the time ; it would use up your water faster than is useful . Diarrhea can lead to dehydration , which is n't good . This has nothing to do with the bladder or kidneys .

Our eyes have something called “ dynamic range ” , which is basically how light and dark we can perceive things before they ’re just a blinding white or an impenetrable black . Our eyes and brain can adjust where on the brightness scale that range is placed to a degree , by our pupils opening and closing and the brain ramping up or damping down the “ volume ” of the incoming signals from the optical nerve . This means that in a dark tunnel , we can see the ground around us but the end of the tunnel just looks bright white , because your pupils are open wide and the signals from our eyes are being pumped up a notch . Outside the tunnel on a bright day looking towards it , we would see everything around us normally , but the tunnel itself just looks like a dark hole , because your brain and eyes are n’t able to perceive the bright daylight and the dark tunnel at the same time . This is also why it sucks when someone turns a light on at 2 am ; your brain and eyes need time to recalibrate for the new lighting . This is a pretty fun quirk of our physiology , and comes into play in developing video games .

Firefighter here , I actually just finished an arson investigation class so this question had great timing . Depending on the severity of the fire , there ’s two ways . If there was a good working fire which was extinguished and the house is still standing , firstly the investigator arriving on scene would scan the exterior of the structure for any possible signs of arson ( gas cans , burnt matches , generally anything out of the ordinary ) . The investigator would then go inside the structure , and they ’d scan the flooring ( if hardwood or concrete ) for scorch marks from flammable liquids , which almost all flammable liquids will leave a distinct scorch mark which is asymmetrical . If none of that reveals anything , they ’d move on to other common points of ignition , such as electrical outlets and appliances . Typically the point of origin for fires will leave a distinct origin mark as long as the structure was n’t burned beyond recognition . If nothing is found from that , the cause of the fire will probably be marked as undetermined , due to no solid evidence being recovered .

The answer is : it depends . High decibel ( high volume ) sound puts a lot of strain on your ear drum . When hearing is damaged , it is often damaged in specific ranges ; what 's damaged is the moving parts in the ear and/or the nervous systems ' sensitivity to those signals . Generally , people with impaired hearing lose the clarity to pick up specific frequencies of vibration ; continued exposure to high decibel sound on those frequencies will continue the degradataion , and may spill over into other frequencies . But that 's not the only type of hearing impairment . People with Tinnitus ( a ringing in the ear ) are experiencing something unrelated to the ear drum . Their ear drum may be excellent at picking up vibrations from the air , but this is overlaid with a high pitched whine or ringing that can drown out some frequencies . Exposure to loud noise will degrade the drum just like it would with anyone else . Then there 's people who have full - on neural issues where audio is n't processed correctly , even though the signal to the brain is solid .

Think about burning a piece of toast . Can you unburn the toast ? No . Why not ? Because we did n’t change the toast into a new thing called burnt toast , we just burned up part of the toast . The way our universe works , so far as we can tell , this only goes one way . Once you burnt the toast you ca n’t make it back the way it was . Even if you had a way or rebuilding it , it would n’t be the exact same toast . Even if you found a way to rebuild it with the exact same stuff and it was the same toast ( impossible as far as we know ) then you would have needed to spend lots and lots of energy to do that , which means we still lost something , right ? Not quite . We did n’t lose anything , really we did n’t even lose anything when we burn the toast . We just converted what was toast into other things . The universe did n’t lose anything , it still has the same amount of stuff it had before . We see it as loss because the heat and burnt crumbs are n’t as useful to us . The universe does n’t care for toast , it ’s not picky at all , it just wants to keep all its stuff .

The answer to your question is yes and no . You actually have two copies of every gene , one you inherit from your mother and one you inherit from your father . These copies are called alleles . The genetics for weight are complicated . There is no one single gene responsible for it and it is strongly influenced by environment ( both external things like stress and internal things like what you eat and how much you exercise ) . The set of alleles you have regarding propensity for weight are not going to be identical to you mother , because you have the contribution from your father , as well . So the exact combination of alleles you inherit from each parent will determine the genetic ( but not environmental ) contribution to your weight . In that regard , the genetics does change from one generation to the next . As I already mentioned , though , weight is not just genetic . It is strongly influenced by diet and exercise . If you maintain a healthy weight through doing those things , then even if both of your parents are heavy set , you might not be . That being said , you are * not * affecting your genetics .

The heart pumps blood almost directly into itself , and drains blood from its venous circulation directly into the right atrium . This is the main difference . Your other muscle tissues are far away , there is a lot of them relative to the size of the heart , and they receive blood more slowly . This means more delays in getting oxygen to these tissues , and more delay removing metabolic waste products , and just a * lot * of muscle tissue to supply . When we exercise , the expanse of our skeletal muscles is simply too much for our body to run at peak efficiency indefinitely . Our muscles run out of oxygen , glucose , and build up waste products eventually . The heart , conversely , is first in line for the good stuff from our arterial blood supply . Similarly , it 's sized such that more than enough blood can get to it , and feed / remove waste from it , so tat it can run indefinitely at peak efficiency . That said , there are things that can happen which cause the heart to become less effective and have to grow in size to compensate . It is n't getting tired per se , but it 's certainly strained in these situations . This is cardiomegaly , and is related to heart failure .

How this kind of thing works depends a lot on where you live . Here , in Sweden , next of kin automatically inherit . In fact , the Law of inheritance specifies that known next of kin have a right to inherit . You may write a will , but next of kin will always have legal rights to 50 % of the estate . A will that gives next of kin with legal rights a cold hand is disregarded . If there is no will , next of kin inherit according to non - negotiable priority rules . Up to a certain point . If there is no kin with inheritance rights , and no will , the estate goes to a public entity that automatically inherits and sells off the estate . Northern Ireland is a constituent country of the UK ; Ireland ( sometimes called the Republic or Ireland , or , more properly , Éire ) is not . This is important , because Northern Ireland is divided ( roughly 50/50 ) over the issue of whether to remain part of the UK or join the Republic . For many decades until the 1990s there was a guerilla war going on there , with terrorist attacks on both sides . The British and Irish governments finally managed to broker a peace , which is so far still holding , but only just . The CTA means that people can pass from Ireland to the UK without border checks and without custom checks .

There 's two types of contact friction : * static * friction and * kinetic * friction . Static friction is the force that it takes to push a stationary object and start it sliding / skidding across the ground . Kinetic friction is the force it takes to keep pushing something that is already sliding . Static friction is always greater than kinetic friction . Cars work by static friction . Even though the tire moves forward , the tire rubber does n't actually slide along the ground ( unless you 're skidding or burning out ) . The point of contact between the ground and the tire is stationary , so the friction between car and ground is static friction . This friction is how the car moves forward - it spins its wheels to push backward on the ground , and so it pushes itself forward . When your car is skidding / sliding and you slam on the brakes , your tires lock up and start sliding across the ground . Static friction becomes kinetic friction . Since kinetic friction is lower than static friction , this means that the force your car can exert on the ground is lower . This means that your traction is lower , and your ability to control the motion of the car is lower .

As others have mentioned , cement is an ingredient in concrete . But an important detail is why we use concrete instead of cement . It turns out that one reason cement is so strong is that it creates a crystaline structure that grows over time ( which is why cement and concrete get stronger over time ) . But while the crystals are strong in terms of compression , it can fracture along the planes of the crystal . This is similar to how diamonds are cut or sometimes even break in someone 's ring when dropped . Even though diamond is the hardest naturally occurring material , a hit at the right place at the right angle will cause the crystal to break along one of the crystal planes . So how do you make cement stronger ? You make sure the crystals do n't grow too big to prevent this type of breaking . To do this , you add sand and/or rock . The crystal structure stops and a new crystal has to start in a new direction . The fact that the crystals are small and have random orientations mean it 's very difficult to cause this crystal breaking . That 's why concrete is stronger than cement .

It 's irreversible because it 's destructive , information is lost in the process . The only way to reverse a hash is to plug the hash into a database and hope that someone has entered one , and only one input string associated with it . Hashes are of a constant data size regardless of the length of the input . For example , the length of an MD5 hash is 128 bits , the length of SHA-1 is 160 bits , and the length of SHA-2 is one of 224 , 256 , 384 , or 512 bits depending on the particular algorithm used . For any given input , the MD5 hash of that input will always be 128 bits in length . A 5 byte text document and 1 gigabyte video both have 128 bit MD5 hashes . This is a one to one forward relationship . However , hash algorithms usually have no input constraints , the range of possible inputs is infinite . Thus , while any one input will have exactly one hash associated with it , there are an infinite number of inputs which will have that same hash . When two different inputs have the same hash , this is called a hash collision and programmers need to be mindful that this does occur .

We know the height and location of Everest 's peak the same way we know most of the terrain around us , through surveying . The simplest explanation of surveying is that you start with two reference points that you know the location of * very * accurately . It does n't really matter which two points , but you especially want to know the distance between them super accurately . From there , you can locate any third point that is visible from the first two by measuring the angles between them . Any triangle adds up to 180 degrees , after all . You can figure out distances because you know the angles , and you know one distance very accurately , and sine and cosine are your friends . And you can measure relative heights by having a vertical reference , like weight that hangs on a cord , and measuring the angle from it as well . Once you have a third point , you can use any pair of points to generate a fourth . And any two of those four to generate a fifth , and so on . Eventually you have a bunch of triangles radiating out from your starting two points , and you can measure the whole country or whole world this way .

It 's mostly because it 's a lot more convenient to define it that way , because it makes things shorter to write and clearer . We could have defined prime numbers as including 1 , but then basically every theorem about prime numbers would have to exclude them . For example , the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says ( in one formulation ): > Every positive integer greater than 1 can be represented in exactly one way as a product of one or more primes , up to the order of the factors . If you defined prime numbers such that 1 was also prime , you 'd have to write : > Every positive integer greater than 1 can be represented in exactly one way as a product of one or more primes greater than 1 , up to the order of the factors . There are lots and lots of theorems that would have to be rephrased in the same way , so as a practical matter , it 's just more useful if the term " prime number " does n't include 1 .

From a biological standpoint , free radicals are unavoidable , but you have antioxidants in your body that are used to deal with them . You ca n't really take anything to boost it unless you 're planning on IVing vitamin C. Normally , molecules and atoms like to pair up their electrons . This makes them more stable . When atoms have an unpaired electon , this is known as a free radical . It is high energy , short lived , and basically reacts with anything it touches . It can cause cellular and DNA damage . Free radicals are a consequence of using oxygen ( respiration ) and your white blood cells use free radicals as a way to kill things ( it 's basically like a shotgun ) . They can also convert free radicals into useful components called reactive ( oxygen ) species which act as signalling molecules , and the aforementioned damaging molecules . Your body have mechanisms to deal with them when you 're healthy , called antioxidants . However , you can be in a state of oxidative stress when antioxidants are being diminished and you have raised free radicals / oxidants going around .

Black is the absence of visible light . So in that sense , light itself can not be black , unless you consider other frequencies of light ( electromagnetic radiation ) that you can not see . In a dark room , this light will not visibly illuminate anything , so you could say , by some definitions , the color of this light is black . On the other hand , shining such " black light " on a visibly illuminated surface will not make it look more black . This is different from , say , red light , which will tend to make things look more reddish . E.g. if you take a piece of paper in a well - lit room and shine a red light onto it , it will make the paper look reddish . Doing the same with invisible " black light " will not make it look blacker , or even change the paper 's appearance at all . So in that sense it 's not really fair to say that invisible light is black , and more accurate to say it has no color whatsoever . Things that look black do n't necessarily reflect 0 light . Say you 're watching a movie projected on a white screen . In one scene , a black car drives into shot . If you have a good projector setup , the car will look really black .

Radioactive decay relies on probability . There is no definite amount of time that one element will take to decay into another the same way that there is no definite amount of coin tosses it would take to land a heads . Hypothetically , you could toss a coin indefinitely and never land a heads . However , when you have an incredibly large amount of atoms together , the probability of decay can essentially be thought of as the " average " time of decay . The larger the sample size , the better the approximation . If you were to take the decay time of every individual atom of a sample and plotted it , it would essentially give a bell curve , with the half - life of that element being derived from the peak . Since there is an incredibly large number of atoms in a given sample , this approximation is very good .

TL;DR : Your plastic bottle will almost always wind up in a bale of sorted " mixed plastic " in a few days , maybe a week or so . But it 's hard to say how long it will be until that bale is processed into recycled plastic granules / pellets and then used to make consumer goods . Let 's start with you putting your plastic bottle in a recycling bin . What happens next ? First , the bin gets collected by a waste management company . This may or may not be the same company that collects non - recyclable garbage in any given area , but it 's almost always done with trucks dedicated to recycling . The recycling trucks dump their loads at a recovery facility that may or may not be owned by the same company that owns the trucks . These drop offs occur pretty much all day during business hours , but any given recycling bin is typically only collected once a week . Second , the recovery facility sorts incoming " mixed material " into different categories using a number of different processes , some automated , some manual . Paper is sorted with an " air knife " that blows it onto a different belt while leaving heavier materials behind .

Your bank gives you a statement that is from their point of view . In their point of view , money you give them in a deposit is money that can be taken out by you at any time . This is a liability from their point of view . In accounting , all accounts have a " normal balance " , so liabilities have a credit " normal balance " , while assets have a debit " normal balance " . Normal balance means that when the liability account increases - your account at the bank - it increases on the credit side . So when your bank account balance goes up , so does the bank 's liability regarding that account . This is all part of double entry accounting . So when you deposit money , there 's also an associated debit with that credit . Debits always go first in any accounting transaction , to help clear up confusion when entering them in . The bank would put this in their " books " as a debit to their asset account ( money coming in ) , and a credit to the liability account ( where the money came from ) . Obviously banks are more sophisticated in their accounting practices now .

You need to understand the difference between capital and interest . In a bank , a whole bunch of people put some money into the bank ( called capital ) . The bank pools this capital and invests it in something like shares , or property or bonds or mortgages or something . This investment earns the bank extra money ( called interest ) . At the end , the bank gives all the participants back the full amount of capital they originally deposited , and a share of the interest the bank earned . In a pyramid scheme , a whole bunch of people put capital into a fund . The fund manager usually does n't invest this capital in anything , so there is n't generally any interest . At the end , the capital gets divided up between the participants according to some formula where some people get more than the capital they put in . This means that everyone else gets less than the capital they put in . Usually some people get nothing back at all .

This is a question which illustrates how incompatible reality can be with mathematical rigour . In mathematics , a perfect sphere sitting on top of a perfectly flat plane would indeed have a single point of intersection . Such a flat plane would be a ' tangent plane ' to the sphere . However , in reality , nothing can be ' perfectly spherical ' or ' perfectly flat ' , as both of these properties are defined rigorously by mathematics alone . A sphere for instance is a mathematical object with very specific rules , e.g. * Every point on the surface of the sphere is equidistant from it 's centre . * Every point on the surface of the sphere has the same curvature . And conclusions you can draw from the properties such as : * The maximum distance between two points on a sphere is achieved when they can be connected by a straight line through the centre of the sphere . * The sphere looks exactly the same from any direction . These very specific mathematical conditions are too specific to be consistent with the real world .

A Turing machine consists of only a few things . A paper tape , a head that can either read , erase , or write a symbol on that tape , and advance / reverse the tape by one step . It 's an impractical computer design , but very easy to reason about and prove properties . It turns out that this extremely limited machine can compute anything that is computable - the mathematician Turing proved this , and so it is a very important mathematical result . Now , your PC is not designed like a Turing machine . For example , its memory is random access - you can read any memory location you want , you do n't have to advance a paper tape 10,000,000 positions . However , it is " turing complete " - we can prove that it can do everything that the Turing machine can do , which therefore means it can compute anything that is computable . This makes the proof easy . If you show a device can do the few simple things the Turing machine does , it must be a general purpose computing machine . It can be very difficult to proof that it is general purpose otherwise , if you try to take all its capabilities into account .

Identical twins are where a single sperm fertilizes a single egg and somewhere along the line , the embryo splits in two , so you get two individuals that are genetically identical . You get ' Siamese ' twins when the embryo only partly splits . It splits enough to form two separate individuals , but does n't completely physically split apart . So , you can have ' extreme ' conjoined twins like Abby and Brittany Hensel . They look like a single person with two heads , but the truth is they have separate hearts , stomachs , lungs and Spinal cords . In their case this essentially means that each of them has half a body under their control . Abby has no control over and ca n't feel the arm and leg on Brittany 's side and vice versa and they each only have control over their half of the body .

> So Like is there a real scheme to these names ? There is no real rhyme or reason to the naming of ship classes if that is what you are asking . Each country has its own method for naming ships and conventions may change . However , the first ship of a class typically carries the name of the class . For example , the USS Nimitz is the first ship of the Nimitz class aircraft carriers , and the USS Ohio is the first ship of the Ohio class submarines . It is extremely ineffective to conceptualise , plan , design , construct , and maintain a single bespoke ship . Economies of scale come into heavy play in ship building , so it 's most cost effective to build multiple ships all based on the same design and the same core components , while incorporating revisions , learning opportunities , and new technologies into newer ships of the same class . All of the Nimitz class aircraft carriers have minor differences that a result of their being built at a rate of one every 5 or so years with a scheduled mid - life overhaul . There are 8 or 9 different designs for the Arleigh - Burke class destroyer organised into 3 major revisions .

I 'm not sure . Used to work in visual neuroscience , and this is my best guess . I 'd love if someone has a definite answer though ! I think the main culprit is visual glare . Light travels in straight lines , but you get glare when light is scattered in a disorganised pattern \(usually strong light , like car headlights in rain\ ) . Your brain has to process everything you see , and its less work if you can see everything clearly . If you have to perceive an indistinct shape , your higher visual processing areas have to work harder . Glare from bright light will make it harder to perceive things around you . So what I think might be going on is that glare \(which again is disorganised , scattered light\ ) means that you 're perceiving a different pattern of scattered light from each eye . Your brain has to interpret and combine both images , which is a lot of work \(this is normally easy because they 're usually the same\ ) . Shutting off one eye \(half the signal\ ) means you have less work to do , and might make it easier to see . Either that or its something really simple that I 've missed , like shutting one eye makes it easier to decrease the pupil size in your open eye !
